## Page 5527

And “the point here” is that a servant who is a messenger is superior to a prophet who is a king, just as Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad—blessings and peace be upon them—are superior to Joseph, David, and Solomon—peace be upon them. Likewise, those who are foremost and brought near to Allah are superior to the righteous companions of the right who are not among those foremost and brought near. Whoever fulfils what Allah has made obligatory upon him and does whatever he likes among permissible things belongs to the latter group. Whoever does only what Allah loves and is pleased with, intending to use what has been made permissible to him to help him fulfil Allah’s commands, belongs to the former group.

Section

Allah Most High mentions “His friends”—those who follow a moderate course and those who are foremost—in Surah Fātir, saying:

“Then We caused those whom We chose from among Our servants to inherit the Book. Among them are those who wrong themselves, those who follow a moderate course, and those who are foremost in good deeds by Allah’s permission. That is the great bounty.”

“Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter, adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be silk.”

“And they will say, ‘Praise be to Allah, who has removed all sorrow from us. Indeed, our Lord is All-Forgiving, Most Appreciative.’”

“‘He who, out of His bounty, has settled us in the everlasting abode, where neither toil nor weariness touches us.’”

However, the three categories mentioned in this verse refer specifically to the nation of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as Allah Most High says: “Then

---

## Page 5528

We caused those whom We chose from among Our servants to inherit the Book. Among them are those who wrong themselves, those who follow a moderate course, and those who are foremost in good deeds by Allah’s permission. That is the great bounty.”

The nation of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, are those who inherited the Book after the earlier nations. This is not restricted to those who have memorized the Quran; rather, everyone who believes in the Quran is included among them. Allah divided them into those who wrong themselves, those who follow a moderate course, and those who are foremost. This differs from the verses in Surahs al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mutaffifīn, and al-Infitār, which encompass all the earlier nations, believers and disbelievers alike. This division, however, concerns the nation of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

“Those who wrong themselves” are those who commit sins and persist in them. Whoever truly repents of his sin, whatever that sin may be, is not thereby excluded from those who are foremost. “Those who follow a moderate course” fulfil their obligations and avoid what is forbidden. “Those who are foremost in good deeds” fulfil their obligations and perform voluntary acts of worship, as described in those verses. Whoever truly repents of his sin, whatever that sin may be, is not thereby excluded from those who are foremost or those who follow a moderate course, as Allah Most High says:

“And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous.”

“Those who spend in ease and hardship, restrain their anger, and pardon people—and Allah loves the doers of good.”

“And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins—and who forgives sins except Allah?—and do not knowingly persist in what they have done.”

“Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will abide forever. How excellent is the reward of

---

## Page 5529

those who do good.”

“Those who follow a moderate course” fulfil their obligations and avoid what is forbidden, while “those who are foremost in good deeds” fulfil their obligations and perform voluntary acts of worship, as described in those verses.

His words, “Gardens of everlasting residence, which they will enter,” are among the evidence Ahl al-Sunnah cite to establish that none of those who affirm Allah’s oneness will remain in Hell forever. As for many perpetrators of major sins entering Hell, this is established through mass-transmitted reports from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Likewise, mass-transmitted reports establish their eventual departure from Hell, the intercession of our Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for perpetrators of major sins, and the deliverance from Hell of those who leave it through the intercession of our Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the intercession of others.

Whoever says that perpetrators of major sins will remain in Hell forever, and interprets the verse to mean that only those who are foremost will enter those gardens, whereas those who follow a moderate course or wrong themselves will not—as some of the Mu'tazilah have interpreted it—is met with the opposing interpretation of the Murji’ah. They do not affirm with certainty that any perpetrator of major sins will enter Hell, and claim that all perpetrators of major sins might enter Paradise without punishment. Both positions contradict the mass-transmitted Sunnah of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the consensus of the early generations of the Muslim community and its leading scholars.

The falsity of the positions of “both groups” is demonstrated by Allah Most High’s statement, which occurs in two verses of His Book:

“Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.”

The Most High thus declares that He does not forgive associating partners with Him, and that He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. This cannot be understood as referring to those who repent, as claimed by some among

---

## Page 5530

the Mu'tazilah, for Allah forgives associating partners with Him when a person repents, and He likewise forgives lesser sins for those who repent. Such forgiveness is therefore not made contingent on His will.

Thus, when speaking of forgiveness for those who repent, the Most High said:

“Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.’”

Here He made forgiveness universal and unqualified, for Allah forgives His servant any sin of which he repents. Whoever repents of associating partners with Allah, Allah forgives him; whoever repents of major sins, Allah forgives him. Whatever sin His servant repents of, Allah forgives him. Thus, in the verse concerning repentance, He made forgiveness universal and unqualified, whereas in the other verse He made a distinction and imposed a condition: He singled out associating partners with Him as something He does not forgive, and made forgiveness of anything else contingent on His will. Denial of the Creator is included in associating partners with Him.

This demonstrates the falsity of the view of anyone who categorically affirms forgiveness for every sinner—or considers it possible that no sin will be punished. By mentioning the association of partners with Him, He also draws attention to what is even graver, such as denial of the Creator. For if that view were correct, He would not have stated that He forgives some but not others. If everyone who wronged himself were forgiven without repentance or good deeds that erase sins, He would not have made that forgiveness contingent on His will.

The Most High’s words,

“but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills,”

are evidence that He forgives some but not others. Thus, both outright denial and a blanket suspension of judgment are invalid.

## Page 5531

Section

Since the “friends of Allah, Mighty and Majestic,” are the pious believers, and people differ in their faith and piety, their friendship with Allah varies accordingly. Likewise, since they differ in disbelief and hypocrisy, their enmity towards Allah varies accordingly.

The foundation of faith and piety is belief in Allah’s messengers. This is encompassed in belief in the Seal of the Messengers, Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for belief in him entails belief in all of Allah’s Books and messengers. The foundation of disbelief and hypocrisy is rejection of the messengers and what they brought. This is the disbelief for which a person deserves punishment in the Hereafter, for Allah Most High has stated in His Book that He does not punish anyone until the message has reached them.

Allah Most High said:

“And We would never punish until We had sent a messenger.”

And He Most High said:

“Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. And We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron and Solomon, and We gave David the Psalms.”

“And We sent messengers whose stories We have related to you before, and messengers whose stories We have not related to you. And Allah spoke to Moses directly.”

## Page 5532

“messengers bringing good news and warnings, so that people would have no argument against Allah after the messengers.”

Allah Most High said concerning the people of the Fire:

“Whenever a group is cast into it, its keepers will ask them, ‘Did no warner come to you?’”

“They will say, ‘Yes, a warner did come to us, but we denied him and said: Allah has revealed nothing; you are only in great error.’”

He thus states that whenever a group is cast into the Fire, they acknowledge that a warner came to them and that they rejected him. This shows that every group cast into it consists of those who rejected the warner. Allah Most High also said, addressing Iblīs:

“I will surely fill Hell with you and all those among them who follow you.”

He thus states that He will fill it with Iblīs and his followers. Once it is filled with them, no one else will enter it. It is therefore clear that none will enter the Fire except those who followed Satan. This indicates that no one without sin will enter it, for such a person has neither followed Satan nor committed sin. What preceded also indicates that none will enter it except those against whom proof has been established through the messengers.

Section

Some people believe in the messengers in general terms. As for detailed belief, much of what the messengers brought may have reached a person, while some of it has not. He believes in whatever has reached him from the messengers, while remaining unaware of what has not reached him; had it reached him, he would have believed in it. Nevertheless, he believes in general terms in everything the messengers brought. If such a person acts upon what he knows Allah has commanded him to do, along with

---

## Page 5533

his faith and piety, he is one of the friends of Allah Most High. His share of friendship with Allah is commensurate with his faith and piety. As for matters concerning which proof has not been established against him, Allah Most High has not required him to know them or believe in them in detail, so He will not punish him for failing to do so. Nevertheless, he misses out on the fullness of friendship with Allah in proportion to what he has missed of those matters. Thus, someone who knows what the messengers brought, believes in it in detail, and acts upon it is more complete in faith and friendship with Allah than someone who neither knows it in detail nor acts upon it. Yet both are friends of Allah Most High.

Paradise has ranks that differ immensely, and Allah’s believing, pious friends occupy those ranks according to their faith and piety.

He, Blessed and Most High, said:

“Whoever desires this fleeting life, We hasten therein whatever We will for whomever We choose. Then We have appointed Hell for him, which he will enter, condemned and banished.”

“But whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it as he should, while being a believer—it is they whose striving will be appreciated.”

“To each We extend the gifts of your Lord—to these and to those. The gifts of your Lord are not withheld.”

“See how We have favoured some over others. But the Hereafter is greater in ranks and greater in distinction.”

Allah, Glorified and Most High, thus explains that He extends His gifts both to those who desire this world and to those who desire the Hereafter, and that His gifts are withheld from neither the righteous nor the wicked. Then He, Most High, said:

“See how We have favoured some over others. But the Hereafter is greater in ranks and greater in distinction.”

Allah, Glorified be He, thus explains that the differences in rank among the people of the Hereafter are greater than those among people in this world, and that its ranks are greater than the ranks of this world. He has also made clear

Section

Since a servant can only be a friend of Allah if he is a believer who fears Him, as He, Most High, says:

“Indeed, the friends of Allah will have no fear, nor will they grieve—those who believe and are mindful of Him,”

and as stated in the well-known hadith in Sahīh al-Bukhārī, already cited, in which Allah, Blessed and Most High, says:

“My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts of worship until I love him,”

and since he cannot be a believer who fears Allah until he draws near to Him through the obligatory acts of worship, thereby becoming one of the righteous

---

## Page 5536

—those of the right hand—and thereafter continues to draw near through voluntary acts of worship until he becomes one of the foremost, those brought near to Allah, it is evident that no disbeliever or hypocrite can be a friend of Allah. The same applies to those whose faith and worship are not valid, even supposing that they bear no sin, such as the children of disbelievers and those whom the call to Islam has not reached—even if it is held that they will not be punished until a messenger is sent to them. They cannot be among Allah’s friends unless they are believers who fear Him. Whoever does not draw near to Allah, whether by doing good deeds or refraining from evil deeds, is not among His friends. The same applies to the insane and to children, for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“The pen of accountability has been lifted from three: the insane person until he regains his sanity, the child until he reaches puberty, and the sleeper until he awakens.”

This hadith was narrated by the compilers of the Sunan collections on the authority of ‘Alī and ‘Ā’ishah, may Allah be pleased with them both. The scholars versed in hadith have unanimously accepted it. However, according to the majority of scholars, the acts of worship of a child who has reached the age of discernment are valid, and he is rewarded for them.

As for the insane person from whom the pen of accountability has been lifted, none of his acts of worship is valid, by scholarly consensus. Neither his faith nor his disbelief is valid, nor are his prayer or any other acts of worship. Indeed, rational people generally consider him unfit even for worldly pursuits such as commerce and crafts. He is not fit to work as a cloth merchant, perfumer, blacksmith, or carpenter, and his contracts are invalid by scholarly consensus. Thus, his sales, purchases, marriage, divorce, acknowledgments, and testimony are not valid, nor any other

---

## Page 5537

statements. Rather, all his statements are without legal effect: no ruling of Islamic law, reward, or punishment attaches to them. This differs from a child who has reached the age of discernment: in some matters, his statements have legal effect according to scriptural texts and scholarly consensus, while in others their effect is disputed.

If an insane person’s faith, fear of Allah, and drawing near to Him through obligatory and voluntary acts of worship are not valid, and he therefore cannot be a friend of Allah, then no one may believe that he is a friend of Allah. This is especially so when the evidence offered is either some disclosure of hidden matters heard from him, or some exercise of extraordinary power—for example, seeing him point at someone who then dies or falls into a fit. For it is known that disbelievers and hypocrites—among the polytheists and the People of the Book—have disclosures of hidden matters and extraordinary powers originating from devils, as do soothsayers, sorcerers, and devotees among the polytheists and the People of the Book.

No one may therefore infer from such things alone that a person is a friend of Allah, even if nothing is known about him that contradicts friendship with Allah. How, then, could this be permissible when something is known about him that does contradict it? For example, he may be known not to believe that following the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is obligatory both inwardly and outwardly; rather, he believes that he follows the outward religious law, but not the inward reality. Or he may believe that Allah’s friends have a path to Allah other than the path of the prophets, peace be upon them.

Or he may say, “The prophets have made the path narrow,” or, “They are exemplars for ordinary people, not the elect,” and similar things said by some who claim friendship with Allah. Such people harbour disbelief that is incompatible with faith, let alone friendship with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Whoever cites the extraordinary feats performed by any of them as evidence of their friendship with Allah is more astray than the Jews and Christians.

---

## Page 5538

The same applies to an insane person, for his insanity precludes the validity of the faith and acts of worship that are prerequisites for friendship with Allah. As for someone who is sometimes insane and sometimes lucid, if, during his lucid periods, he believes in Allah and His Messenger, fulfils his obligations, and avoids what is forbidden, then his insanity does not prevent Allah from rewarding him for the faith and fear of Allah he displayed while lucid. His share of friendship with Allah will be commensurate with that.

Likewise, if someone becomes insane after having had faith and feared Allah, Allah will reward and recompense him for his previous faith and fear of Him. He will not nullify that because of the insanity with which the person has been afflicted through no sin of his own. During his insanity, he is not held accountable.

Accordingly, if someone presents himself as a friend of Allah while neither fulfilling his obligations nor avoiding what is forbidden—and may even do things contrary to these requirements—no one may say, “This is a friend of Allah.” If such a person is not insane, but is merely bewildered without being insane, or if he loses his reason through insanity at times and regains it at others, yet does not fulfil his obligations and instead believes that he is not obliged to follow the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, then he is a disbeliever. If, however, he is insane both inwardly and outwardly and is no longer held accountable, then, although he is not punished as disbelievers are punished, he is not entitled to the honour from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to which people of faith and fear of Allah are entitled. In neither case may anyone believe him to be a friend of Allah. But if he had a lucid period during which he believed in Allah and feared Him, his share of friendship with Allah would be commensurate with that.

---

## Page 5539

But if he harbours disbelief or hypocrisy while lucid, or was a disbeliever or hypocrite before becoming insane, then he bears disbelief or hypocrisy for which he is liable to punishment. His insanity does not absolve him of the disbelief or hypocrisy he displays while lucid.

Section

Allah’s friends have no distinctive outward features in matters that are permissible. They are not distinguished by wearing one kind of clothing rather than another when both are permissible, nor by shaving, trimming, or braiding their hair when that is permissible. As the saying goes:

“How many a truthful believer wears a coat,
And how many a heretic wears a cloak!”

Rather, they are found among all groups within the community of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, provided they are not among those given to manifest religious innovations or wickedness. They are found among people devoted to the Quran and people of knowledge, among those who wage jihad and wield the sword, and among merchants, craftsmen, and farmers. Allah mentions the various groups within the community of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, in His words, Most High:

“Your Lord knows that you stand in prayer for nearly two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, as do some of those with you. Allah determines the night and the day. He knows that you cannot keep precise account of it, so He has turned to you in mercy. Recite, then, whatever you can of the Quran. He knows that some of you will be ill, others travelling through the land seeking Allah’s bounty, and others fighting in Allah’s cause. So recite whatever you can of it.”

---

## Page 5540

The early generations called people of religious devotion and learning “the reciters,” a designation that included both scholars and ascetics. Later, the terms “Sufis” and “the poor” came into use. The term “Sufi” derives from wearing wool (sūf); this is the correct explanation. It has also been said to derive from safwat al-fuqahā’ (the elite of the jurists); from Sūfa ibn Udd ibn Tānja, an Arab tribe known for religious devotion; from the people of the Suffa (the shaded portico); from safā (purity); from safwa (the elite); or from the foremost rank before Allah Most High. These explanations are weak, for if that were its derivation, the term would have been suffī, safā’ī, safawī, or saffī, rather than sūfī.

The designation “the poor” also came to refer to those following the spiritual path. This is a later usage. People have disputed which designation is superior: “Sufi” or “poor.” They also dispute which is better: a grateful rich person or a patient poor person.

This latter question was the subject of an early disagreement between al-Junayd and Abū al-‘Abbās ibn ‘Atā’, and two positions on it have been reported from Ahmad ibn Hanbal. The correct position on all of this is expressed in the words of Allah, Blessed and Most High:

“O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.”

And in the Sahīh, Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reports from the Prophet

---

## Page 5541

, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he was asked:

“Which people are best?” He replied, “The most righteous among them.” They said, “That is not what we are asking you about.” He replied, “Joseph, the prophet of Allah, son of Jacob, the prophet of Allah, son of Isaac, the prophet of Allah, son of Abraham, the close friend of Allah.” They said, “That is not what we are asking you about.” He replied, “Are you asking me about the ancestral stocks of the Arabs? People are like mines of gold and silver: the best of them in pre-Islamic times are the best of them in Islam, provided they gain understanding of the religion.”

Thus, the Quran and Sunnah establish that the most noble people in Allah’s sight are the most righteous. In the Sunan, it is reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“No Arab is superior to a non-Arab, nor a non-Arab to an Arab; no black person is superior to a white person, nor a white person to a black person, except through righteousness. You all descend from Adam, and Adam was created from dust.”

It is also reported that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah Most High has removed from you the arrogance of pre-Islamic ignorance and its pride in ancestry. People are of two kinds: a righteous believer and a wicked, wretched person.”

Whoever among these groups is most mindful of Allah is most noble in His sight. If two people are equal in righteousness, they are equal in rank. The term “poverty” in the revealed texts may refer to a lack of wealth or to a creature’s need for its Creator, as Allah Most High says:

“Alms are only for the poor and the needy.”

and He Most High says:

## Page 5545

is jihad in Allah’s cause.” He also said:

“Their sides forsake their beds; they call upon their Lord in fear and hope, and spend out of what We have provided for them. No soul knows what joy is kept hidden for them as a reward for what they used to do.”

Then he said, “O Muādh, shall I tell you what holds all of that together?”

I replied, “Yes.”

He said, “Restrain this tongue of yours,” and took hold of his tongue.

Muādh said, “O Messenger of Allah, will we really be held accountable for what we say?”

He replied, “For shame, O Muādh! What casts people into the Fire on their noses but the harvest of their tongues?”

This is explained by his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as authentically reported in the two Sahīhs:

“Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.”

Speaking good is better than remaining silent about it, while refraining from evil speech is better than uttering it. As for perpetual silence, it is a prohibited religious innovation. Likewise, abstaining from eating bread and meat and from drinking water is also among the blameworthy religious innovations. As authentically reported in Sahīh al-Bukhārī, Ibn Abbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, narrated that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw a man standing in the sun and asked, “What is this?”

They replied, “It is Abū Isrā’īl. He has vowed to stand in the sun, not to seek shade or speak, and to fast.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Tell him to sit down, seek shade, speak, and complete his fast.”

## Page 5546

It is also authentically reported in the two Sahīhs that Anas narrated:

“Some men asked about the worship of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and seemed to consider it little. They said, ‘But which of us is like the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?’ Then one of them said, ‘As for me, I shall fast without ever breaking my fast.’ Another said, ‘As for me, I shall pray at night and never sleep.’ Another said, ‘As for me, I shall not eat meat.’ Another said, ‘As for me, I shall not marry women.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘What is the matter with men who say such things? I fast and break my fast, pray at night and sleep, eat meat and marry women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me.’”

This means following a different way in the belief that it is better than his. Whoever does so has disassociated himself from Allah and His Messenger. Allah Most High says:

“Who would turn away from the religion of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself?”

Rather, every Muslim must believe that the best speech is Allah’s speech and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. It is authentically reported that he would proclaim this in his sermon every Friday.

Section

It is not a condition of being an ally of Allah that one be infallible, never making a mistake or falling into error. Rather, some knowledge of the Sharia may remain unknown to him, and certain religious matters may become confused for him, to the point that he regards some things as commanded by Allah and others as forbidden

---

## Page 5547

by Allah. He may also suppose that certain extraordinary occurrences are among the miraculous gifts granted to Allah Most High’s allies, when in fact they are from Satan, who has disguised them for him because of his deficient spiritual rank. He does not recognize that they are from Satan, although he may not thereby cease to be an ally of Allah Most High.

For Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has pardoned this community for mistakes, forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to do. Allah Most High says:

“The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and so have the believers. All have believed in Allah, His angels, His Books, and His messengers: ‘We make no distinction between any of His messengers.’ And they say, ‘We hear and obey. We seek Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return.’”

“Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It will have the good it has earned, and it will bear the evil it has earned. ‘Our Lord, do not hold us accountable if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no strength to bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so grant us victory over the disbelieving people.’”

It is authentically established in the two Sahīhs that Allah, glorified is He, answered this supplication and said, “I have done so.” In Sahīh Muslim, Ibn ‘Abbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, narrated:

“When this verse was revealed—‘Whether you disclose what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. He then forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah has power over all things’—their hearts were gripped by a distress more severe than anything they had ever felt before. ---

## Page 5548

up to His words, ‘or make a mistake.’ Allah said, ‘I have done so.’ ‘Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us.’ He said, ‘I have done so.’ ‘Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no strength to bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so grant us victory over the disbelieving people.’ He said, ‘I have done so.’”

Allah Most High also says:

“There is no blame upon you for what you do by mistake, but only for what your hearts deliberately intend.”

It is authentically established in the two Sahīhs, in narrations from Abū Hurayra and ‘Amr ibn al-‘Ās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When a judge exercises independent judgment and is correct, he has two rewards; if he errs, he has one reward.”

Thus, he did not deem someone sinful for erring in the exercise of independent judgment. Rather, he granted him a reward for his effort and declared his error forgiven. However, someone whose independent judgment is correct receives two rewards and is therefore superior to him.

Since an ally of Allah may make mistakes, people are not obliged to believe everything an ally of Allah says; otherwise, he would be a prophet. Indeed, an ally of Allah may not rely on what is cast into his heart, or on experiences he regards as inspiration, communication, or an address from the True One, unless it accords with the revealed law. Rather, he must assess all of this against what Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, brought. If it agrees with that, he accepts it; if it contradicts it, he does not accept it. If he does not know whether it agrees or contradicts, he must suspend judgment.

In this matter, people fall into “three categories”: two extremes and a middle course. Some, once they believe that a person is an ally of Allah, agree with him in everything they think has been communicated

---

## Page 5549

to his heart from his Lord, and unquestioningly accept everything he does. Others, when they see him say or do something that does not accord with the revealed law, exclude him entirely from Allah’s allies, even if he has erred while exercising independent judgment. The best course lies between these extremes: he should neither be regarded as infallible nor held sinful when he errs in exercising independent judgment. He is not to be followed in everything he says, nor judged a disbeliever or an evildoer when he has exercised independent judgment. People are obliged to follow what Allah sent His Messenger with. However, if he disagrees with some jurists while agreeing with others, no one has the right to compel him to adopt the opposing opinion and say, “This man has contradicted the revealed law.”

It is authentically established in the two Sahīhs that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Among the nations before you were men who received inspiration. If there is anyone like them in my community, ‘Umar is one of them.”

Al-Tirmidhī and others narrated that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Had I not been sent among you, ‘Umar would have been sent among you.”

In another hadith:

“Allah has placed the truth upon ‘Umar’s tongue and in his heart.”

It also states:

“Had there been a prophet after me, it would have been ‘Umar.”

‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say, “We did not consider it unlikely that al-sakīna spoke through ‘Umar’s tongue.” This is authentically established from him through the narration of al-Sha‘bī.

Ibn ‘Umar said:

“Whenever ‘Umar said of something, ‘I believe it to be such-and-such,’ it turned out as he said.”

Qays ibn Tāriq said, “We used to say that an angel spoke through ‘Umar’s tongue.”

And ‘Umar used to say:

## Page 5550

“Draw close to those who obey Allah and listen to what they say, for truths are made manifest to them.”

These truths which ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said become manifest to the obedient are matters that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, discloses to them. It is thus established that Allah’s allies receive communications and have hidden matters disclosed to them. The best of these people in this community after Abū Bakr is ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb, may Allah be pleased with them both, for the best of this community after its Prophet is Abū Bakr, followed by ‘Umar.

An authentic report specifically identifies ‘Umar as one who receives inspiration in this community. Whoever might be supposed to receive inspiration or communications in the community of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ‘Umar is superior to him. Nevertheless, ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, would do what was incumbent upon him: he would assess whatever came to him against what the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had brought. Sometimes it agreed with that, and this was counted among ‘Umar’s virtues, as when the Quran was revealed in agreement with his views on more than one occasion. At other times it differed, and ‘Umar would retract his view, as he did at al-Hudaybiya, when he had favored fighting the polytheists. The account is well known in al-Bukhārī and elsewhere.

For “the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, set out to perform ‘umrah (the lesser pilgrimage) in the sixth year after the Hijrah, accompanied by approximately fourteen hundred Muslims. These were the people who pledged allegiance to him beneath the tree. Following negotiations between himself and the polytheists, he concluded a peace agreement with them, undertaking to return that year and perform ‘umrah the following year. He agreed to conditions in their favor that entailed a degree of humiliation for the Muslims in

---

## Page 5551

outward appearance. This weighed heavily on many Muslims, but Allah and His Messenger had greater knowledge and wisdom concerning the benefit it entailed. ‘Umar was among those who disliked it, to the point that he said to the Prophet, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace, ‘O Messenger of Allah, are we not upon the truth and our enemy upon falsehood?’

He replied, ‘Yes.’

‘Umar asked, ‘Are not our slain in Paradise and their slain in the Fire?’

He replied, ‘Yes.’

‘Umar said, ‘Why, then, should we accept humiliation in our religion?’

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, told him, ‘I am the Messenger of Allah. He will grant me victory, and I will not disobey Him.’

‘Umar then asked, ‘Did you not tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?’

He replied, ‘Yes. But did I tell you that you would come to it this year?’

‘Umar answered, ‘No.’

He said, ‘You will indeed come to it and circumambulate it.’

‘Umar then went to Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them both, and said to him what he had said to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Abū Bakr gave him the same answer as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

Yet Abū Bakr had not heard the Prophet’s answer, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Thus Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, was more completely in accord with Allah and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, than ‘Umar was. ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, retracted his position and said, “I performed deeds on that account.”

Likewise, when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, died, ‘Umar initially denied his death. But when Abū Bakr said that he had died, ‘Umar retracted his position. Likewise, regarding “fighting those who withheld zakat,” ‘Umar said to Abū Bakr, “How can we fight the people when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘I have been commanded to

---

## Page 5552

fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah. Once they do so, they will have protected their lives and property from me, except where a rightful claim applies.’?”

Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, replied, “Did he not say, ‘Except where a rightful claim applies’? Zakat is one such rightful claim. By Allah, if they withheld from me even a young she-goat that they used to give to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, I would fight them for withholding it.”

‘Umar said, “By Allah, as soon as I saw that Allah had opened Abū Bakr’s heart to fighting, I knew that it was right.”

There are similar examples demonstrating Abū Bakr’s superiority over ‘Umar, even though ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, was a muhaddath (one granted inspiration). The rank of the siddīq (one of consummate truthfulness) is above that of the muhaddath, because the siddīq receives from the infallible Messenger everything the Messenger says and does, whereas the muhaddath receives certain things from his own heart. His heart, however, is not infallible, so he must test what he receives against what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, brought.

For this reason, ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, would consult the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, debate with them, and defer to them in certain matters. They would dispute some matters with him, and he would present evidence against them while they presented evidence against him from the Quran and Sunnah. He allowed them to disagree with him and did not tell them, “I am a muhaddath, inspired and spoken to, so you must accept what I say and not oppose me.”

Thus, if anyone claims—or his companions claim on his behalf—that he is an ally of Allah who is spoken to, and that his followers must therefore accept everything he says, never oppose him, and accept his spiritual state without assessing it against the Quran and Sunnah, then both he and they are mistaken. Such a person is among the most misguided of people. For ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb, may Allah be pleased with him, is superior to him, and he is

---

## Page 5553

the Commander of the Faithful, yet the Muslims would dispute what he said, while both he and they adhered to the Quran and Sunnah. The early generations of this community and its leading scholars agreed that anyone’s statements may be accepted or rejected, except those of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

This is one of the distinctions between the prophets and others. The prophets, may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon them, must be believed in everything they convey from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and obeyed in what they command. This is unlike Allah’s allies: it is not obligatory to obey everything they command or believe everything they report. Rather, their commands and reports must be assessed against the Quran and Sunnah. Whatever agrees with the Quran and Sunnah must be accepted, and whatever contradicts them must be rejected—even if the person who said it is one of Allah’s allies and has exercised independent judgment, is excused for what he said, and is rewarded for his effort. Nevertheless, if he contradicts the Quran and Sunnah, he is mistaken. His error is forgiven if he has feared Allah to the best of his ability, for Allah Most High says:

“So fear Allah as much as you are able.”

This explains His words, Most High:

“O you who believe, fear Allah as He should be feared.”

Ibn Mas‘ūd and others said, “Fearing Him as He should be feared means that He is obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, and thanked and not met with ingratitude.” That is, according to your ability, for Allah Most High does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. As He, Most High, says:

“Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. It will have the good it has earned, and bear the evil it has earned.”

And He, Most High, says:

“But those who believe and do righteous deeds—We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity—will be the inhabitants of Paradise, abiding there forever.”

And He, Most High, says: “And give full measure

and weight with justice. We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity.”

Those are the ones who have been true, and those are the ones who fear Allah.”

What I have mentioned—that Allah’s allies must adhere firmly to the Quran and Sunnah, and that none of them is infallible such that he or anyone else may follow whatever occurs in his heart without assessing it against the Quran and Sunnah—is something upon which the allies of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, have agreed. Anyone who disagrees with this is not among those allies of Allah, glorified is He, whom Allah has commanded

Anyone who goes against any part of what the Messenger brought, following someone whom he believes to be a friend of Allah, bases his position on the assumption that this person is a friend of Allah and that a friend of Allah must never be contradicted in anything. None of these things indicates that the person is a friend of Allah. The miraculous gifts bestowed upon the friends of Allah Most High are greater than these things. It is therefore impermissible to suppose that everyone who displays any such feat is a friend of Allah. They are recognized by the light of faith and the Quran, by the inward realities of faith, and by the outward observances prescribed by Islam.

Section

“Reality”—the reality of religion, the religion of the Lord of all worlds—is what the prophets and messengers agreed upon, even though each had a law and a way. Shirʿa means sharīʿa (religious law). Allah Most High says:

“To each of you We have prescribed a law and a way.”

The Most High also says:

“Then We set you upon a law in matters of religion, so follow it, and do not follow the desires of those who do not know. They can be of no help to you against Allah. Indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another, while Allah is the ally of the righteous.”

Minhāj means a path. The Most High says:

Ahl al-Sunnah al-Nabawiyyah fī Naqd Kalām Ahl al-Shī‘ah wa-l-Qadariyyah”.

In short, the Sunni and Shia groups agree that the best member of this community after its Prophet is one of the caliphs. No one who comes after the Companions can be superior to the Companions. Later, a number of people emerged, each claiming to be the Seal of Allah’s Close Friends. Some of them claim that the Seal of Allah’s Close Friends surpasses the Seal of the Prophets in knowledge of Allah, and that the prophets acquire their knowledge of Allah through him. Such is the claim of Ibn Arabī, the author of al-Futūhāt al-Makkiyyah and al-Fusūs. It is as one would say to someone who declared, “The roof fell upon them from beneath them”: “Neither reason nor Quran!”

## Page 5569

“Those messengers—We favored some of them over others. Among them were those to whom Allah spoke, and He raised some of them in rank.”

There are other proofs besides these. Each of the prophets receives revelation from Allah. The communities before us needed people granted inspiration, unlike the community of Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace. and righteous deeds that He had distributed among the other prophets. Thus, the excellence with which Allah favored him came from Allah, through what He revealed and sent to him, not through a human intermediary.

Whatever guidance and true religion he attains comes through Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Likewise, anyone reached by the message of a messenger sent to him can be a close friend of Allah only by following that messenger.

then he is worse than those Jews and Christians who said:

He is therefore an unbeliever, and his unbelief is greater than theirs. For inward knowledge—the knowledge of the faith, understanding, and states of the heart—is knowledge of the inward realities of faith. This is nobler than knowledge merely of the outward acts of Islam.

## Page 5571

Thus, if someone claims that Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—knew only these outward matters, but not the realities of faith, and that he himself does not derive these realities from the Quran and the Sunnah, he is claiming that the portion of the Messenger’s teachings in which he believes is inferior to the other portion. This is worse than someone who says, “I believe in part and disbelieve in part,” without claiming that the part he believes in is the lesser of the two.

These heretics claim that “closeness to Allah” is superior to “prophethood.” They mislead people by saying, “His closeness to Allah is superior to his prophethood,” and reciting:

“The station of prophethood lies between the two:
Just above the messenger, below the close friend.”

They say, “We share with him in his closeness to Allah, which is greater than his messengership.” This is among their gravest errors. No one has equalled Muhammad in his closeness to Allah—not Abraham or Moses, let alone these heretics.

Every messenger is a prophet and a close friend of Allah. Thus, a messenger is both a prophet and a close friend of Allah: his messengership encompasses his prophethood, and his prophethood encompasses his closeness to Allah. If they suppose that Allah merely informs him without his being a close friend of Allah, this is an impossible supposition. For when Allah informs him, he cannot be anything other than a close friend of Allah. His prophethood cannot be separated from his closeness to Allah; and even if it were supposed to be separate, no one would equal the Messenger in his closeness to Allah.

---

## Page 5572

These people may claim—as does Ibn ‘Arabī, the author of “al-Fusūs”—that they draw from the same source as the angel through whom revelation is conveyed to the Messenger. This is because they adopted “the creed of the philosophers” and then presented it in the guise of “spiritual unveiling.”

These philosophers maintain that the celestial spheres are eternal, without beginning, and have a cause which they seek to resemble, as Aristotle and his followers say; or that they have a cause which necessitates their existence by its very essence, as their later followers, such as Ibn Sīnā and others, say. They do not affirm that these spheres belong to a Lord who created the heavens, the earth, and everything between them in six days, nor that He created things by His will and power. They also deny that He knows particulars: either they deny His knowledge altogether, as Aristotle does, or they say that, concerning changing things, He knows only their universals, as Ibn Sīnā does. In reality, this position amounts to denying His knowledge of those things.

For everything that exists in external reality is an individual particular. Each individual celestial sphere is a particular, as are all concrete entities, their attributes, and their actions. Whoever knows only universals knows none of the things that actually exist. Universals exist as universals only in the mind, not in concrete reality.

These people are discussed at length elsewhere, in “Radd ta‘ārud al-‘aql wa-l-naql” (Refuting the Conflict between Reason and Revelation) and other works. Their unbelief is greater than that of the Jews and Christians, and even that of the Arab polytheists. All these groups affirm that Allah created the heavens and the earth, and that He brought created beings into existence by His will and power. Aristotle and other philosophers like him

---

## Page 5573

and the Greeks worshipped the celestial bodies and idols. They had no knowledge of the angels and prophets, and Aristotle’s books contain no mention of any of these. Their learning was chiefly concerned with natural phenomena. As for divine matters, each of them was seldom right and frequently wrong. Even after abrogation and alteration, the Jews and Christians know far more about divine matters than they do. Their later followers, however, such as Ibn Sīnā, sought to patch together their predecessors’ teachings and what the Messengers had brought. They borrowed elements from the principles of the Jahmiyyah and the Muʿtazilah and constructed a doctrine to which philosophers belonging to religious communities may profess allegiance. It contains errors and contradictions, some of which we have pointed out elsewhere.

When these thinkers saw that the mission of Messengers such as Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—had dazzled the world, acknowledged that the law with which Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—was sent was the greatest law ever to reach the world, and found that the prophets had spoken of angels and jinn, they sought to reconcile all this with the teachings of their Greek predecessors. Yet those predecessors were the furthest of all people from knowing Allah, His angels, His Books, His Messengers, and the Last Day.

Those predecessors affirmed ten intellects, which they called “immaterial entities” and “separate entities.” This notion was originally derived from the soul’s separation from the body. They called these entities “separate” because they are separate from matter and free of it. They also affirmed the celestial spheres, assigning a soul to each sphere. Most of them regarded these souls as accidents, while some regarded them as substances. Upon examination, these “immaterial entities” which they affirmed amount to things

---

## Page 5574

that exist in the mind, not in external reality, just as Plato’s followers posited “abstract Platonic Forms.” They posited matter abstracted from form, and abstract duration and void. Their most accomplished thinkers acknowledged that these exist only in the mind, not in external reality.

When their later followers, such as Ibn Sīnā, sought to establish prophethood on their corrupt principles, they claimed that prophethood has three distinctive characteristics, and that whoever possesses them is a prophet.

The first is that he possesses an intellectual faculty, which they call the “sacred faculty,” through which he acquires knowledge without instruction.

The second is that he possesses an imaginative faculty that presents to him in images what he apprehends intellectually within himself. Thus, he sees forms within himself or hears sounds within himself, just as a sleeper sees and hears, although these have no external existence. They claimed that those forms are Allah’s angels and those sounds are the speech of Allah Most High.

The third is that he possesses an active faculty through which he influences the matter of the world. They reduced the miracles of the prophets, the extraordinary gifts bestowed upon Allah’s righteous servants, and the extraordinary feats of sorcerers to powers of the soul. Thus, they acknowledged those that accorded with their principles, such as turning a staff into a serpent, but not the splitting of the moon and the like, for they deny that such things occurred.

---

## Page 5575

We have discussed these people at length in several places. We have explained that their claims are utterly unsound; that ordinary individuals and followers of the prophets attain things greater than what they have designated as distinctive characteristics; and that the angels described by the messengers are living, speaking beings, the greatest of Allah’s creatures. They are numerous, as Allah Most High says:

“And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him.”

They are not ten in number, nor are they accidents. These people, moreover, claim that the first emanation is the “First Intellect,” from which everything beneath it emanated, and that the “Tenth Active Intellect” is the lord of everything below the lunar sphere. The falsity of all this is known by necessity from the religion of the messengers: no angel is the originator of everything other than Allah.

These people claim that this is the intellect mentioned in a report which states:

“When Allah first created the intellect, He said to it, ‘Come forward,’ and it came forward. Then He said to it, ‘Go back,’ and it went back. Then He said, ‘By My might, I have created nothing more honoured in My sight than you. Through you I take, and through you I give. Yours is the reward, and upon you is the punishment.’”

They also call it “the Pen,” citing the hadith beginning, “When Allah first created the Pen,” narrated by al-Tirmidhī.

The report they mention concerning the intellect is a lie, fabricated according to the hadith experts, as stated by Abū Hātim al-Bustī, al-Dāraqutnī, Ibn al-Jawzī and others. It does not appear in any of the authoritative hadith collections. Yet even so,

---

## Page 5576

its wording, if authentic, would constitute evidence against them. For it reads: “When Allah Most High first created the intellect, He said to it”—or, according to another version, “When Allah created the intellect, He said to it.” The report thus means that He addressed it at the very beginning of its creation, not that it was the first of all created things. The word awwal (“first”) is in the accusative as an adverb of time, corresponding to lammā (“when”) in the other wording.

The report continues: “I have created nothing more honoured in My sight than you.” This implies that He had created other things before it. He then said: “Through you I take, and through you I give. Yours is the reward, and upon you is the punishment.” Thus, He mentioned four kinds of accidents, whereas they maintain that all the substances of the upper and lower worlds emanated from that intellect. How far apart these two accounts are!

Their error arises because the word “intellect” in Muslim usage does not mean what it means in the usage of these Greeks. In Muslim usage, ʿaql (“reasoning”) is the verbal noun of ʿaqala, yaʿqilu (“to reason”), as in the Quran:

“And they will say, ‘If only we had listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze.’”

“Indeed, in that are signs for people who reason.”

“Have they not travelled through the land, so that they may have hearts with which to reason, or ears with which to hear?”

“Intellect” also denotes the innate faculty Allah Most High has placed in human beings by which they reason. For those people, however, the intellect is a self-subsisting substance, like a being endowed with intellect. This does not accord with the language of the messengers and the Quran.

As Abū Hāmid relates, their “realm of creation” is the realm of bodies, while he calls the intellect and souls the “realm of command.” The intellect may also be called the realm of jabarūt (supreme power), souls the realm of malakūt (dominion), and bodies

---

## Page 5577

the realm of mulk (sovereignty). Those unfamiliar with the language of the messengers and the meaning of the Quran and Sunnah suppose that their references to sovereignty, dominion and supreme power accord with this scheme. But that is not so.

These people mislead Muslims in many ways. For example, they describe the “celestial sphere” as “originated,” meaning merely that it is caused, even though they consider it eternal. Yet whatever is originated must have been preceded by nonexistence. Neither in Arabic nor in any other language is something eternal and without beginning called originated. Allah has declared that He is the Creator of everything. Everything created is originated, and everything originated comes into existence after not having existed.

However, the speculative theologians among the Jahmiyyah and Muʿtazilah debated them inadequately: they neither properly understood what the messengers had conveyed nor rigorously established the conclusions of reason. Thus, they neither championed Islam nor defeated its enemies. They shared some of those people’s false premises while disputing some of their sound rational conclusions. Their shortcomings in knowledge derived from revelation and reason therefore helped strengthen the others’ misguidance, as has been explained at length elsewhere.

These philosophers sometimes identify “Gabriel” with the image that takes shape within the soul of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while imagination is subordinate to the intellect. Then came heretics who shared the views of these heretical philosophers and claimed to be “friends of Allah,” that Allah’s friends are superior to His prophets, and that they receive directly from Allah without an intermediary. Among them was Ibn ʿArabī, author of al-Futūhāt and al-Fusūs, who said:

## Page 5578

that he draws from the same source as the angel who conveys revelation to the Messenger. By “source” he means the intellect, and by “angel” he means imagination. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has described the angels in His Book in terms that contradict these people’s claims. For example, the Exalted says:

## Page 5580

It is established in the two Sahīh collections, on the authority of ‘Ā’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “saw Gabriel in the form in which he was created only twice.” This means the first occasion on the highest horizon and the other descent by the lote tree of the utmost boundary.

Elsewhere, Allah describes Gabriel, peace be upon him, as the Trustworthy Spirit and the Holy Spirit, among other attributes which make clear that he is among the greatest of Allah Most High’s living, intelligent creatures, and that he is a substance subsisting in his own right—not an image in the Prophet’s mind, as claimed by these heretical philosophers and those who claim to be friends of Allah and more knowledgeable than the prophets.

Ultimately, their position amounts to denying the “foundations of faith”: belief in Allah, His angels, His Books, His messengers, and the Last Day. In reality, their position is a denial of the Creator, for they have identified the existence of creation with the existence of the Creator, saying, “Existence is one.” They have failed to distinguish between numerical unity and unity of kind. Existing things share in what is denoted by existence, just as human beings share in what is denoted by humanity, and animals in what is denoted by animal. Yet this shared universal exists as a shared universal only in the mind. In actual reality, the animal nature subsisting in this human being is not the animal nature subsisting in a horse, and the existence of the heavens is not the very same existence as that of a human being. Thus, the existence of the Creator—majestic is His glory—is not like the existence of His creatures.

---

## Page 5581

In essence, their position is that of Pharaoh, who denied the Creator. He did not deny the reality we witness, but claimed that it exists of itself and has no maker. These people agreed with him on this, but claimed that it is Allah. They were therefore more astray than he was, even though the falsity of his position was more obvious than theirs. Accordingly, they maintained that idol worshippers worshipped none but Allah, saying:

“Since Pharaoh held the position of command and wielded the sword, even if he was unjust by the standards of religious law, he accordingly said, ‘I am your lord most high’—meaning: although all are lords in some respect, I am higher than you by virtue of the outward authority I have been given over you.”

They said:

“When the sorcerers recognized that Pharaoh had spoken truthfully, they acknowledged this and said, ‘So decree whatever you will decree; you can only decree concerning this worldly life.’ They said: Thus Pharaoh’s declaration, ‘I am your lord most high,’ was true, and Pharaoh was the Real Himself.”

They then denied the reality of the Last Day, claiming that the people of Hell enjoy bliss just as the people of Paradise do. Thus, they disbelieved in Allah, the Last Day, His angels, His Books, and His messengers, while claiming to be the very elite of the innermost circle of Allah’s friends. They also claimed to be superior to the prophets, and that the prophets derive their knowledge of Allah only from their light.

This is not the place to expound upon these people’s heresy. However, since the discussion concerns “the friends of Allah” and the distinction between “the friends of the Most Merciful and the friends of Satan,” and since these people are among the most emphatic in claiming friendship with Allah while being among Satan’s closest allies, we have drawn attention to this. For this reason, most of their discourse concerns states

“Whoever turns a blind eye to the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We assign to him a devil who becomes his companion.”

“They certainly turn them away from the path, while they think they are rightly guided.”

Up to His words:

I disavow your having previously associated me with Allah. Indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.’”

Allah Most High also says:

“And when Satan made their deeds seem fair to them and said, ‘No one among the people can overcome you today, and I am your protector.’ But when the two forces came within sight of one another, he turned on his heels and said, ‘I have nothing to do with you. I see what you do not see. I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment.’”

It has been related from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in an authentic hadith

---

## Page 5583

that “he saw Gabriel marshaling the angels.”

When the devils see Allah’s angels, with whom He supports His servants, they flee from them. Allah supports His believing servants with His angels. Allah Most High says:

“When your Lord revealed to the angels, ‘I am with you, so strengthen those who believe.’”

Allah Most High also says:

“O you who believe, remember Allah’s favor upon you when armies came against you, and We sent against them a wind and armies you did not see.”

Allah Most High also says:

“When he said to his companion, ‘Do not grieve; Allah is with us.’ Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with armies you did not see.”

Allah Most High also says:

“When you said to the believers, ‘Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?’”

“Yes indeed! If you remain steadfast and mindful of Allah, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels bearing marks of distinction.”

These people, however, are visited by spirits that speak to them and appear before them. They are jinn and devils, yet these people imagine them to be angels—like the spirits that speak to those who worship the heavenly bodies and idols.

Among the first of these people to appear in Islam was al-Mukhtār ibn Abī ʿUbayd, whom the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, foretold in the authentic hadith recorded by Muslim in his Sahīh. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“There will be among Thaqīf a liar and a destroyer.”

The liar was al-Mukhtār ibn Abī ʿUbayd, and the destroyer was al-Hajjāj ibn Yūsuf.

Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās were told, “Al-Mukhtār claims that something descends to him.” They both replied, “He has spoken the truth. Allah Most High says:

‘Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?’

‘They descend upon every sinful liar.’”

And the other said, when he was told that

---

## Page 5584

al-Mukhtār claimed to receive revelation, he replied, “Allah Most High says:

‘Indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you.’”

The spirit from which the author of al-Futūhāt claims to have received that book is one of these satanic spirits. Thus, he describes various forms of seclusion involving particular foods and other specified things. Such practices open the way for those who undertake them to communicate with the jinn and devils. They imagine this to be among the miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s righteous servants, whereas it is nothing but satanic states. I know a number of these people. Some would be carried through the air to distant places and brought back. Others would receive stolen property, which the devils stole and brought to them. Others would be shown where stolen property was, in return for a fee they received from people or a gift people gave them when they directed them to their stolen possessions, and similar things.

Since these people’s states were satanic, they opposed the messengers—may Allah Most High bless them and grant them peace—as can be seen in the writings of the author of al-Futūhāt al-Makkiyya and al-Fusūs, and similar works. He praises disbelievers such as the peoples of Noah and Hūd, Pharaoh, and others, while disparaging prophets such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Aaron. He censures Muslim shaykhs whom Muslims hold in esteem, such as al-Junayd ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Abd Allāh al-Tustarī, while praising those whom Muslims condemn, such as al-Hallāj and others like him, as he recounts in his imaginary, satanic visions. Al-Junayd—may Allah sanctify his soul—was indeed one of the leading guides to the truth. He was asked about Allah’s oneness

---

## Page 5585

and he replied: “Affirming Allah’s oneness means distinguishing what has a beginning from what is eternal.” He thus explained that affirming Allah’s oneness means distinguishing the Eternal from what has been brought into being, and the Creator from creation. The author of al-Fusūs rejected this, saying in his imaginary, satanic conversation with him: “O Junayd, can anyone distinguish what has been brought into being from the Eternal unless he is other than both?”

He therefore declared al-Junayd mistaken for saying, “Distinguishing what has a beginning from what is eternal,” because his own position is that the existence of what has been brought into being is identical with the existence of the Eternal. As he says in his Fusūs:

“Among His Most Beautiful Names is ‘the Most High.’ Above whom, when none exists but He? And beyond what, when there is nothing but He? His exaltedness is therefore in relation to Himself, and He is the very reality of all existing things. Thus, those called originated things are exalted by virtue of His essence and are none other than He.”

He goes on to say:

“He is the very reality of what is hidden and the very reality of what is manifest. There is none who sees Him but He, and none who speaks of Him but He. He is the one called Abū Sa‘īd al-Kharrāz and by other names that have come into being.”

This heretic should be told: Someone who distinguishes between two things in knowledge and speech need not be a third entity, other than both. Every person distinguishes between himself and others without being a third entity. The servant knows that he is a servant and distinguishes between himself and his Creator. The Creator—exalted is His majesty—distinguishes between Himself and His creatures and knows that He is their Lord and that they are His servants, as the Quran declares in numerous places. Appealing to the Quran as evidence is appropriate when addressing believers who acknowledge it inwardly and outwardly. But as for these

---

## Page 5586

heretics, they make the same claims as al-Tilimsānī, one of their number and the most adept exponent of their monism. When al-Fusūs was read to him, he was told, “The Quran contradicts your Fusūs.”

He replied, “The entire Quran is polytheism; only our teachings affirm Allah’s oneness.”

He was asked, “If existence is one, why is a wife lawful and a sister forbidden?”

He replied, “To us, all is lawful. But these veiled people said, ‘It is forbidden,’ so we said, ‘It is forbidden to you.’”

Besides its enormous unbelief, this is plainly self-contradictory. If existence is one, who is veiled, and who imposes the veil?

Thus, one of their shaykhs said to his disciple, “Whoever tells you that anything other than Allah exists in the universe has lied.”

His disciple replied, “Then who is it that lies?”

They told another person, “These are loci of manifestation.”

He asked them, “Are the loci of manifestation other than that which is manifest, or are they identical? If they are other, you have affirmed a relation; if they are identical, there is no distinction.”

Elsewhere, we have discussed at length the exposure of these people’s secrets and explained the true nature of each one’s position. We explained that the author of al-Fusūs holds that the nonexistent is a thing and that the existence of the Real governs it. He thus distinguishes between existence and subsistence.

The Mu‘tazilites who said that the nonexistent is a thing subsisting outside the mind, despite their misguidance, are better than he is. They said that the Lord created, for these things subsisting in nonexistence, an existence distinct from His own. This man, however, claimed that the Lord’s very existence emanated upon it, so there is no

---

## Page 5587

created existence distinct from the Creator’s existence, in his view. His companion, al-Sadr al-Qūnawī, distinguishes between the absolute and the particular. Being closer to philosophy, he did not acknowledge that the nonexistent is a thing; instead, he identified the Real with absolute existence and composed Miftāh ghayb al-jamʿ wa-l-wujūd.

This position goes even further in negating the Creator and His existence. For the absolute, conditioned by absoluteness—the intellectual universal—exists only in minds, not in concrete reality. As for the absolute without any condition—the natural universal—even if it is said to exist externally, it exists externally only as a particular. According to those who affirm its external existence, it is part of that particular. It therefore follows that the Lord’s existence either has no external reality, is part of the existence of created beings, or is identical with their existence. Does a part create the whole, or does a thing create itself? Does nonexistence create existence? Or can part of a thing be the creator of the whole?

These people avoid the term “indwelling,” because it entails something that indwells and a locus in which it dwells. They also avoid the term “union,” because it entails two things, one uniting with the other, whereas, according to them, existence is one.

They say: “The Christians became unbelievers only because they singled out the Messiah as being Allah. Had they extended this to all, they would not have become unbelievers.”

Likewise, they say of idolaters: “They erred only because they worshipped some

---

## Page 5588

manifestations rather than others; had they worshipped them all, they would not have erred”—according to them. In their view, the fully realized gnostic is not harmed by worshipping idols.

Besides the grave unbelief it contains, this position involves an inescapable contradiction, for they may be asked: “Who, then, is mistaken?” Yet they say: “The Lord is characterized by all the imperfections that characterize created beings.” They also say: “Created beings are characterized by all the perfections that characterize the Creator.” They repeat what the author of al-Fusūs said:

“The One who is exalted in Himself is He whose perfection encompasses all attributes of existence and relations of nonexistence, whether praiseworthy according to custom, reason, or religious law, or blameworthy according to custom, reason, and religious law. This belongs exclusively to the One named Allah.”

Despite this unbelief, they cannot escape contradiction, for it is known through sense perception and reason that this thing is not that thing. These people repeat what al-Tilimsānī used to say: “Through unveiling, we have established what contradicts clear reason.” They also say: “Whoever seeks realization”—meaning their realization—“must abandon reason and religious law.”

I have said to those among them whom I addressed: “It is well known that the unveiling granted to the prophets is greater and more complete than that granted to anyone else, and that their reports are more truthful than anyone else’s. The prophets—may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon them—report things that people’s minds are incapable of knowing, not things that

---

## Page 5589

people know through reason to be impossible. They report matters that bewilder the mind, not matters that reason deems impossible. Nothing reported by the Messenger can contradict sound reason, nor can two conclusive proofs contradict one another, whether both are rational, both are scriptural, or one is rational and the other scriptural. What, then, of someone who claims an unveiling that contradicts the plain teachings of revelation and sound reason?”

These people may not deliberately lie. Rather, they imagine things that exist within their own minds and suppose that they exist externally. They also see things that do exist externally, but suppose them to be miraculous gifts granted to the righteous, when they are actually deceptions wrought by devils.

These advocates of oneness may place the saints above the prophets and maintain that prophethood has not ceased, as is reported of Ibn Sab‘īn and others. They posit “three” levels, saying: “The servant first witnesses obedience and disobedience, then obedience without disobedience, then neither obedience nor disobedience.”

The “first witnessing” is the correct one: distinguishing between acts of obedience and acts of disobedience. By the “second witnessing,” however, they mean witnessing divine decree. Thus, one of them says: “I disbelieve in a Lord who is disobeyed.” This person claims that disobedience means opposing the divine will—that is, what Allah wills to occur. All created beings are subject to the rule of this will. Their poet says:

---

## Page 5590

“I have become subject to whatever You choose for me;
thus all my deeds are acts of obedience.”

It is well known that this contradicts what Allah sent His messengers with and revealed in His Books. For the disobedience that makes a person deserving of blame and punishment consists in opposing the command of Allah and His Messenger. As the Exalted says:

“These are the limits set by Allah. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, to remain there forever. That is the great triumph.”

“And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him into a Fire, to remain there forever, and he will have a humiliating punishment.”

We shall explain the difference between the universal will and the religious will, and between the universal command and the religious command. This “question” had confused a group of Sufis, so al-Junayd—may Allah have mercy on him—clarified it for them. Whoever followed al-Junayd in this was on the right course, while whoever opposed him went astray. They had been discussing how all things occur through Allah’s will and power, and the witnessing of this oneness, which they call the “first unification.” Al-Junayd explained to them that one must also witness the “second distinction”: while witnessing that all things share in being subject to Allah’s will, power, and creation, one must distinguish between what He commands, loves, and is pleased with, and what He forbids, dislikes, and is displeased with. One must also distinguish between His allies and His enemies. As the Exalted says:

“Shall We then treat those who submit to Allah like the criminals?”

“What is the matter with you? How do you judge?”

And the Exalted says:

“Or shall We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like those who spread corruption on earth? Or shall We treat the righteous like the wicked?”

And the Exalted says: “Or

---

## Page 5591

do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their life and death? How evil is their judgment!”

And the Exalted says:

“The blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds equal to those who do evil. How little you take heed!”

Thus, the position of the early generations of this community and its leading scholars was that Allah is the Creator, Lord, and Sovereign of everything. Whatever He wills occurs, and whatever He does not will does not occur. There is no Lord besides Him. Nevertheless, He commands obedience and forbids disobedience. He does not love corruption, does not approve of disbelief for His servants, and does not command indecency. Although it occurs by His will, He neither loves nor approves of it; rather, He hates it, censures those who commit it, and punishes them.

As for the “third rank”—in which one witnesses neither obedience nor disobedience—a person at this rank regards existence as one. They consider this the ultimate realization and friendship with Allah. In reality, however, it is the utmost deviation concerning Allah’s names and signs, and the utmost enmity towards Allah. For whoever adopts this perspective takes Jews, Christians, and all other disbelievers as allies, whereas the Exalted has said:

“Whoever among you takes them as allies is indeed one of them.”

He does not disavow polytheism and idols, and thus departs from the religion of Abraham, Allah’s intimate friend—may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon him. Allah the Exalted says:

“You have an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, ‘We disown you and whatever you worship besides Allah. We reject you, and enmity and hatred have arisen between us and you forever, until you believe in Allah alone.’”

And Allah’s intimate friend said—upon him

---

## Page 5592

be peace—to his polytheistic people:

“Have you considered what you have been worshipping,
you and your forefathers?
They are enemies to me, except the Lord of all worlds.”

The Exalted also says:

“You will not find people who believe in Allah and the Last Day showing affection to those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their kindred. Those are the ones in whose hearts He has inscribed faith and whom He has strengthened with a spirit from Him.”

Some of these people have written books and poems expounding their doctrine, such as Ibn al-Fārid’s poem entitled Nazm al-Sulūk (The Spiritual Path in Verse), in which he says:

to his own reality, in union, with every prostration.

And other words of this kind. For this reason, when the author of these words was dying, he recited the following verses:
