## Page 5593

“If what I have suffered reflects my standing with you in love,
then I have squandered my days.

For he used to think that he was Allah. But when Allah’s angels came to take his soul, the falsity of what he had believed became clear to him. Allah Most High says:

“Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.”

Everything in the heavens and the earth therefore glorifies Allah; it is not Allah. Then the Most High says:

“To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things.”

“He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He has knowledge of all things.”

It is reported in Sahīh Muslim that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say in his supplication:

“O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the mighty Throne, our Lord and the Lord of all things, Splitter of grain and fruit stones, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Quran! I seek refuge in You from the evil of every creature whose forelock You hold. You are the First, and nothing is before You; You are the Last, and nothing is after You; You are the Manifest, and nothing is above You; You are the Hidden, and nothing is nearer than You. Settle my debt for me and free me from poverty.”

Then He says:

“He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then rose over the Throne. He knows what enters the earth and what emerges from it, what descends from heaven and what ascends into it. He is with you wherever you are, and Allah sees all that you do.”

---

## Page 5594

Thus He stated that the heavens and the earth—and, elsewhere, “whatever is between them”—are created and glorify Him. He, glory be to Him, also declared that He knows everything. As for His words, “He is with you,” the word “with” does not, in Arabic, imply that one of two things is intermingled with the other. For example, the Most High says:

“Fear Allah and be with the truthful.”

And the Most High says:

“Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are firm against the disbelievers.”

And the Most High says:

“And those who believed afterwards, emigrated, and strove alongside you—they are of you.”

The word “with” occurs in the Quran in both a general and a specific sense. The general sense appears in this verse and in the verse of Sūrat al-Mujādilah:

“Do you not see that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? No three converse in secret without Him being their fourth, nor five without Him being their sixth, nor fewer than that nor more without Him being with them wherever they may be. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, He will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah has knowledge of all things.”

He began the passage with knowledge and ended it with knowledge. Hence Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Dahhāk, Sufyān al-Thawrī, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: He is with them through His knowledge.

As for His being with particular people in a specific sense, this appears in the words of the Most High:

“Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who do good.”

And in His words to Moses:

“Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see.”

And the Most High says:

“When he said to his companion, ‘Do not grieve; indeed, Allah is with us.’”

This refers to the Prophet

---

## Page 5595

—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—and Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. Thus, He is with Moses and Aaron, but not Pharaoh; with Muhammad and his companion, but not Abū Jahl and His other enemies; and with those who fear Him and those who do good, but not the unjust aggressors. If “being with” meant that He Himself is everywhere, the specific and general statements would contradict one another. Rather, it means that He is with these people through His help and support, but not with those others.

As for the words of the Most High:

“It is He who is God in heaven and God on earth,”

they mean that He is the God of those in the heavens and those on earth, as Allah Most High says:

“To Him belongs the highest description in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.”

Likewise, His words:

“And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth,”

mean that He is the One worshipped in the heavens and on earth, as explained by the leading scholars, including Imam Ahmad and others.

The early generations of the Muslim community and its leading scholars unanimously agreed that the Lord Most High is distinct from His creation. He is described as He described Himself and as His Messenger—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—described Him, without distorting or denying His attributes, specifying how they are, or likening them to those of creation. He is described with attributes of perfection, not attributes of deficiency, and it is known that nothing is like Him in His attributes of perfection. As Allah Most High says:

“Say, ‘He is Allah, the One;
Allah, the Eternal Refuge.
He neither begets nor is born,
and there is none comparable to Him.’”

Ibn ‘Abbās said: “Al-Samad is the All-Knowing, whose knowledge is perfect; the Magnificent, whose magnificence is perfect; the All-Powerful, whose power is perfect; the All-Wise, whose wisdom is perfect; the Master, whose mastery is perfect.

---

## Page 5596

And Ibn Mas‘ūd and others said: “He is the One who has no hollow interior.” Al-Ahad (the One) is He who has no equal. His name al-Samad affirms that He possesses the attributes of perfection and is free of all deficiencies, while His name al-Ahad affirms that nothing is like Him. We have discussed this at length in our commentary on this surah and our explanation of how it equals one-third of the Quran.

Section

Many people confuse the realities pertaining to divine command, religion, and faith with those pertaining to creation, divine decree, and the cosmic order. For creation and command belong to Allah, glorified and exalted is He, as He Most High says:

“Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then rose over the Throne. He brings the night as a covering over the day, pursuing it swiftly. The sun, the moon, and the stars are subject to His command. Surely, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of all worlds.”

He, glorified is He, is the Creator, Lord, and Sovereign of everything. There is no creator besides Him and no lord other than Him. Whatever He wills comes to pass, and whatever He does not will does not come to pass. Every movement and every state of rest in existence occurs through His decree, ordainment, will, power, and creation.

He, glorified is He, has commanded obedience to Himself and His messengers and forbidden disobedience to Himself and His messengers. He has commanded that He alone be worshipped and that worship be devoted sincerely to Him, and He has forbidden associating partners with Allah. Thus, the greatest of good deeds is

---

## Page 5597

worshipping Allah alone, and the greatest evil is associating partners with Him.

Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives anything less than that for whom He wills.”

He Most High also says:

“Among people are those who take others besides Allah as equals, loving them as they love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah.”

In the two Sahīh collections, Ibn Mas‘ūd, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

“I said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?’ He said, ‘To set up a rival to Allah when He is the One who created you.’ I asked, ‘Then which?’ He said, ‘To kill your child for fear that he will share your food.’ I asked, ‘Then which?’ He said, ‘To commit adultery with your neighbour’s wife.’ Allah then revealed in confirmation of this:

‘And those who do not invoke another god besides Allah, nor kill a soul whom Allah has forbidden to be killed, except by right, nor commit adultery. Whoever does so will face a penalty. The punishment will be multiplied for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will remain in it forever, humiliated—except those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds. For them Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And Allah is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.’”

He, glorified is He, has commanded justice, excellence in doing good, and giving to relatives, and has forbidden indecency, wrongdoing, and oppression. He has declared that He loves those who fear Him, those who do good, those who act justly, those who repeatedly repent, those who purify themselves, and those who fight in His cause in ranks as though they were a firmly joined structure.

He detests what He has forbidden, as He says in Surah Subhān:

“The evil of all these things is detested by your Lord.”

He has forbidden associating partners with Him and mistreating parents, and has commanded that relatives be given their due rights

---

## Page 5598

and has forbidden squandering and stinginess, keeping one’s hand shackled to one’s neck, and stretching it out without restraint. He has forbidden killing a soul without right, adultery, and approaching an orphan’s property except in the best manner, until He says:

“The evil of all these things is detested by your Lord.”

He, glorified is He, does not love corruption, nor does He approve of disbelief for His servants.

The servant is commanded to turn continually to Allah Most High in repentance. Allah Most High says:

“Turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, so that you may succeed.”

In Sahīh al-Bukhārī, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is reported to have said:

“O people, turn to your Lord in repentance. By Him in whose hand is my soul, I seek Allah’s forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance more than seventy times a day.”

In Sahīh Muslim, he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is reported to have said:

In the Sunan collections, Ibn ‘Umar said:

Allah, glorified is He, has commanded His servants to conclude their righteous deeds by seeking forgiveness. Thus, when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had pronounced the salutation ending the prayer, he would seek forgiveness three times and say:

“O Allah, You are Peace, and from You comes peace. Blessed are You, Possessor of majesty and honour.”

## Page 5599

as is established in an authentic hadith from him. Allah Most High has said:

“And to the three who were left behind, until the earth, despite its vastness, became confining to them, and their own souls became a burden to them, and they knew that there was no refuge from Allah except in Him. ## Page 5600

say when bowing and prostrating:

In the two Sahīh collections, Abū Bakr al-Siddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “O Messenger of Allah, teach me a supplication to recite in my prayer.” He replied:

In the Sunan collections, Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “O Messenger of Allah, teach me a supplication to recite in the morning and evening.” He replied:

No one, then, should imagine that they have no need to repent to Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins. Rather, everyone constantly needs this.

## Page 5601

man. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.”

“So that Allah may punish the hypocrites, men and women, and the polytheists, men and women, and turn in mercy to the believers, men and women. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

Man is unjust and ignorant, and the highest attainment of believing men and women is repentance. Allah Most High has told us in His Book of the repentance of His righteous servants and His forgiveness of them.

It is authentically reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“No one will enter Paradise by his deeds.” They asked, “Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?” He replied, “Not even me, unless Allah envelops me in mercy and bounty from Him.”

This does not contradict His words:

“Eat and drink with pleasure for what you did in days gone by.”

For the Messenger negated the sense of exchange and equivalence conveyed by the preposition bi (“by”), whereas the Quran affirmed its causal sense.

As for the saying, “When Allah loves a servant, sins do not harm him,” it means that when Allah loves a servant, He inspires him to repent and seek forgiveness, so that he does not persist in sin. Whoever thinks that sins do not harm someone who persists in them is misguided, opposing the Book, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the early generations and the imams. Rather, whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. His praiseworthy servants are none other than those mentioned in His words, Most High:

“And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing.”

“Those who spend in prosperity and adversity, restrain their anger, and pardon others—and Allah loves those who do good.”

“And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves,

---

## Page 5602

remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins—and who forgives sins except Allah?—and do not knowingly persist in what they have done.”

Whoever thinks that “divine decree” is an excuse for sinners is like the polytheists of whom Allah Most High said:

“Those who associate partners with Allah will say, ‘Had Allah willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have associated partners with Him, nor would we have forbidden anything.’”

Allah Most High said in reply to them:

“Likewise, those before them denied the truth until they tasted Our punishment. Say, ‘Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? You follow nothing but conjecture, and you do nothing but guess.’”

“Say, ‘To Allah belongs the conclusive argument. Had He willed, He would have guided you all.’”

If “divine decree” were an excuse for anyone, Allah would not have punished those who rejected the messengers, such as the people of Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, the overturned cities, and the people of Pharaoh. Nor would He have commanded that the prescribed punishments be carried out upon transgressors. No one invokes divine decree as an excuse unless he is following his desires without guidance from Allah.

Whoever regards divine decree as an excuse that absolves sinners of blame and punishment must neither blame nor punish anyone who wrongs him. Rather, he must regard whatever brings pleasure and whatever brings pain as equal, making no distinction between someone who treats him well and someone who treats him badly. Human nature, reason, and divine law all rule this out.

Allah Most High has said:

“Should We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like those who spread corruption on earth? Or should We treat the God-fearing like the wicked?”

And He Most High said:

“Should We then treat the Muslims like the criminals?”

And He Most High said:

“Or do those who

---

## Page 5603

commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their life and death? How evil is their judgment!”

And He Most High said:

“Did you think that We created you without purpose, and that you would not be returned to Us?”

And He Most High said:

“Does man think that he will be left without responsibility?”

That is, left unattended, neither commanded nor forbidden.

It is established in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Adam and Moses disputed. Moses said, ‘O Adam, you are the father of mankind. Allah created you with His Hand, breathed into you of His spirit, and made His angels prostrate before you. Why did you cause us and yourself to be expelled from Paradise?’

“Adam replied, ‘You are Moses, whom Allah chose to speak to, and for whom He wrote the Torah with His Hand. How long before I was created did you find it written against me: “Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray”?’

“He replied, ‘Forty years.’

“Adam said, ‘Then why do you blame me for something Allah decreed for me forty years before I was created?’”

He said: “Thus Adam prevailed over Moses in argument.” That is, he defeated him by his argument.

Two groups have gone astray concerning this hadith. One group rejected it because they thought it entailed absolving those who disobey Allah of blame and punishment on account of divine decree. Another group, worse than the first, took it as an argument in their favor. They may even say: “Divine decree

---

## Page 5604

is a justification for the people of spiritual reality (ahl al-haqīqah) who have witnessed it, or for those who do not regard themselves as acting.”

Some have said that Adam prevailed over Moses in argument only because he was his father, because he had repented, because the sin occurred under one revealed law while the blame was expressed under another, or because this applies in this world but not in the Hereafter. All of this is false.

Rather, the meaning of the hadith is that Moses, peace be upon him, blamed his father only for the calamity that had befallen them because he ate from the tree. He said to him, “Why did you cause us and yourself to be expelled from Paradise?” He did not blame him merely for having committed a sin and then repented of it. Moses knew that someone who repents of a sin is not to be blamed, and he too had repented. Had Adam believed that divine decree absolved him of blame, he would not have said:

“Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers.”

The believer is commanded to be patient and submit when calamities strike, and to seek forgiveness and repent when he sins. Allah Most High said:

“So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true. And seek forgiveness for your sin.”

Thus, He commanded him to endure calamities patiently and seek forgiveness for his faults.

And He Most High said:

“No calamity befalls except by Allah’s permission. And whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart.”

Ibn Masʿūd said: “This is a man whom calamity strikes, who knows that it is from Allah, and so is content and submits.”

When believers suffer a calamity such as illness, poverty, or humiliation, they patiently endure Allah’s decree, even if it results from someone else’s sin. For example, if a father spends his wealth on sinful acts and his children become poor as a result, they must patiently endure what

---

## Page 5605

has befallen them. If they blame their father because of how they themselves have been affected, he reminds them of divine decree.

“Patience” is obligatory by scholarly consensus. Higher than this is contentment with Allah’s decree. Some have held that “contentment” is obligatory, while others have held that it is recommended, which is the correct view. Higher still is to thank Allah for the calamity, recognizing His favor in making it a means of expiating one’s sins, raising one’s rank, turning back to Him, humbly beseeching Him, and sincerely placing one’s trust and hope in Him rather than in created beings.

As for people of transgression and misguidance, you find them invoking divine decree as an excuse when they sin and follow their desires, yet attributing good deeds to themselves when Allah blesses them with them. As some scholars have said: “When you obey, you are a Qadarī; when you sin, a Jabrī. Whatever doctrine suits your desires, you adopt.”

When people of guidance and sound judgment perform a good deed, they recognize Allah’s favor upon them in it: He is the One who blessed them, made them Muslims, enabled them to establish prayer, and inspired them with piety. They recognize that there is neither might nor power except through Him. Through this recognition of divine decree, they are freed from self-admiration, reproachful reminders of their favors, and hurtful conduct. When they commit a sin, they seek Allah’s forgiveness and repent to Him for it.

In Sahīh al-Bukhārī, Shaddād ibn Aws reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The best supplication for forgiveness is for the servant to say: ‘O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me, and I am Your servant. I remain faithful to Your covenant and promise as best I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favor upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me

---

## Page 5606

for none forgives sins but You.’ Whoever says this in the morning with firm conviction in it, then dies that night, will enter Paradise.”

In an authentic hadith, Abū Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, narrated from his Lord, Blessed and Exalted, that He said:

“O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another. O My servants, you sin by night and by day, and I forgive all sins and do not mind doing so. So seek My forgiveness, and I will forgive you.

“O My servants, all of you are hungry except those whom I feed. So ask Me for food, and I will feed you. O My servants, all of you are naked except those whom I clothe. So ask Me for clothing, and I will clothe you. O My servants, all of you are astray except those whom I guide. So seek My guidance, and I will guide you.

“O My servants, you will never be able to harm Me, nor will you ever be able to benefit Me. O My servants, if the first and last of you, humans and jinn alike, were all as pious at heart as the most pious person among you, that would add nothing to My dominion. O My servants, if the first and last of you, humans and jinn alike, were all as wicked at heart as the most wicked person among you, that would diminish My dominion in no way.

“O My servants, if the first and last of you, humans and jinn alike, gathered on a single plain and asked of Me, and I gave each person what he asked for, that would diminish what I possess no more than a single dip of a needle diminishes the sea.

---

## Page 5607

Thus He, glorified be He, commands the servant to praise Allah for whatever good he finds, and to blame no one but himself if he finds evil.

Many people speak in the language of “reality” without distinguishing between the reality of creation and divine decree, which concerns His creation and will, and the reality of religion and divine command, which concerns His pleasure and love. Nor do they distinguish between someone who adheres to religious reality in accordance with what Allah commanded through His messengers, and someone who follows his own spiritual experience and inward perception without assessing them against the Quran and Sunnah.

Likewise, many people use the term “Sharia” without distinguishing between the law revealed by Allah Most High—the Quran and Sunnah with which Allah sent His Messenger—and the law embodied in a judge’s ruling. No created being is permitted to depart from the revealed law, and none departs from it except a disbeliever. A judge, however, sometimes rules correctly and sometimes errs.

This is when he is knowledgeable and just. Otherwise, it is reported in the Sunan collections that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“There are three kinds of judges: two are in the Fire and one is in Paradise. A man who knows the truth and judges accordingly is in Paradise. A man who judges people’s cases in ignorance is in the Fire. And a man who knows the truth but rules contrary to it is in the Fire.”

The finest of all knowledgeable and just judges is the foremost of Adam’s descendants, Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. It is authentically reported from him in the two Sahīh collections that he said:

“You bring your disputes before me, and some of you may present their arguments more eloquently than others. I judge only on the basis of what I hear. So whoever

---

## Page 5608

is awarded by me anything that rightfully belongs to his brother must not take it, for I am only assigning him a piece of the Fire.”

Thus, the foremost of creation explained that if he gives a judgment based on what he has heard, while the actual facts are otherwise, the person in whose favour he rules may not take what he has been awarded: he is only assigning him a piece of the Fire. The scholars agree on this concerning cases of outright ownership. If a judge rules on the basis of what he considers legally valid proof, such as witness testimony or an admission, while the actual facts differ from what appears outwardly, the person in whose favour he rules may not take what he has been awarded, by scholarly agreement. If he rules on contracts and annulments on a similar basis, most scholars hold that the same applies. This is the position of Mālik, al-Shāfi‘ī and Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Abū Hanīfa, may Allah be pleased with him, distinguished between the two categories.

Thus, when the terms “religious law” and “Sharia” mean the Quran and Sunnah, neither any of Allah’s allies nor anyone else may depart from them. Whoever thinks that any of Allah’s allies has a path to Allah other than following Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, inwardly and outwardly, and does not follow him inwardly and outwardly, is a disbeliever.

Whoever invokes the account of Moses and al-Khidr to support this is mistaken on two counts.

The first is that Moses was not sent to al-Khidr, nor was al-Khidr obliged to follow him, for Moses was sent to the Children of Israel. As for Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his message encompasses both kinds of accountable beings, jinn and humans; and even if

---

## Page 5609

those superior to al-Khidr—such as Abraham, Moses and Jesus—had lived to see him, they would have been obliged to follow him. How much more so al-Khidr, whether he was a prophet or an ally of Allah! This is why al-Khidr said to Moses:

“There is knowledge from Allah that He has taught me which you do not know, and there is knowledge from Allah that He has taught you which I do not know.”

None of the jinn or humans whom the message of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has reached may say anything like this.

The second is that what al-Khidr did did not contravene the religious law of Moses, peace be upon him. Moses did not know the circumstances that made those actions permissible; once al-Khidr explained them to him, he agreed with him. Making a hole in the ship and then repairing it, for the benefit of its owners and out of fear that the oppressor would seize it, was an act of kindness towards them, and that is permissible. Killing an assailant is permissible, even if he is a minor. Someone who cannot be prevented from leading his parents into disbelief except by being killed may be killed.

When Najda al-Harūrī asked Ibn ‘Abbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, about killing boys, he told him: “If you know about them what al-Khidr knew about that boy, then kill them; otherwise, do not kill them.” Reported by al-Bukhārī.

As for showing kindness to an orphan without compensation and patiently enduring hunger, these are righteous deeds. Thus, none of this contravened Allah’s religious law.

When, however, “religious law” means a judge’s ruling, that ruling may be unjust or just, correct or mistaken. “Religious law” may also mean the opinions of the leading jurists, such as Abū Hanīfa, al-Thawrī, Mālik ibn Anas, al-Awzā‘ī and al-Layth ibn

---

## Page 5610

Sa‘d, al-Shāfi‘ī, Ahmad, Ishāq, Dāwūd and others. Their opinions must be supported by evidence from the Quran and Sunnah. Following another’s opinion on his authority is permissible where doing so is allowed. That is, following any one of them is not obligatory upon the entire Muslim community as following the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is obligatory. Nor is following any one of them on his authority forbidden, as following someone who speaks without knowledge is forbidden.

If, however, someone adds to the religious law something that does not belong to it, such as fabricated hadiths, or interprets the texts contrary to Allah’s intent, or does anything similar, this constitutes alteration. One must therefore distinguish between revealed religious law, interpreted religious law and altered religious law, just as one distinguishes between the reality of the created order and the religious reality pertaining to divine commands, and between what is substantiated by the Quran and Sunnah and what relies solely on an individual’s spiritual experience and ecstasy.

Section

In His Book, Allah has distinguished, with regard to “will,” “command,” “decree,” “permission,” “prohibition,” “raising up,” “sending,” “speech” and “making,” between what pertains to the created order—which He creates, determines and decrees, even though He has not commanded it, does not love it, does not reward those who do it and does not make them His pious allies—and what pertains to religion, which He commands and prescribes, for which He rewards people, honours them and makes them His pious allies

---

## Page 5611

and members of His successful party and His victorious army. This is among the greatest distinctions by which Allah’s allies are distinguished from His enemies. Whoever the Lord, glorified and exalted is He, employs in what He loves and is pleased with, and who dies in that state, is among His allies. Whoever devotes his deeds to what the Lord hates and dislikes, and dies in that state, is among His enemies.

Thus, the “will pertaining to the created order” is His will concerning all that He creates. All created things fall within His will pertaining to the created order. His will pertaining to religion, however, entails His love and pleasure and encompasses what He has commanded and established as religious law and religion. This is confined to faith and righteous deeds. Allah Most High says:

“Whoever Allah wills to guide, He opens his heart to Islam; and whoever He wills to lead astray, He makes his heart tight and constricted, as though he were climbing into the sky.”

Noah, peace be upon him, said to his people:

“My advice will not benefit you, even if I wish to advise you, if Allah wills to lead you astray.”

Allah Most High says:

“When Allah wills harm for a people, none can avert it, and they have no protector besides Him.”

Concerning the second kind of will, Allah Most High says:

“Whoever is ill or on a journey must fast an equal number of other days. Allah intends ease for you and does not intend hardship for you.”

He says in the verse concerning purification:

“Allah does not intend to impose hardship upon you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favour upon you, so that you may be grateful.”

After mentioning which marriages He has permitted and which He has forbidden, He says:

“Allah intends to make things clear to you, guide you to the ways of those before you, and accept your repentance. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.”

“Allah intends to accept your repentance, but those who follow their desires wish you to deviate far from the right path.”

“Allah intends to lighten your burden, for mankind was created weak.”

After mentioning what He commanded the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to do and what He forbade them, He says:

The meaning is that He has commanded you, O members of the household, to do what removes impurity from you and purifies you completely. Whoever obeys His command is purified and has impurity removed from him, unlike whoever disobeys Him.

As for “command,” He says concerning the command pertaining to the created order:

Allah Most High also says:

“Indeed, Allah commands you to return trusts to their rightful owners and, when you judge between people, to judge with justice. Excellent indeed is what Allah admonishes you to do. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.”

As for “permission,” He says concerning permission pertaining to the created order, when mentioning magic:

Allah Most High also says:

“We have sent no messenger except to be obeyed

by Allah’s permission.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by Allah’s permission.”

As for “decree,” He says concerning the decree pertaining to the created order:

He, glorified be He, also says:

“When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.”

Concerning the decree pertaining to religion, He says:

That is, He has commanded this. It does not mean that He has predestined it, for others besides Him have indeed been worshipped, as He has stated in several places. For example, Allah Most High says:

It is established in an authentic report that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say:

“I seek refuge in all of Allah’s perfect words from the evil of what He has created, from His wrath and punishment, from the evil of His servants, and from the promptings of the devils and their coming into my presence.”

He also said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Whoever stops at a place and says, ‘I seek refuge in Allah’s perfect words from the evil of what He has created,’ nothing will harm him until he leaves that place.”

He used to say:

“I seek refuge in Allah’s perfect words, beyond which neither the righteous nor the wicked can pass, from the evil of what He has created in the earth, from the evil of what emerges from it, from the evil of the trials of night and day, and from the evil of everyone who comes by night, except one who comes with good, O

---

## Page 5616

Most Merciful.”

“Allah’s perfect words, beyond which neither the righteous nor the wicked can pass” are those by which He brought all things into being. Neither the righteous nor the wicked can escape His creative act, His will, or His power. As for His “words pertaining to religion”—His revealed Books and the commands and prohibitions they contain—the righteous obey them, while the wicked disobey them. Allah’s pious allies are those who obey His words, His ordaining, His permission, and His will in matters of religion.

As for His words pertaining to the created order, beyond which neither the righteous nor the wicked can pass, all creation falls under them, including Iblīs and his hosts, all disbelievers, and everyone else who enters the Fire. Although all creatures are alike in being encompassed by His creation, will, power, and decree, they differ with respect to His commands and prohibitions, His love, pleasure, and anger.

Allah’s pious allies are those who do what is commanded, refrain from what is forbidden, and patiently endure what is decreed. He loves them and they love Him; He is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. His enemies, the allies of the devils, although subject to His power, are those whom He hates, with whom He is angry, whom He curses, and to whom He is an enemy.

A detailed explanation of these points belongs elsewhere. I have written here only to draw attention to the principal aspects of “the distinction between the allies of the Most Merciful and the allies of Satan.” The essential distinction between the two lies in

Allah Most High also says:

“So I swear by those that recede, that run their courses and retreat to cover.”

This means the stars that remain concealed in the sky before they rise. When they appear, people see them moving across the sky; when they set, they withdraw to their hiding place, which conceals them.

“And by the night as it retreats”—that is, when it departs and dawn approaches—“and by the dawn

---

## Page 5619

as it breathes”—that is, as it arrives.

“Indeed, this is the word of a noble messenger”—namely Gabriel, peace be upon him—“possessed of strength, held in honor by the Lord of the Throne, obeyed there and trustworthy.” That is, he is obeyed in heaven and is trustworthy. Then He says:

“Your companion is not mad.”

That is, your companion whom Allah bestowed upon you as a blessing when He sent him to you as a messenger of your own kind, living among you, since you could not bear to see the angels. As Allah Most High says:

“They say, ‘Why has an angel not been sent down to him?’ Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been settled, and they would have been granted no respite. And had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man”—to the end of the verse.

Allah Most High also says:

“He certainly saw him on the clear horizon”—that is, he saw Gabriel, peace be upon him.

“Nor is he danīn concerning the unseen”—that is, accused. In the other reading, “danīn”—that is, miserly, concealing knowledge and imparting it only for payment, as those who withhold knowledge unless they receive compensation do.

“Nor is this the word of an accursed devil.”

Thus He declared Gabriel, peace be upon him, free of being a devil, just as He declared Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, free of being a poet or a soothsayer.

Allah’s God-fearing allies are therefore those who follow the example of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. They do what he commanded and refrain from what he forbade. They follow his example in those matters in which he instructed them to follow him. Allah supports them with His angels and a spirit from Him, and casts some of His light into their hearts. They receive the miraculous favors with which Allah honors His God-fearing allies. The miraculous favors granted to the best of Allah’s allies serve to establish a proof in religion or meet a need of the Muslims, just as the miracles of their Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, served these purposes.

---

## Page 5620

The miraculous favors granted to Allah’s allies come only through the blessing of following His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. They therefore fall, in reality, within the miracles of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. These include the splitting of the moon; the pebbles glorifying Allah in his palm; trees coming to him; the palm trunk yearning for him; his description of Jerusalem on the night of the Ascension; his accounts of past and future events; his bringing the mighty Book; and his multiplying food and drink on many occasions.

During the Battle of the Trench, for example, he fed the army to their fill from a pot of food without its contents diminishing, as related in the well-known hadith of Umm Salamah. During the expedition to Khaybar, he quenched the army’s thirst from a waterskin without its contents diminishing. In the year of Tabūk, he filled the army’s vessels from a small quantity of food without it diminishing, although they numbered some 30,000. Water flowed from between his fingers on several occasions, providing enough for everyone with him—as at al-Hudaybiyah, where they numbered some 1,400 or 1,500. He also restored Abū Qatādah’s eye after it had fallen onto his cheek, and it became the better of his two eyes.

[When he sent Muhammad ibn Maslamah to kill Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, Muhammad fell and broke his leg. The Prophet stroked it, and it healed.] (*)

He fed 130 men with roast meat, cutting off a piece for each of them and making two portions of it. They all ate from it, and some remained afterward. There was also the debt of thirty wasqs that ʿAbdullāh, Jābir’s father, owed to a Jewish man. Jābir said:

“He instructed the creditor to take all the dates in settlement of what was owed to him, but he refused. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then walked among the date palms and said to Jābir, ‘Harvest the dates for him.’ He paid him the thirty wasqs in full, and seventeen wasqs remained.”

There are many such examples. I have collected about a thousand miracles.

## Page 5621

The miraculous favors granted to the Companions, the Successors after them, and all other righteous people are exceedingly numerous.

For example, “Usayd ibn Hudayr” was reciting Sūrat al-Kahf when something like a canopy containing lamps descended from heaven. These were angels who had descended because of his recitation. Angels used to greet ʿImrān ibn Husayn. Salmān and Abū al-Dardāʾ were eating from a dish when the dish—or its contents—glorified Allah. ʿAbbād ibn Bishr and Usayd ibn Hudayr left the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a dark night, and a light like the tip of a whip shone for them. When they parted, the light divided, accompanying each of them. This was narrated by al-Bukhārī and others.

There is also the account of {al-Siddīq, recorded in the two Sahīh collections: he took three guests home with him, and whenever he ate a morsel, an even greater quantity grew beneath it. They ate their fill, and the food became more plentiful than it had been before. Abū Bakr and his wife looked at it and found that there was more than before. He took it to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Many people came to him, ate from it, and were satisfied}.

“Khubayb ibn ʿAdī” was held captive by the polytheists in Mecca—may Allah Most High honor it. Grapes would be brought to him to eat, although there was not a single grape in Mecca.

And “ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayrah: he was killed as a martyr, and they searched for his body but could not find it.

and when he was killed, he was lifted up, and ‘Āmir ibn al-Tufayl saw him being raised. ‘Urwah said: “They believe that the angels lifted him up.”

“Khālid ibn al-Walīd” besieged a strongly fortified fortress. Its people said, “We will not submit until you drink

poison.” He drank it, and it did him no harm.

and his supplications would be answered. When they ran out of water, he prayed to Allah that they might have water to drink and perform ablution, and a supply for what lay ahead. A servant girl put poison in his food, but it did not harm him. A woman turned his wife against him, so he supplicated against her, and she became blind. She then came to him and repented, so he supplicated for her, and Allah restored her sight.

He supplicated Allah Most High to make ritual purification easy for him in winter, and water would be brought to him with steam rising from it. He also supplicated his Lord to protect his heart from Satan while he was praying, and Satan could gain no power over it.

to retrieve it, and found that the grave had been made spacious as far as the eye could see.

This is a vast subject, and the miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s close servants have been discussed at length elsewhere. As for the instances we know of concerning particular individuals, and those we know of in our own time, they are numerous.

## Page 5628

It should also be understood that miraculous gifts may be granted according to a person’s need. If someone whose faith is weak, or who is in need, requires them, he may receive what strengthens his faith and meets his need. Someone whose closeness to Allah is more complete may have no need of them, and so receive nothing of this kind because of his higher rank and his lack of need—not because of any deficiency in his closeness to Allah. For this reason, such occurrences were more frequent among the Successors than among the Companions. This differs from the case of those through whom extraordinary events occur to guide people and meet their needs: these people are of greater rank.

This is unlike satanic states, such as the case of ‘Abd Allāh ibn Sayyād, who appeared during the Prophet’s lifetime, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Some of the Companions thought that he was the Dajjāl. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, withheld judgment about him until it later became clear to him that he was not the Dajjāl. He was, however, one of the soothsayers. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him, “I have concealed something for you.” He replied, “Al-dukh, al-dukh (smoke, smoke).” He had concealed for him Surah al-Dukhān (Smoke). The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then said to him, “Begone! You will never exceed your station.”

He meant: you are merely one of the brethren of the soothsayers. A soothsayer would have a companion from among the devils who informed him of many unseen matters through what he overheard by stealth. They would mix truth with falsehood, as related in the authentic hadith narrated by al-Bukhārī and others, in which the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The angels descend into the clouds and mention a matter decreed in heaven. The devils listen by stealth and convey it to the soothsayers, who add a hundred lies of their own to it.”

---

## Page 5629

Muslim also narrated a hadith from Ibn ‘Abbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said:

“While the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was among a group of the Ansār, a shooting star was hurled, shining brightly. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked, ‘What would you say in the days of ignorance when you saw something like this?’ They replied, ‘We would say that a great man had died or a great man had been born.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘These are not hurled because of anyone’s death or birth. Rather, when our Lord, blessed and exalted is He, decrees a matter, the bearers of the Throne glorify Him. Then the inhabitants of the heaven nearest to them glorify Him, followed by those nearest to them, until the glorification reaches the inhabitants of this heaven. Then the inhabitants of the seventh heaven ask the bearers of the Throne, “What did our Lord say?” They tell them, and the inhabitants of each heaven in turn ask for the news, until it reaches the inhabitants of the lowest heaven. The devils snatch a hearing and are pelted, then pass what they heard on to their allies. Whatever they convey accurately is true, but they add to it.’”

In another narration, Ma‘mar said: “I asked al-Zuhrī, ‘Were they hurled in the days of ignorance?’ He replied, ‘Yes, but it intensified when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sent.’”

Al-Aswad al-‘Ansī, who claimed prophethood, had devils who informed him of certain unseen matters. When the Muslims fought him, they feared that the devils would tell him what they were saying about him. Eventually, his wife helped them against him after his disbelief became clear to her, and they killed him.

---

## Page 5630

Likewise, Musaylima the Liar had devils who informed him of unseen matters and helped him with certain things. There are many such people, including al-Hārith al-Dimashqī, who appeared in Syria during the reign of ‘Abd al-Malik ibn Marwān and claimed prophethood. Devils would free his feet from shackles and prevent weapons from piercing him, and a marble slab would glorify Allah when he stroked it with his hand. He would show people men and horsemen in the air, saying, “These are angels,” when in fact they were jinn. When the Muslims seized him to kill him, a man thrust a spear at him, but it did not pierce him. ‘Abd al-Malik said to the man, “You did not mention Allah’s name.” He then mentioned Allah’s name, thrust the spear at him, and killed him.

Similarly, those who experience satanic states find that their devils leave them when something that drives them away, such as the Throne Verse, is recited in their presence. This is established in the authentic hadith collection in the account of Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him:

“When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entrusted him with guarding the zakāt al-fitr alms, a devil stole from him night after night. Each time, he would seize him, but the devil would repent, so he would release him. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would ask him, ‘What did your captive do last night?’ He would reply, ‘He claimed that he would not return.’ The Prophet would say, ‘He has lied to you, and he will return.’ On the third occasion, the devil said, ‘Let me go, and I will teach you something that will benefit you: when you go to bed, recite the Throne Verse, “Allah—there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence,” to its end. A guardian from Allah will remain over you, and no devil will approach you until morning.’ When he informed the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said, ‘He has told you the truth

---

## Page 5631

though he is a habitual liar.’” He also told him that it was a devil.

Thus, when someone sincerely recites this verse in the presence of satanic states, it dispels them. This applies, for example, to someone who enters fire through a satanic state, or attends a gathering of whistling and clapping, where devils descend upon him and speak through his tongue in words whose meaning is unknown and which may be unintelligible. He may disclose what is in the heart of someone present, or speak in different languages, just as a jinn speaks through the tongue of a possessed person. The person experiencing this state is unaware of it, like someone whom Satan throws into convulsions through his touch, possessing him and speaking through his tongue. When he regains consciousness, he has no awareness of anything he said. Thus, a possessed person may be struck without the blows affecting the human being. On regaining consciousness, he reports that he felt nothing, because the blows fell upon the jinn possessing him.

Among these people are those to whom a devil brings foods, fruits, sweets, and other things unavailable in that place. Others are carried through the air by a jinn to Mecca, Jerusalem, or elsewhere. Some are carried there late on the Day of ‘Arafa and brought back that very night. Such a person does not perform Hajj as prescribed by Islamic law. Rather, he goes in his ordinary clothes, does not enter the consecrated state for pilgrimage when he comes level with the appointed boundary, does not recite the pilgrim’s invocation, does not stop at Muzdalifa, does not circumambulate the House, does not perform the ritual passage between al-Safā and al-Marwa, and does not stone the pillars. Instead, he stands at ‘Arafa in his ordinary clothes and returns that very night. This is not Hajj.

For this reason, one of these people saw the angels recording the pilgrims and asked, “Will you not record me?” They replied, “You are not among the pilgrims”—meaning those performing Hajj as prescribed by Islamic law.

---

## Page 5632

There are several distinctions between the miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s allies and the satanic states that resemble them.

One is that “the miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s allies” arise from faith and piety, whereas “satanic states” arise from what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden. Allah Most High says:

“Say, ‘My Lord has only forbidden immoral deeds, whether committed openly or secretly, sin, unjust aggression, associating with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and saying about Allah what you do not know.’”

Speaking about Allah without knowledge, associating partners with Him, wrongdoing, and immoral deeds have all been forbidden by Allah Most High and His Messenger. They therefore cannot be grounds for Allah Most High to honor someone with miraculous gifts. Thus, if such phenomena do not occur through prayer, remembrance of Allah, and recitation of the Quran, but instead occur through what Satan loves and through practices involving the association of partners with Allah, such as seeking aid from created beings—or if they are used to wrong others and commit immoral deeds—then they are satanic states, not miraculous gifts from the Most Merciful.

Among these people are those whose devil descends upon them when they attend a gathering of whistling and clapping, until it carries them through the air and takes them out of that house. If one of Allah Most High’s allies arrives, he drives the devil away, and the person falls. This has happened to more than one person.

Among these people are those who seek aid from a created being, living or dead, whether that living person is a Muslim, a Christian, or a polytheist. The devil then assumes the form of the person whose aid is sought

---

## Page 5633

and fulfills some of the needs of the person seeking aid. The latter then imagines that it is that person, or an angel in his form. In reality, it is a devil who has led him astray because he associated partners with Allah, just as devils used to enter idols and speak to the polytheists.

To some of these people, the devil appears and says, “I am al-Khidr.” He may tell them certain things and help them achieve some of their aims, as has happened to a number of Muslims, Jews, and Christians. Among many disbelievers in the lands of the East and West, someone dies, and a devil then comes in his form after his death. They believe that it is the deceased himself. The devil pays his debts, returns property entrusted to him, attends to matters connected with the deceased, goes in to his wife, and leaves. They may even have cremated their dead, as the disbelievers of India do, yet they imagine that he has returned to life after his death.

Among these people was a shaykh in Egypt who instructed his servant, saying, “When I die, do not let anyone wash me, for I shall come and wash myself.” When he died, his servant saw someone in his form and believed that it was the shaykh himself who had entered and washed himself. When the visitor had finished the washing—that is, washing the deceased—he vanished. This was a devil who had misled the deceased by telling him, “After death, you will come and wash yourself.” When the man died, the devil again came in his form to mislead the living, just as he had previously misled the deceased.

---

## Page 5634

Some of them see a throne in the air with a light above it and hear someone addressing them, saying, “I am your Lord.” If the person has discernment, he recognizes that it is a devil, rebukes it, and seeks refuge in Allah from it, whereupon it disappears.

Some of them see figures while awake, one of whom claims to be a prophet, a man of truth, or a righteous shaykh. This has happened to more than one person. Others see in a dream that some eminent figure—whether al-Siddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, or someone else—has cut or shaved their hair, or dressed them in his cap or garment. They then awake wearing a cap, with their hair shaved or trimmed. In reality, it was the jinn who shaved or trimmed their hair.

These satanic experiences occur to those who depart from the Quran and Sunnah. They differ in degree, and the jinn who associate with them are of their own kind and follow their beliefs. Among the jinn are disbelievers, evildoers, and those who err. If the human is a disbeliever, an evildoer, or ignorant, they join him in disbelief, wickedness, and misguidance. They may assist him if he agrees to the acts of disbelief they choose, such as adjuring them by the names of those they revere among the jinn and others; writing Allah’s names or some of His words with filth; or reversing the order of Sūrat al-Fātihah, Sūrat al-Ikhlās, the Verse of the Throne, or other passages, and writing them with filth. They then make water sink into the ground for him and transport it, because of the acts of disbelief with which he pleases them.

They may also bring him a woman or boy whom he desires, either through the air or driven and forced to come to him. There are many other such things, which would take too long to describe, and belief in them is belief

---

## Page 5635

in al-jibt and al-tāghūt. Al-jibt means sorcery, while al-tāghūt refers to devils and idols. If a man obeys Allah and His Messenger inwardly and outwardly, they can neither join him in such things nor make peace with him.

Since the prescribed worship of Muslims takes place in mosques, which are the houses of Allah, those who frequent the mosques are further removed from satanic experiences. decayed—that is, decomposed?” He replied, “Allah has forbidden the earth to consume the flesh of the prophets.”

Allah Most High has said in His Book concerning the polytheists among the people of Noah, peace be upon him:

“And they said, ‘Never abandon your gods; never abandon Wadd, Suwā‘, Yaghūth, Ya‘ūq or Nasr.’”

Ibn ‘Abbās and others among the early generations said: These were righteous men among Noah’s people. When they died, the people remained in devotion at their graves, then fashioned statues of them and worshipped them. This was the beginning of idol worship.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, therefore forbade taking graves as places of worship, to close the door to associating partners with Allah. Likewise, he forbade prayer at sunrise and sunset, because the polytheists prostrate to the sun at those times, and Satan accompanies it as it rises and sets. Prayer at those times would thus resemble the prayer of the polytheists, so he closed this door.

Satan leads the children of Adam astray to the extent that he is able. Whoever worships the sun, moon and stars and invokes them—as those who practise invoking the stars do—has a devil descend upon him, speak to him and tell him about certain matters. They call this “the spirit of the stars,” but it is a devil. Although a devil may help a person achieve some of his aims, he harms him many times more than he benefits him. Whoever obeys him will ultimately come to evil, unless Allah turns to him in forgiveness. Likewise, devils may speak to idol worshippers

## Page 5638

and likewise to those who seek help from someone dead or absent, or who call upon the dead, supplicate to Allah through them, or believe that supplication at their graves is better than in homes and mosques. They transmit a hadith that the experts unanimously agree is fabricated:

Since withdrawing into caves and wildernesses is among the innovations that neither Allah nor His Messenger prescribed, devils frequently take refuge in caves and mountains: the Cave of Blood on Mount Qāsiyūn; Mount Lebanon on the Syrian coast; Mount al-Fath at Aswan in Egypt; mountains in Rūm and Khurāsān; mountains in al-Jazīra; and other such places

## Page 5639

and Mount al-Likām, Mount al-Ahyash, Mount Sūlān near Ardabīl, Mount Shuhnak near Tabrīz, Mount Māshkū near Aqashwān, Mount Nahāwand, and other mountains where some people suppose there are righteous men from among humankind, whom they call “men of the unseen.” Yet those present there are men from among the jinn, for there are men among the jinn just as there are among humankind. People fall into three groups regarding extraordinary phenomena:

“One group” denies that such things occur to anyone other than prophets, though it may acknowledge them in general

but rejects what it is told about many people because, in its view, they are not among Allah’s allies. Others suppose that anyone who displays any extraordinary phenomenon is an ally of Allah. The former deny that there could be anyone among them who displays extraordinary phenomena. The correct position is the third: they do have supporters of their own kind, not allies of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. As Allah Most High says:

“O you who believe, do not take the Jews and Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. Whoever among you takes them as allies is indeed one of them.”

Devils attach themselves to these worshippers and ascetics who are not among Allah’s pious allies who follow the Quran and Sunnah. Each may therefore display extraordinary feats suited to his condition. However, their feats counteract one another, and when a firmly established ally of Allah Most High is present, he nullifies their feats. Each of them inevitably exhibits falsehood—whether through ignorance or deliberately—and sin corresponding to the condition of the devils attached to them. “Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?”

“They descend upon every sinful liar.”

A “liar” is one who habitually lies, and “sinful” means wicked.

Among the strongest means of reinforcing satanic states is listening to singing and musical instruments. This is the listening practiced by the polytheists. Allah Most High says:

“Their prayer at the House was nothing but

## Page 5641

whistling and clapping.” Ibn ‘Abbās, Ibn ‘Umar—may Allah be pleased with them—and others among the early generations explained that “tasdiya” means clapping the hands, while “mukā’” is a sound like whistling. this verse:

## Page 5643

but rather regarded it as a blameworthy innovation. Al-Shāfiʿī even said:

Allah’s friends who possess knowledge recognize this and know that Satan has a considerable share in it. Thus, the best of those among them who attended such gatherings repented of doing so. The further someone is from knowledge and from perfect friendship with Allah, the greater Satan’s share in him. It is like wine, yet its effect on souls is greater than that of wine. Thus, when its practitioners become deeply intoxicated, devils descend upon them, speak through the tongues of some, and carry others through the air. Enmity may arise among them, just as it does among wine drinkers. One person’s devils may be stronger than another’s, and so they kill the latter.

The ignorant suppose that this is among the miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s God-fearing friends. In reality, it distances the person concerned from Allah and belongs to satanic states. Killing a Muslim is lawful only on grounds permitted by Allah. How, then, could killing someone whose life is inviolable be something with which Allah honors His friends? The highest honor lies in remaining steadfast in uprightness. Allah has granted no servant an honor comparable to helping him do what He loves and is pleased with, and granting him more of what brings him nearer to Him and raises his rank.

Extraordinary phenomena include those pertaining to knowledge, such as unveilings; those pertaining to power and dominion, such as actions that transcend the ordinary course of events; and those that are

---

## Page 5644

a form of freedom from need for the kinds of knowledge, authority, wealth, and sufficiency outwardly granted to people.

Whatever Allah grants His servant of these things, if he uses it to help him do what Allah loves and is pleased with, what brings him nearer to Him and raises his rank, and what Allah and His Messenger command, he thereby gains greater distinction and nearness to Allah and His Messenger, and his rank rises. If, however, he uses it to help him do what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, such as associating partners with Allah, wrongdoing, and acts of indecency, he thereby deserves blame and punishment. Unless Allah Most High comes to his aid by granting him repentance or good deeds that erase sins, he will be like other sinners.

Thus, those who possess extraordinary abilities are often punished: sometimes by being deprived of them, just as a king is deposed from his kingdom or a scholar is stripped of his knowledge; sometimes by being deprived of voluntary acts of worship, descending from a special degree of friendship with Allah to its general degree; sometimes by falling to the rank of the defiantly sinful; and sometimes by apostatizing from Islam. This occurs among those whose extraordinary feats are satanic, for many of them apostatize from Islam. Many do not know that these feats are satanic, but suppose them to be miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s friends. Some of them suppose that when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, grants a servant something beyond the ordinary course of events, He will not hold him accountable for it—just as some suppose that when Allah grants a servant dominion, wealth, and power to act, He will not hold him accountable for these things.

Some use extraordinary abilities to pursue permissible matters that are neither commanded nor forbidden. Such a person belongs to the general body of Allah’s friends: the righteous who follow a middle course. As for the foremost, those brought near to Allah, they rank above these, just as the servant

## Page 5645

who is a messenger ranks above the prophet who is a king.

Since extraordinary feats often lower a man’s rank, many righteous people repent of such things and seek Allah Most High’s forgiveness, just as they repent of sins such as unlawful sexual intercourse and theft. When such feats are offered to some of them, they ask Allah to remove them. I know someone who sets out to hunt birds, and sparrows and other birds speak to him, saying, “Take me so that the poor may eat me.” A devil has entered them, just as it enters human beings, and speaks these words to him.

Some people are inside a locked house, then find themselves outside it without having opened it, or the reverse. The same happens at city gates: the jinn have swiftly carried them in or out. Or lights pass before someone, or a person he seeks appears before him. This comes from devils assuming the form of his companion. When he recites the Verse of the Throne repeatedly, all of this disappears.

## Page 5646

such as his conceiving of control over birds and locusts in the air. Whenever he thinks of the birds or locusts moving right or left, they go where he wishes. They carry him to Mecca and bring him back, and bring him figures of beautiful appearance, telling him, “These are the cherubic angels; they wished to visit you.” He thinks to himself, “How have they taken the form of beardless youths?” Then he raises his head and finds them bearded. He is told, “The sign that you are the Mahdī is that a mole will appear on your body.” It appears, and he sees it. Other things happen too, all of them part of Satan’s cunning.

This is a vast subject. Were I to recount what I know of it, it would require a large volume. Allah Most High has said:

“As for man, when his Lord tests him by honouring him and granting him blessings, he says, ‘My Lord has honoured me.’”

“But when He tests him by restricting his provision, he says, ‘My Lord has humiliated me.’”

Allah, Blessed and Most High, says:

“No!”

The word “No” conveys both rebuke and a call to attention: a rebuke against speaking in this way, and a call to heed the statements and commands that follow. Not everyone who receives worldly blessings regarded as marks of honour is thereby being honoured by Allah, Mighty and Majestic; nor is everyone whose share of them He restricts thereby being humiliated by Him. Rather, He—glory be to Him—tests His servant through prosperity and adversity. He may bestow worldly blessings upon someone whom He does not love and who holds no honour with Him, thereby leading him gradually towards ruin. And He may shield someone whom He loves and takes as His friend from such blessings, lest they diminish his rank with Him or cause him to fall into conduct that He dislikes.

---

## Page 5647

Moreover, “miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s friends” must arise from faith and mindfulness of Allah. Whatever arises from disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience belongs to the extraordinary feats of Allah’s enemies, not to the miraculous gifts of His friends.

Thus, if a person’s extraordinary feats do not occur through prayer, Quran recitation, remembrance of Allah, night prayer, and supplication, but occur instead through associating partners with Allah—such as invoking the dead or the absent—or through wickedness, disobedience, and consuming forbidden things, such as snakes, wasps, beetles, blood, and other impurities, or through singing and dancing, especially with non-mahram women and beardless youths; if his extraordinary powers weaken when he hears the Quran and grow stronger when he hears Satan’s pipes, so that he dances long into the night, yet when prayer time comes he prays sitting down or pecks through his prayer like a rooster; and if he hates listening to the Quran, recoils from it, and forces himself to listen, having no love for it and finding in it neither spiritual relish nor delight in his state of ecstasy, while he loves listening to whistling and clapping and experiences ecstatic feelings through them—then these are satanic states. He is among those encompassed by the words of Allah Most High:

“Whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil who becomes his companion.”

The Quran is the remembrance of the Most Merciful. Allah Most High says:

“But whoever turns away from My remembrance will have a life of hardship, and We will raise him up blind on the Day of Resurrection.”

“He will say, ‘My Lord, why have You raised me up blind when I used to see?’”

“He will say, ‘So it is: Our signs came to you, but you forgot them; and so today you will be forgotten.’”

This means: you abandoned acting upon them. Ibn ‘Abbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said, “Allah has guaranteed that whoever reads His Book and acts upon its teachings will neither go astray in this world nor suffer misery in the Hereafter.” He then recited this verse.

## Page 5651

Then, after the jinn heard the Quran, they came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and believed in him. They were the jinn of Nisibis, as established in al-Sahīh in the hadith of Ibn Mas‘ūd. It is also related that he recited Surah al-Rahmān to them, and whenever he said:

“Then which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?”

they replied: “We deny none of Your favors, our Lord; to You belongs all praise.”

“When they met the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, they asked him for provisions for themselves and their animals. He said: ‘You may have every bone over which Allah’s name has been mentioned; you will find it abundantly covered with meat. Every dropping will be fodder for your animals.’ The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘Do not cleanse yourselves with either of these after relieving yourselves, for they are provisions for your brothers among the jinn.’”

This prohibition is established from him through several channels. Scholars have cited it as evidence prohibiting the use of these things for cleansing after relieving oneself. They said: “If using the provisions of the jinn and their animals for such cleansing is forbidden, then it is all the more forbidden to use food and fodder intended for humans and their animals.”

Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, was sent to all humans and jinn. This is of far greater standing before Allah Most High than the jinn’s being subjected to Solomon, peace be upon him. They were subjected to Solomon, who exercised royal authority over them, whereas Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, was sent to them to command them to do what Allah and His Messenger commanded, for he is Allah’s servant and Messenger. The station of a servant-messenger is above that of a prophet-king.

The disbelievers among the jinn will enter the Fire, according to explicit scriptural evidence and scholarly consensus. As for the believers among them, the majority of

---

## Page 5652

scholars hold that they will enter Paradise. The majority of scholars also hold that the messengers were human and that no messenger was sent from among the jinn. There are, however, warners among them. A detailed discussion of these matters belongs elsewhere.

The point here is that relations between jinn and humans take various forms:

A human who commands the jinn to do what Allah and His Messenger have commanded—worshipping Allah alone and obeying His Prophet—and commands humans to do likewise is among the foremost allies of Allah Most High. In this capacity, he is one of the Messenger’s successors and deputies.

Someone who employs the jinn in matters lawful for him is like someone who employs humans in matters lawful for him. For example, he may command them to fulfill their obligations, forbid them from doing what is unlawful for them, and employ them in matters lawful for him. He thus stands in the position of kings who do the same. Supposing that he is one of the allies of Allah Most High, he belongs, at most, to the general ranks of Allah’s allies, standing as a prophet-king does in relation to a servant-messenger: as Solomon and Joseph stand in relation to Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad—may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon them all.

Whoever employs the jinn in what Allah and His Messenger forbid—whether in associating partners with Allah, killing someone whose life is inviolable, or committing aggression against such people short of killing them, such as making someone ill

---

## Page 5653

or making him forget what he has learned, or other such wrongs—or in sexual immorality, such as having someone brought to him for illicit relations—has sought their assistance in sin and aggression. If he seeks their assistance in disbelief, he is a disbeliever; if he seeks their assistance in sins, he is sinful, whether his sin amounts to unrighteousness or falls short of it.

If, however, his knowledge of the Sharia is incomplete and he seeks their assistance in things he supposes to be miraculous gifts—for example, having them assist him in performing Hajj, fly him through the air during innovated devotional listening sessions, carry him to Arafat without his performing the lawful Hajj commanded by Allah and His Messenger, or transport him from one city to another, and the like—then he is deluded, and they have deceived him.

Many such people may not know that these things come from the jinn. They have merely heard that Allah’s allies receive miraculous gifts and perform extraordinary feats. Yet they lack sufficient understanding of the realities of faith and knowledge of the Quran to distinguish miraculous gifts from the Most Merciful from satanic deceptions. The jinn therefore deceive each person according to his beliefs. If he is a polytheist who worships celestial bodies and idols, they lead him to imagine that he benefits from that worship. His intention is to seek the intercession and mediation of the king, prophet, or righteous shaykh in whose likeness the idol was fashioned. He thus considers himself righteous, whereas his worship is, in reality, directed to Satan. Allah Most High says:

“And on the Day He gathers them all together, He will say to the angels, ‘Was it you that these people used to worship?’

They will say, ‘Glory be to You! You are our Protector, not they. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them believed in them.’”

---

## Page 5654

This is why those who prostrate to the sun, moon, and stars intend to prostrate to them, but the devil draws alongside these objects when they prostrate, so that their prostration is directed to him. This is also why the devil assumes the likeness of those whom the polytheists call upon for help. If someone is a Christian and calls upon George or someone else for help, the devil appears in the likeness of George or whoever he calls upon. If someone professes Islam and calls upon a Muslim shaykh of whom he thinks well, the devil appears in that shaykh’s likeness. If someone is among the polytheists of India, he appears in the likeness of whoever that polytheist reveres. Now, if the shaykh being called upon is knowledgeable about the Sharia, the devil does not inform him that he has appeared in his likeness to his companions who call upon him for help. If, however, the shaykh has no knowledge of what they have said, the devil conveys their words to him. They then imagine that the shaykh has heard their voices from afar and answered them, whereas this happens only through the devil’s mediation.

One shaykh who had experienced something like this in the form of disclosures of hidden matters and communication related what had happened. He said:

“The jinn show me something gleaming, like water and glass.” In it they depict for him whatever he is asked to report. He said: “I then inform people of it. They also convey to me the words of my companions who call upon me for help. I answer, and they deliver my reply to them.”

Many of the shaykhs who had experienced numerous such extraordinary feats, when someone unfamiliar with these feats denied them and said, “You do this through trickery, just as

---

## Page 5655

someone enters a fire using talq stone, bitter-orange peel, frog fat, and other tricks based on natural properties,” these shaykhs would be astonished and say, “By Allah, we know nothing of these tricks.”

When someone knowledgeable explained to them, “You are indeed truthful about that, but these experiences are satanic,” they acknowledged this. Those among them whom Allah enabled to repent then repented, once the truth became clear to them and various indications showed them that these experiences came from the devil. They recognized their demonic origin when they saw that they occurred through such things as innovations condemned by the Sharia and acts of disobedience to Allah, but not during the prescribed acts of worship that Allah and His Messenger love. They then knew that these were the devil’s deceptive feats for his allies, not miraculous favors bestowed by the Most Merciful upon His friends.

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knows best what is correct. To Him is the return and final destination. May Allah bestow blessings and peace upon Muhammad, the foremost of His messengers and prophets, and upon his family, Companions, supporters, followers, and successors—blessings and peace through which we may merit his intercession.

“Āmīn.”
