## Page 5772

A comparable example is the hadith about a sheep that was on the point of death, which a woman slaughtered without its owners’ permission. They asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he permitted them to eat it. He did not require the woman who slaughtered it to compensate them for any reduction in its value caused by slaughtering it, because customary permission existed, and customary permission is equivalent to verbal permission. For this reason:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gave the pledge of allegiance on ‘Uthmān’s behalf in his absence, without asking his permission verbally.”

Likewise, when Abū Talhah invited him and a few others to his home, he set out with everyone in the mosque, knowing that Abū Talhah would gladly welcome them, because of the blessing Allah would bestow. The same applies to the hadith of Jābir. It is also authentically established that a butcher invited him, and he sought his permission for another person accompanying him, because he did not know that the butcher would be as willing to welcome him as he knew Abū Talhah, Jābir and others would be.

Similarly, killing the boy was a case of repelling an aggressor against his parents, because al-Khidr knew that he would tempt them away from their religion. Killing children is permissible if they fight the Muslims; indeed, it is permissible to kill them to repel an attack on property. Thus, it is established in Sahīh al-Bukhārī that when Najdah al-Harūrī asked Ibn ‘Abbās about killing boys, he replied:

“If you know about them what al-Khidr knew about the boy, then kill them; otherwise, do not kill them.”

Likewise, the two Sahīhs relate:

“When ‘Umar asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for permission to kill Ibn Sayyād, who was approaching puberty, because he thought him to be the Dajjāl, the Prophet replied, ‘If he is, you will never be given power over him; and if he is not, there is no good for you in killing him.’”

He did not say, “If he is, there is no good for you in killing him.” Rather, he said, “You will never be given power over him.”

---

## Page 5773

And this indicates that, had it been possible to kill him before he reached puberty in order to put an end to his corruption, doing so would not have been forbidden. Otherwise, his young age would have been sufficient grounds for the ruling: when the more general ground independently establishes a ruling, the more specific ground has no effect. This is comparable to his saying about the cat:

“It is not impure; it is among those, male and female, who move about among you.”

As for rebuilding the wall, this involved only forgoing payment despite their hunger. Al-Khidr explained that its owners deserved his freely given assistance because of their character and their father’s righteousness, even though he himself was hungry.

Related to this is the fact that some grounds for obligation, prohibition and permissibility are apparent, so that people share knowledge of them. Others are hidden from some people but apparent to others through ordinary means. Still others are hidden and become known through unveiling. The story of al-Khidr belongs to this category.

This occurs frequently within our community. For example, someone may be served food and have it disclosed to him that it was unlawfully seized. It then becomes forbidden for him to eat it, although it is not forbidden for someone unaware of that fact. Or he may obtain property whose owner, he knows, has permitted him to use it; he may therefore lawfully make use of it, whereas someone unaware of that permission may not. There are other similar examples.

In such cases, if the shaykh is known for truthfulness and sincerity, the matter falls within the scope of his exercise of judgment, in which he is sometimes right and sometimes mistaken,

---

## Page 5774

for unveilings are subject to correctness and error, just as dreams and their interpretation, opinions and transmitted reports are. Nothing is entirely free from error except what is reliably established from the Messenger. All matters must therefore be referred back to the message with which he was sent. This is why a man of consummate truthfulness who receives everything from the Messenger, such as Abū Bakr, is superior to someone who receives inspiration, such as Umar. The former would clarify matters that confused the latter, bringing him back to what was correct. This is what Abū Bakr did with Umar on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, on the day the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, died, regarding fighting those who withheld zakah, and on other occasions. We have discussed this subject at length elsewhere.

The point is that nothing in the story of al-Khidr permits anyone whatsoever to contravene the law of Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Admittedly, the term “religious law” has acquired several meanings in common usage. Some people use it to mean judicial rulings. Undoubtedly, a judge’s ruling may accord with the underlying truth, or it may contradict it. Hence the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in the hadith narrated by Umm Salamah and recorded by both al-Bukhārī and Muslim:

“You bring your disputes before me, and some of you may present their arguments more eloquently than others. I judge only according to what I hear. If I award anyone something that rightfully belongs to his brother, he must not take it, for I am only awarding him a piece of the Fire.”

Muslims agree that a judge’s ruling concerning rights in general does not alter the underlying reality of the matter. Thus, if he were to award Zayd’s property to Umar on the basis of an admission or evidence,

---

## Page 5775

that ruling would be invalid in terms of the underlying reality and would not make the property lawful for him. By Muslim consensus, he may not take it while knowing the actual circumstances. Likewise, according to the vast majority of the Muslim community, if a judge rules concerning a contract, the annulment of a marriage, a divorce, or a sale, his ruling does not change the underlying reality. Some, however, maintain that his ruling does change it in these matters because he has authority over the conclusion and dissolution of contracts. The majority’s position is correct. It is the position of Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Ahmad, the other jurists of the Hijaz and the scholars of hadith, and many Iraqi jurists.

Furthermore, the term “religious law” is used in our time in three senses: revealed law, interpreted law, and altered law. “Revealed law” is the Quran and Sunnah, which everyone must follow. Whoever believes that some people are not obliged to follow it is a disbeliever.

“Interpreted law” concerns matters open to scholarly judgment over which scholars have disagreed. Following one of the scholars qualified to exercise such judgment is permissible for someone who believes that his evidence is stronger, or for someone permitted to follow his authority. Muslims as a whole are not obliged to follow any particular individual other than Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Thus many students of jurisprudence, when they see one of the righteous shaykhs, believe that he may be in the right and that someone else has contravened

---

## Page 5776

religious law, when he has only contravened what that student supposes to be religious law. The student’s understanding may be mistaken, in which case he is rewarded for his scholarly effort and forgiven for his error. The other person, too, may have exercised scholarly judgment and been mistaken.

As for “altered law,” it includes fabricated hadiths, corrupt interpretations, invalid analogies, and forbidden adherence to another’s authority. This, too, is prohibited. This is one source of dispute: many students of jurisprudence and speculative theologians may require Sufis and those who profess spiritual poverty to follow their particular school, adhere to the authority of their chosen scholar, and accept their judge’s ruling as binding both inwardly and outwardly. They regard departure from this as departure from the law brought by Muhammad. This is ignorance and injustice on their part; indeed, making such an unrestricted claim is disbelief and hypocrisy. Likewise, many Sufis and those who profess spiritual poverty hold a similar view concerning their shaykh and the authority they follow. In this respect, they are no different from the others.

Each of these groups may permit departure from what the Quran and Sunnah have brought on account of something they suppose contradicts them: what one calls spiritual experience, ecstasy, unveilings, and communications, or what the other calls analogy, opinion, rational arguments, and conclusive proofs. All of this belongs to the branches of hypocrisy. Rather, everyone must believe the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in everything he has reported and obey him in everything he has commanded. No one may oppose him by drawing comparisons or appealing to people’s opinions. Everything that contradicts him is error and misguidance.

---

## Page 5777

We have discussed this elsewhere in greater detail than space permits here. May Allah Most High guide us and all our brethren to the words and deeds, inward and outward, that He loves and is pleased with, in every circumstance.

Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best. All praise belongs to Allah alone. May His blessings and peace be upon His Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his Companions.

---

## Page 5778

Shaykh al-Islām was asked:

Is the hadith reported concerning the abdāl (replacements) authentic, or is its chain of transmission broken? Are the abdāl confined to Syria, or are they found wherever the observances of Islam are upheld according to the Quran and Sunnah, whether in Syria or other regions? Is it true that a friend of Allah may be sitting among a group of people and his body disappear? What do the learned scholars say about the titles given to certain people associated with religious devotion and virtue, such as: “This is the Succour of Succours,” “This is the Pole of Poles,” “This is the Pole of the World,” “This is the Great Pole,” and “This is the Seal of the Friends of Allah”?

He answered:

As for the titles commonly used by many devout worshippers and ordinary people, such as the “Succour” in Mecca, the “Four Pegs,” the “Seven Poles,” the “Forty Abdāl,” and the “Three Hundred Noble Ones,” these titles are not found in the Book of Allah Most High. Nor are they transmitted from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, through an authentic chain of transmission, or even a weak one that could support the expressions concerning the abdāl.

---

## Page 5779

For a Syrian hadith with a broken chain of transmission has been reported concerning them from 'Alī ibn Abī Tālib—may Allah be pleased with him—and traced back to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as saying:

“Among them—meaning the people of Syria—are the abdāl, forty men. Whenever one man dies, Allah Most High replaces him with another.”

These titles, arranged in this hierarchy, are not found in the words of the early generations. Nor are they transmitted with this hierarchy and these meanings from the shaykhs generally accepted by the Muslim community. Rather, they are found in this form only in reports from certain intermediate shaykhs, who used them either when transmitting them from others or simply mentioning them.

In this and similar matters of religious knowledge, truth has become confused with falsehood among most people of later times. Thus, there is truth in it that calls for acceptance and falsehood that calls for rejection. Many people have consequently fallen into two opposite extremes: some have rejected it all because of the falsehood they found in it, while others have accepted it all because of the truth they found in it. The correct approach is simply to affirm the truth and reject the falsehood.

This fulfills what the Prophet, peace be upon him, foretold: that this community would follow the ways of those before it, just as one arrow’s feather matches another. For the people of the two Scriptures mixed truth with falsehood. This is the alteration and distortion that occurred in their religion; and thus religion is changed

---

## Page 5780

sometimes through alteration and at other times through abrogation. This religion, however, will never be abrogated. Yet there will be those who introduce into it distortion, alteration, lies, and concealment, thereby mixing truth with falsehood. Allah will unfailingly raise up within it people through whom His proof is established, as successors to the messengers. They will purge it of the distortions of extremists, the fabrications of those who promote falsehood, and the misinterpretations of the ignorant. Thus Allah establishes the truth and nullifies falsehood, however much the polytheists may dislike it.

Through the Books sent down from heaven and the legacy of knowledge transmitted from the Seal of the Prophets, Allah distinguishes truth from falsehood and judges between people concerning their differences. This makes it clear that these titles, with their specified numbers, hierarchy, and ranks, do not hold true in every age. Rather, it must be stated categorically that this claim, in its universal and unrestricted form, is false. Believers are sometimes few and sometimes numerous; likewise, those among them who are foremost in faith and brought near to Allah are sometimes few and sometimes numerous, and they move from place to place. It is not a requirement for the allies of Allah—the people of faith and piety, including those foremost in faith and brought near to Him—to remain in one place throughout all ages. Nor is it a requirement for the allies of Allah—the people of faith and piety, including those foremost in faith and brought near to Him—to be of a fixed number.

Allah sent His Messenger with the truth, and a small group in Mecca believed alongside him. They were fewer than seven, then fewer than forty, then fewer than seventy, then fewer than

---

## Page 5781

three hundred. It is therefore clear that these numbers were not to be found among them, nor could such ranks have been held by unbelievers. Then he and his Companions migrated to Medina. It was the home of migration, the Sunnah, and support for the faith; the seat of prophethood and the site of the caliphate that succeeded it. There the pledges of allegiance were given to the rightly guided caliphs—Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, and ʿAlī, may Allah Most High be pleased with them all—even though the latter left it after receiving the pledge there. It is impossible that anyone in Mecca during their time could have been superior to them.

Islam then spread throughout the east and west of the earth. At every period, the believers included devout allies of Allah—indeed, steadfastly truthful people, foremost in faith and brought near to Him—in numbers that only the Lord of the worlds can count. They were not limited to three hundred or three thousand. After the three virtuous generations had passed away, the generations that have since passed included devout allies of Allah—indeed, people foremost in faith and brought near to Him—whose numbers are unknown. They are neither confined to a fixed number nor restricted to a particular period. Anyone who assigns them a fixed number advances a false claim, whether deliberately or mistakenly.

We therefore ask him: Who were the Pole and the three, and so on up to seven hundred, in the time of Adam, Noah, and Abraham, and before Muhammad—peace and blessings be upon them—during the interval between messengers, when people in general were unbelievers? Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, Abraham was a community in himself, devoutly obedient to Allah, upright in faith.”

That is, he alone was a believer, while all the people were unbelievers. In Sahīh al-Bukhārī, it is reported that he said to Sarah:

“There is no believer on earth today other than you and me.”

And Allah Most High says: “He is the One who

---

## Page 5782

sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although before that they were in manifest error.”

If they claim that these people existed after our Messenger, peace be upon him, we ask them: In what period did they exist? Who was the first of them? By what verse, what well-known hadith in the Six Books, and what consensus transmitted through numerous independent channels from the first three generations has their existence in these numbers been established, so that we should believe in it? For beliefs are to be held only on the basis of these three forms of evidence and rational proof:

“Say: Bring your proof, if you are truthful.”

If they do not produce these four forms of evidence sanctioned by the revealed Law, they are undoubtedly lying, and we do not accept their falsehoods as beliefs. Their claim would also entail that Allah, glorified and exalted be He, provides for the unbelievers and grants them victory over their enemy directly, without an intermediary, but provides for the believers and grants them victory through created intermediaries. Yet honour lies in the absence of an intermediary, as in “the spirit of Allah” and “the she-camel of Allah.” Reflect without becoming bewildered, and commit this principle firmly to memory.

“As for the titles al-ghawth and al-ghiyāth (succour and aid)”

None but Allah deserves them, for He is the source of aid for those who seek it. Thus, no one may seek deliverance from anyone other than Him, neither an angel brought near to Him nor a prophet sent by Him. Whoever claims that the people of the earth submit their petitions, in which they seek

---

## Page 5783

relief from their distress and the descent of mercy, to the three hundred, who pass them on to the seventy, the seventy to the forty, the forty to the seven, the seven to the four, and the four to the ghawth, is a liar, misguided and a polytheist. For the polytheists themselves were as Allah Most High described them when He said:

“When distress befalls you at sea, all those you call upon fail you except Him.”

And He, glorified and exalted be He, said:

“Who is it that answers the distressed when he calls upon Him?”

How, then, could believers subsequently submit their petitions to Him through intermediary gatekeepers, when He, Most High, says:

“When My servants ask you about Me, I am indeed near. I answer the prayer of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me, that they may be rightly guided.”

And Abraham, peace be upon him, said, praying for the people of Mecca:

“Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in a barren valley near Your Sacred House, our Lord, so that they may establish prayer. So make the hearts of some people incline towards them, and provide them with fruits, that they may be grateful.”

“Our Lord, You know what we conceal and what we reveal. Nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from Allah.”

“Praise be to Allah, who has granted me Ishmael and Isaac in old age. Indeed, my Lord hears all prayers.”

And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said to his Companions when they raised their voices in remembrance of Allah: “O people, be easy on yourselves! You are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent; rather, you are calling upon

---

## Page 5784

One who is All-Hearing and near. Indeed, the One upon whom you call is nearer to each of you than the neck of his mount.” This is a vast subject.

All Muslims know that neither ordinary Muslims nor their well-known shaykhs used to present their needs to Allah, outwardly or inwardly, through these intermediaries and gatekeepers. Exalted is Allah, far above being likened to created kings and above all else that the wrongdoers say.

This is akin to the claim of the Rāfidah that every age must have an infallible imam who serves as Allah’s proof against those subject to religious obligations, and without whom faith cannot be complete. Yet they also say that he was a boy who entered the cellar more than four hundred and forty years ago, while neither he nor any trace of him is known, and there is no perceptible sign or news of him.

Those who claim these ranks resemble the Rāfidah in certain respects. Indeed, this hierarchy and its numbers resemble, in some respects, the hierarchy of the Ismāʿīliyyah, the Nusayriyyah and others like them, with their al-sābiq (the Preceding One), al-tālī (the Following One), al-nātiq (the Speaker), al-asās (the Foundation), al-jasad (the Body), and other such ranks for which Allah has sent down no authority.

---

## Page 5785

As for the awtād (pegs), one sometimes finds people saying, “So-and-so is one of the awtād,” meaning that through him Allah Most High makes faith and religion firm in the hearts of those whom He guides through him, just as He makes the earth firm with its pegs. This meaning applies to every scholar who possesses this quality. Anyone through whom knowledge and faith are firmly established among people at large is like mighty pegs and great mountains, while someone of lesser standing serves this role to a corresponding degree. This is not restricted to four, or to any smaller or greater number. Rather, these people fixed their number at four in imitation of what astrologers say about the pegs of the earth.

As for the qutb (pivot), one likewise finds them saying, “So-and-so is one of the pivots,” or “So-and-so is a pivot.” Anyone around whom some religious or worldly affair revolves, inwardly or outwardly, is the pivot and centre of that affair. This applies whether the affairs revolving around him are those of his household, street, village or city, and whether they concern religious or worldly matters, inwardly or outwardly. This meaning is not restricted to seven, or to any smaller or greater number. However, the praiseworthy person among these is one around whom the soundness of both worldly and religious affairs revolves, rather than merely that of worldly affairs. Such is the pivot according to their usage. In some ages, one person may happen to be the best of his contemporaries; in another age, two or three may be equal in merit before Allah. It is not necessary that in every age there be one person who is, without qualification, the best of all people in Allah’s sight.

---

## Page 5786

Likewise, the term “badal” (substitute) occurs in the statements of many of them. As for the report traced back to the Prophet, it is more likely that it is not among his words, peace be upon him. Faith was present in the Hijāz and Yemen before the conquest of Syria, while Syria and Iraq were lands of unbelief. Then, concerning the events during the caliphate of ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, it is authentically established that the Prophet, peace be upon him, said:

“A faction will break away from the Muslims, and whichever of the two parties is closer to the truth will kill them.”

Thus, ʿAlī and his companions were closer to the truth than the people of Syria who fought them. It is well known that the Companions who were with ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, such as ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, Sahl ibn Hunayf and others like them, were superior to those who were with Muʿāwiyah—even if Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqās and others who refrained from fighting were superior to those who sided with either of them. Given this, how could one believe that all the abdāl, who are the best of mankind, were among the people of Syria? This is categorically false. Although well-known reports relate the virtues of Syria and its people, Allah has appointed a due measure for everything.

One must speak with knowledge and fairness. Whoever speaks about religion without knowledge falls under the words of Allah Most High:

“Do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge,”

and His words:

“And that you say about Allah what you do not know.”

Whoever speaks with fairness and justice falls under the words of Allah Most High:

“O you who believe, stand firmly for justice as witnesses for Allah,”

and His words:

“And when you speak, be just,”

and His words:

“We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance so that people may uphold justice.”

Those who have used the designation badal have explained it in several ways. One is that they are substitutes for the prophets.

---

## Page 5787

and another is that whenever one of them dies, Allah Most High replaces him with another man; another is that their bad traits, deeds and beliefs have been replaced with good ones. None of these qualities is exclusive to forty people, or to any smaller or larger number, nor are they confined to the inhabitants of any particular region. This clarification also makes plain the meaning of the designation “nujabā’” (noble ones).

The point is that these designations are sometimes interpreted in ways invalidated by the Quran, the Sunnah and the consensus of the early generations. For example, some explain “ghawth” (succour) as the person through whom Allah provides the inhabitants of the earth with sustenance and victory. This resembles what Christians say about the pope. Yet this supposed ghawth has neither existence nor effect, much like the awaited one who entered the cellar some four hundred and forty years ago.

Likewise, interpreting “the forty abdāl” to mean that people receive victory and sustenance only through them is false. Rather, victory and sustenance come through various means, among the most potent of which are the believers’ supplications, beneficence and sincerity. This is not restricted to forty people, or to any smaller or larger number. As stated in the well-known hadith, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqās said:

“O Messenger of Allah, if a man is his people’s defender, is he allotted the same share as the weakest among them?”

He replied:

“O Saʿd, are you granted victory and sustenance except through the weak among you—through their supplications, prayers and sincerity?”

There may also be other means of obtaining sustenance and victory, for the wicked and the unbelievers

---

## Page 5788

are also granted sustenance and victory. He may afflict the believers’ land with drought and cause them to fear their enemy so that they turn back to Him and repent of their sins, thus granting them both forgiveness of sins and relief from distress. He may give the unbelievers respite, send abundant rain upon them, and provide them with wealth and children, drawing them gradually towards ruin without their knowing—either to seize them in this world with the grip of One Almighty, All-Powerful, or to multiply their punishment in the Hereafter. Not every blessing is a mark of honour, nor is every trial a punishment. Allah Most High says:

“As for man, when his Lord tests him by honouring him and bestowing favours upon him, he says, ‘My Lord has honoured me.’”

“But when He tests him by restricting his provision, he says, ‘My Lord has humiliated me.’”

“No indeed!”

Among Allah’s God-fearing friends, His sincere and righteous worshippers, and the prophets He sent, there is none whose body was perpetually hidden from people’s sight. Rather, this is akin to the claims that ʿAlī is in the clouds, that Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah is in the mountains of Radwā, that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan is in the cellar at Samarra, that al-Hākim is on a mountain in Egypt, and that the forty abdāl are the men of the unseen on Mount Lebanon. All this and similar claims are the assertions of liars and fabricators.

Certainly, the ordinary course of things may be suspended for a person, so that he is sometimes hidden from people’s sight, whether to protect him from an enemy or for some other reason. But the claim that he remains this way throughout his life is false. Indeed, the light of his heart, the guidance within it, and what it holds of Allah Most High’s secrets, His trust, His lights and knowledge of Him may be hidden from people’s eyes, and his righteousness and friendship with Allah may remain hidden from

---

## Page 5789

most people. This is what actually occurs. The secrets of the True One remain between Him and His friends, and most people do not know. We have already demonstrated that the title ghawth (succour-giver) is altogether invalid; this includes the ghawth of the non-Arabs, the ghawth of Mecca, and the seventh ghawth.

Likewise, the expression “Seal of Allah’s Friends” is invalid and has no foundation. The first to mention it was Muhammad ibn ʿAlī al-Hakīm al-Tirmidhī. A number of people have claimed this title, each asserting that he is the Seal of Allah’s Friends, including Ibn Hamūyah, Ibn ʿArabī, and certain misguided shaykhs in Damascus and elsewhere. Each claims to be superior to the Prophet, peace be upon him, in certain respects, besides making other statements of unbelief and falsehood. All this stems from their ambition to attain the leadership of the Seal of Allah’s Friends, since the leadership of the Seal of the Prophets had eluded them. But they are mistaken.

The Seal of the Prophets is the best of them because of the evidence establishing this, whereas the same does not hold for the seal of Allah’s friends. The best friends of Allah in this community are the earliest pioneers among the Emigrants and the Helpers. The best of this community after its Prophet is Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, followed by ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, then ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, then ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him. Its best generation is the generation among whom the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sent, then those who followed them, then those who followed them.

In reality, the seal of Allah’s friends is the last God-fearing believer to live among people. He is not the best or most excellent of Allah’s friends. Rather, the best and most excellent of them is Abū Bakr al-Siddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, followed by ʿUmar. After the prophets and messengers, the sun has never risen or set upon anyone better than these two.

---

## Page 5790

Shaykh al-Islām—may Allah sanctify his soul—said:

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds. I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah, Lord of the heavens and the earths, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, the Seal of the Prophets. May Allah Most High bless him and his family and grant him enduring peace until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: I have written down what I can recall of the great gathering at the governor’s palace and the parade ground, attended by commanders, secretaries, scholars, the common poor, and others, concerning the “Batā’ihiyyah” on Saturday, the ninth of Jumādā al-Ūlā, in the year five (1). I have done so because of the keen interest in learning about it and people’s eagerness to know what happened. Those who were absent may hear only fragments of the incident,

> **Footnotes:**
> (1) Thus in the original.

---

## Page 5791

while those who witnessed it saw and heard what they did. Even among those present, some heard and saw things that others did not. For this momentous event was far-reaching: it strengthened the religion, made its supreme message prevail, compelled people to follow the Book and the Sunnah, and exposed the falsity of those who departed from them through misleading innovations, corrupt spiritual states, and deception of the Muslims.

Elsewhere I have described the condition of these “Batā’ihiyyah” and their path, as well as the path and condition of Shaykh Ahmad ibn al-Rifā‘ī, explaining where they agreed with the Muslims and where they differed from them. This was to clarify which aspects of their practice belonged to the religion of Islam and which departed from it. Describing all that here would take too long. Here I have written only what I can recall of the account of this well-known encounter in which I debated and confronted them.

I already knew about their condition from what I have mentioned elsewhere: although they profess allegiance to Islam and to the path of spiritual poverty and spiritual discipline, and although some of them exhibit worship, devotion to Allah, spiritual ecstasy, love, asceticism, spiritual poverty, humility, gentleness, courtesy in speech and dealings, spiritual unveiling, the exercise of extraordinary powers, and the like—yet among some of them one also finds polytheism and other forms of unbelief, religious excess and innovations in Islam, disregard for much of what the Messenger brought, contempt for the law of Islam, lying, and deception

---

## Page 5792

and the performance of fraudulent feats, the wrongful consumption of people’s wealth, and hindering others from the path of Allah.

I had already had several encounters with them, during which I explained to those whom I addressed, both among them and others, some of the truth and falsehood found among them, as well as the nature of their states, which they call “signs.” A number of them repented, and several of their shaykhs were disciplined. I also explained how they performed their fraudulent feats, such as handling fire and snakes and producing blood, labdanum, saffron, rosewater, honey, sugar, and other things. Most of this is accomplished through familiar tricks and contrived means.

On more than one occasion, some of them intended to demonstrate these things, but when they saw me challenging them, they withdrew and approached me asking that I conceal their doings. I agreed on condition that they repent. One of their shaykhs even spoke to me at a public gathering attended by many people in a garden, when I challenged them by saying, “I will enter the fire with you after we have washed ourselves with something that removes the means of trickery. Whoever is burned will be the loser.” When they saw that I was serious, they refrained.

That shaykh related that he had once been with one of the Tatar rulers in the East, who had an idol that he worshipped. He said:

“He told me, ‘This idol eats some of this food every day, leaving clear, visible signs of eating in it.’ I denied this, so he said to me, ‘If it does eat, will you agree to die?’ I replied, ‘Yes.’” He continued, “I stayed with him until midday, but no sign of eating appeared in the food. This greatly astonished

---

## Page 5793

the Tatar, who swore solemn oaths, saying, ‘Every day, signs of eating can be seen in it, but today, with you present, none have appeared.’”

I said to this shaykh:

“I shall explain the reason to you. That Tatar is an unbeliever and a polytheist, and his idol has a devil that leads him astray by producing those traces in the food. You had enough of the light of Islam and the support of Allah Most High to make the devil refrain from doing that in your presence. Yet your relation—and that of people like you—to those whose Islam is pure is like the Tatar’s relation to people like you. That Tatar and those like him are black; those whose Islam is unalloyed are white; and you are mottled, with both black and white in you.”

Those present appreciated this comparison. At another gathering, they asked me, “Do you want us to display these signs?”

I replied:

“If you perform them before people who are not versed in these matters—Bedouins, peasants, Turks, ordinary people, or the majority of students of jurisprudence, spiritual aspirants, and Sufis—that will not count in your favour. Whoever has gold should bring it to me in the money-changers’ market, among experts who can distinguish pure gold from adulterated gold and brass. He should not come to me among people who know nothing of such things.”

They said to me, “We will only do this if you lend us your support.”

I replied, “My support is not with you. Rather, I oppose you and will stand in your way, because your purpose in doing this is to overturn the Sharia of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace. If you have the power to display these things, then do so.”

So they went away humiliated.

---

## Page 5794

Some time before this incident, a group of them used to come in with one of their pious shaykhs, wearing iron shackles around their necks. He and his followers were known for certain practices. He would visit me from time to time, and I would address him in the kindest manner.

People then mentioned the innovated outward emblem they displayed, distinguishing themselves from other Muslims and treating it as worship and religion. They led people to believe that this was one of their divine secrets and the distinguishing mark of those endowed with divine gifts who followed their path—I mean the path of that shaykh and his followers. I therefore addressed him about this in the congregational mosque, saying:

“This is an innovation which neither Allah Most High nor His Messenger has prescribed. None of the early generations of this community practised it, nor did any of the shaykhs worthy of being followed. It is not permissible to make it an act of worship or a means of drawing near to Allah Most High, for worshipping Allah through what He has not prescribed is misguidance. Even wearing iron without intending it as worship has been deemed reprehensible by some scholars because of the hadith reported on this subject:

‘The Prophet, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace, saw a man wearing an iron ring and said, “Why do I see you wearing the jewellery of the people of the Fire?”’

“Allah Most High has described the people of the Fire as having shackles around their necks. Resembling the people of the Fire is therefore a reprehensible act.”

Someone remarked, “It is established in the Sahīh, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, that the Prophet, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace, said at the end of the hadith about dreams:

‘I like fetters and dislike neck-shackles. Fetters signify steadfastness in religion.’

“If a neck-shackle is disliked in a dream, how much more so in waking life!”

At that gathering, I said to him what I have related above, or words to that effect, along with

---

## Page 5795

additional remarks. I warned him of the consequences of persisting in innovation and that doing so makes its perpetrator liable to punishment, along with other remarks, most of which I have forgotten because so much time has passed.

The reason is that, by Muslim consensus, practices which are not commended by Islamic law may not be adopted as acts of worship, as means of drawing near to Allah, or as a path to Him and a means of becoming one of His allies and beloved servants. Nor may one believe that Allah loves such practices, or loves those who engage in them on that account, or that adopting them increases a person’s standing with Allah and nearness to Him. Nor may they be made a distinguishing emblem of repentant people who seek Allah’s countenance and are better than those unlike them.

This is a fundamental principle that must be understood and given due attention: permissible things remain permissible only when treated as such. If, however, they are adopted as obligatory or recommended practices, that constitutes a religion which Allah has not prescribed. Classifying as obligatory or recommended something that does not belong to either category is equivalent to classifying as forbidden something that is not forbidden. Nothing is forbidden except what Allah has forbidden, and nothing is religion except what Allah has prescribed. This is why Allah so severely condemns in the Quran those who institute a religion He has not authorized and those who forbid things He has not authorized them to forbid. If this applies to permissible things, what then of reprehensible or forbidden things?

For this reason, such things do not become binding through vows. If a man vows to do something permissible, reprehensible, or forbidden, he is not obliged to do it, unlike someone who vows to obey Allah and is therefore obliged to obey Him. Rather, according to Ahmad and others, he must offer the expiation for breaking an oath if he does not fulfil the vow; according to others, nothing is required of him. Thus, it is not

---

## Page 5796

possible for a vow to turn something that is neither obedience nor worship into (obedience and worship).

Similar to this are the pledges taken from people to follow the path of a particular shaykh, such as the pledges of the people of “futuwwa” (chivalry), the “pellet-shooters,” and the like. A person is not required to commit himself to any of this as a matter of religion and obedience to Allah, except insofar as it constitutes religion and obedience to Allah and His Messenger under Allah’s law. He may, however, be required to offer expiation for breaking such a pledge. For this reason, I have instructed more than one person to turn away from a pledge imposed upon him to follow a less preferable path, or one containing various innovations, and instead adopt something better: obedience to Allah and His Messenger—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—and adherence to the Book and the Sunnah.

Muslims agree that no one may believe or say of an act that it is a means of drawing near to Allah, an act of obedience and righteousness, or an obligatory or recommended path to Allah, unless it is something Allah and His Messenger—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—have commanded. This is known through the evidence established for that purpose. Whatever is known by the consensus of the Muslim community to be neither obligatory nor recommended nor a means of drawing near to Allah may not be believed or described to be a means of drawing near to Him or an act of obedience.

Likewise, they agree that one may not intend thereby to draw near to Allah, worship Him through it, adopt it as religion, or perform it as a good deed. It may not be made part of religion, whether through belief and speech or through intention and action. By neglecting this principle, many scholars and worshippers have fallen into error: they see a practice

---

## Page 5797

as something that, if not unlawful, should not be prohibited, but should instead be declared permissible. They do not distinguish between adopting it as religion, obedience, and righteousness, and engaging in it as one engages in things that are merely permissible. It is well known that adopting it as religion—whether through belief or moderation, or both, or through speech or action, or both—is among the gravest prohibitions and greatest sins. These are reprehensible innovations, more serious than acts of disobedience that are recognized as disobedience and wrongdoing.

Section

When I forbade them to do this, they professed agreement and obedience. Some time passed in this state, while people continued reporting that they persisted in introducing innovations into religion and openly engaging in things contrary to the Muslims’ sacred law. People called for action to be taken against them, but I pursued a course of gentleness and patience, awaiting their return and repentance. I postponed addressing the matter until that shaykh came to the congregational mosque.

He had sent me letter after letter containing arguments, excuses, reproaches, and transmitted reports. Yet this was false discourse that established no proof: it consisted either of fabricated hadiths or of reports from Israelite traditions without sanction in revealed law. The reality of the matter was turning people away from Allah’s path and consuming their wealth unjustly.

I told them, “The answer will be given in person, for a full answer to a letter like this can only be given in that way.” One of them came to us, and we removed the shackle from his neck.

---

## Page 5798

and these people are followers of their own desires, who in many matters worship according to their desires rather than what Allah Most High and His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, have commanded:

“And who is more astray than one who follows his own desire without guidance from Allah?”

Thus, their ecstasy is mostly unrestrained desire: they do not know whom they worship. They bear a strong resemblance to the Christians, concerning whom Allah Most High said:

“O People of the Scripture, do not exceed the bounds of truth in your religion, nor follow the desires of people who went astray before, led many astray, and strayed from the straight path.”

This is why the early generations called the people of innovation “followers of desires.” Their desires drove them to assemble like opposing factions and enter the congregational mosque ready for battle, equipped with the spiritual states they cultivate to overpower others. When the Friday prayer was over, I sent for their shaykh so that we might address him concerning Allah’s command—may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace—and agree to follow His way. Instead, they left the congregational mosque in their crowds and went to the governor’s palace. It seemed that they had reached an agreement with some prominent men concerning what they sought. They then returned to the al-Shāghū mosque—as I was told—shouting and agitating in a most astonishing manner.

I sent for them a second time, to establish the proof and discharge my responsibility, seeking clarification and insight, and hoping to bring benefit and a reminder. They headed to the palace a second time. I was told that they approached from the western side, making a loud uproar, frothing and thundering, shaking their heads and limbs, rolling about in the Barada River, and displaying a rapture which

---

## Page 5799

they used to beguile others towards ruin, and parading their claimed spiritual states and absurd pretensions, which the ignorant people they had led astray accepted from them. When the governor saw this, he was alarmed by the spectacle and asked about them. He was told, “They have come to complain.” He said, “Let some of them enter.” Their shaykh entered and spoke at length, complaining about me and claiming that I had mistreated them. Not everything he said reached me, but someone who was present told me that the governor said to them:

“Does he say these things on his own authority, or does he convey them from Allah and His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?”

They replied, “Rather, he conveys them from Allah and His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

He said, “Then what objection can be made to him?”

They said, “We have spiritual states and a path that are accepted on our authority.”

He said, “Then we shall hear what he has to say, and support whoever has the truth on his side.”

They said, “We want you to lend us your support.”

He said, “No. Rather, I support the truth, whether it is with you or with him.”

They asked, “Must he attend?”

He replied, “Yes.”

They repeated this, so he ordered that they be taken out. He then sent me one of his trusted attendants, a truthful and devout man familiar with their misguidance, who explained the situation to me and told me that the governor wanted to expose the reality of these people.

When I learned this, it was put into my heart that this was something Allah intended: to make the religion prevail and expose the condition of these hypocritical innovators, who had spread throughout the lands. Yet I had no wish to wrong or attack them, or to treat them with anything less than the utmost kindness possible. So I sent someone to explain to them the nature of

---

## Page 5800

the situation and convey my warning: “If I attend, it will bring dire consequences upon you and provoke much talk about you. Whoever sits or stands before the spears of the people of faith has brought humiliation upon himself.”

The messenger returned and reported that they had met with their senior shaykhs, who knew the reality of their secrets. These shaykhs had advised them to comply with what they had been commanded: to follow the Sharia and abandon the reprehensible innovations for which they were being censured. Their shaykh who travelled throughout the lands, including the lands of the Turks, Egypt and elsewhere, said:

“Our spiritual states manifest themselves among the Tatars, but not before the Law of Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allāh.”

The messenger also reported that they had removed the shackles from their necks and agreed to comply. Then I was told that some of the governor’s senior attendants had come to them and said that they must attend the appointed gathering.

That night, I sought Allah’s guidance in making my decision, and asked Him for help, victory and guidance. I followed the path of Allah’s servants in such circumstances, until it was put into my heart that I should enter the fire if the need arose, and that it would be cool and safe for whoever followed the faith of Allah’s intimate friend, while burning those who resembled the Sabians and departed from this path.

Remnants of the Sabians—the enemies of Abraham, the leader of those devoted to pure monotheism—were in the region of al-Batā'ih, allied with those among the Christian masses who resembled them. There is an affinity between the Sabians and the misguided worshippers affiliated with this religion, which anyone who knows the manifest truth will recognize. Thus, the extremists among the Qarmatians and the esotericists, such as the Nusayrīs

---

## Page 5801

and the Ismā'īlīs, go on to resemble the Sabian philosophers, then fall into polytheism, and then into denial of the True One, Most High. Excessive veneration of human beings, innovation in worship, and departure from the Sharia partake of their polytheism, each to its corresponding degree—as seen among the heretics who profess divine union and the extremists among the various groups of devotees.

When morning came, I went to the appointed meeting. I preferred not to bring anyone along to support me, but some of the companions who had been present also went. Allah is the One who brings about all causes.

I later learned that they had visited a number of senior emirs and resorted to their customary deception and fabrication, through which they had gained sway over most of the world’s dignitaries and leaders. They claimed, for example, that they possessed spiritual states in which none of Allah’s friends could rival them; that they followed a path unknown to any scholar; that their shaykh stood among the shaykhs as a caliph; and that these lofty accounts gave them precedence over everyone else. They also claimed that anyone who censured them merely adhered to the outward Law without reaching its inner realities and mysteries; that they had one path and he another; and that they were the ones who had reached the very heart of spiritual realization. Such were their ornate and embellished claims.

Owing to their widespread presence throughout the lands and their sway over kings, emirs, and soldiers, as the light of Islam had become obscured and most people had exchanged light for darkness,

---

## Page 5802

and the traces of the Messenger had been effaced in most cities and the reality of Islam had faded under Tatar rule, they had an immense hold on people’s hearts, and people’s faith in them could not be shaken by anyone’s words.

The informant said:

Those great emirs went early that morning and spoke to the sultan’s deputy on their behalf, extolling their supposedly astonishing powers. He related to me various things that had been said. Allah Most High knows best the truth of the matter. The emir sensed that the truth would emerge upon investigation, so he sent the messenger to me a second time, only to learn that we were already on our way.

Many hostile adherents of innovation—including certain groups of students of jurisprudence, ascetic devotees, and followers of those who taught divine union—were working as hard as they could to support them and mobilizing people to assist them at the gathering. When I arrived, I found everyone eagerly awaiting the meeting, looking forward to what would happen and keen to learn the outcome. The sultan’s deputy and other emirs related to me some of the false allegations they had made.

He said, “They claim that you asked them to undergo a test: to heat collars in a fire and put them on.”

I replied, “That is a blatant fabrication. I shall now describe what happened.”

I said to the emir:

“We do not consider it lawful to order anyone to enter a fire, nor is it permissible to obey someone who orders a person to enter a fire. There is an authentic hadith concerning this. These people are lying about this; they are liars and innovators who have wrought corruption in the Muslims’ religious and worldly affairs to an extent known to Allah.”

And I mentioned

---

## Page 5803

how they had deceived various emirs, including the emir known as al-Aydamurī, Qifjaq, the sultan’s deputy, and others. They had also deceived al-Malik al-‘Ādil Kitghā, both during his reign and while he governed Hama, as well as the Master of Arms, the most eminent emir in Egypt. There was not enough time at the gathering to recount all their deceptions.

I described how they had deceived al-Aydamurī: they would send women to discover private matters within his household, then tell him about these matters as though they had received supernatural insight. They promised him kingship and promised to show him the “men of the unseen.” They made long wooden poles and had men walk on them, like a performer juggling glass balls. These men began walking on Mount al-Mazza, while he watched from afar, seeing people moving about the mountain raised above the ground. They took a great deal of money from him, but eventually their deception was exposed to him.

I said to the emir:

“His son, who serves in the army corps, knows about this; he was among those who told me this story. As for Qifjaq, they put a man inside a grave to speak, making him believe that the dead were speaking. In the cemeteries of Bāb al-Saghīr, they brought him to a man whom they claimed was the hairy man from Mount Lebanon. They did not let him approach the man, but kept him at a distance to receive his blessing. They said that the man had requested a large sum of money from him. Qifjaq said, ‘The shaykh perceives hidden things, and he knows that my treasuries do not contain that much.’ Qifjaq drew near him and pulled at the hair, whereupon the goatskin they had glued to his skin came away.”

---

## Page 5804

and I related this to the emir. For this reason, I was told, after the gathering ended and their true nature became clear to the people, Qifjaq’s associates wrote him a letter describing what had happened. He was then serving as the sultan’s deputy in Hama.

I also explained to the emir that they practised various religious innovations, such as wearing shackles around their necks and similar things, and that we had forbidden them to practise innovations contrary to the Sharia. The emir mentioned the hadith concerning innovation and asked me about it. I cited the hadith of al-‘Irbād ibn Sāriya and that of Jābir ibn ‘Abd Allāh. I subsequently cited both at the public gathering, as I shall recount.

I said to the emir:

“I have not put these people to the test. Rather, they claim to possess spiritual states through which they can enter fire, something those who adhere to the Sharia cannot do. They say, ‘We possess these states, which those who adhere to religious law cannot attain. They have no right to object to us; rather, they must accept our practices, whether they accord with religious law or contradict it.’ I have sought the guidance of Allah, glorified be He, concerning this: if they enter the fire, I shall enter it with them. Whoever is burned, whether from our side or theirs, may Allah’s curse be upon him, and he shall be the defeated party. This is to take place after we wash our bodies with vinegar and hot water.”

The emir asked, “Why is that?”

I replied:

“Because they coat their bodies with preparations made from frog fat, the inner rind of bitter oranges, talq stone, and other substances

---

## Page 5805

as part of the tricks known to them. I do not coat my skin with anything. Once they and I have washed with vinegar and hot water, the trick will be nullified and the truth will become clear.”

The emir was astonished at my willingness to plunge into the fire and asked, “Would you do that?”

I replied:

“Yes. I have sought Allah’s guidance concerning this, and He has placed it in my heart to do so. We do not, however, approve of initiating this or similar acts. Extraordinary occurrences are granted to those of Muhammad’s community who follow him inwardly and outwardly—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—only to establish a proof or meet a need. The proof serves to uphold Allah’s religion, while the need concerns indispensable victory and provision through which Allah’s religion is sustained.

“If these people display what they call their signs and proofs, which they claim invalidate Allah’s religion and His revealed law, we must support Allah and His Messenger—may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace—and strive to defend Allah’s religion and His law with whatever we can offer of our lives, our bodies, and our wealth. We may then counter these tricks they display with whatever signs Allah grants us in support. Let it be known that this is like Moses confronting the sorcerers: when they displayed their sorcery, Allah supported Moses with the staff that swallowed up their sorcery.”

The emir began telling the other emirs dining with him about this, and he was delighted. It seemed that they had led him to believe that these people possessed a spiritual state that no one could counter. While I was sitting between him and the senior emir who had arrived from Egypt, al-Hājj Bahādir, at the head of the dining spread, I heard him speaking to him in Turkish. All I understood was his statement, “Today you will see a great battle.” Perhaps that was

## Page 5806

a reply to someone who had spoken to him about them, according to what was reported. Their senior shaykhs arrived and began gently appealing to the emir to bring about a reconciliation and put an end to the affair. The emir replied, “There can be no reconciliation until the truth becomes clear.”

The emir, Bahādir, and I rose and went to the emir’s seat in a corner of the palace. I heard him telling him about Ayyūb the porter in Egypt, the muwallahīn, and similar matters. This indicated that these people enjoyed a lofty reputation with this emir and were well regarded. Allah knows the true circumstances best, for this was related to me.

The emir wanted Bahādir to witness this encounter so that the truth would become clear to him. He was among the most senior and longest-serving emirs, and among those whom the emir held in the greatest esteem. Having only just arrived, he was someone whose goodwill the emir wished to win and whom he wished to honour. He therefore ordered a carpet to be spread in the square.

The Batā’ihiyya had arrived in large numbers, displaying their satanic states: foaming at the mouth, bellowing, shaking their heads and limbs, leaping, crawling, rolling about, and similar objectionable noises and unusual movements. These were contrary to what Luqmān commanded his son when he said:

“Be moderate in your pace and lower your voice.”

When we had taken our seats, with a vast crowd of emirs, scribes, scholars, dervishes, ordinary people, and others present, and their first shaykh—the complainant—had arrived, together with another shaykh

## Page 5807

who called himself the successor of his master Ahmad and rode with two banners. They called him ‘Abd Allāh the Liar, though I had not known this.

Some time earlier, one of their shaykhs had come to me with a pleasant appearance and engaged in their customary begging. I gave him what he requested and did not realize he was lying until he had left me. It troubled me that his deception had escaped my notice until he was gone. Hardly anyone’s deception escapes me; rather, I recognize it from the outset. This continued to trouble me, and I did not see him again until I debated him. He then told me that he was the man who had met me previously. I marvelled at Allah’s gracious providence: He exposed him before the greatest possible gathering, after he had concealed his deception in our private encounter.

When they had assembled, one of their shaykhs, called Hātim, spoke, essentially asking for reconciliation and pardon for the past, declaring repentance, and saying, “We will comply with what has been requested: abandoning these shackles and other innovations, and following the Sharia.”

I said, “As for repentance, it is accepted. Allah Most High says:

‘The Forgiver of sin, the Accepter of repentance, severe in punishment.’

‘and that My punishment is indeed the painful punishment.’”

Their shaykh who had lodged the complaint then began defending their wearing of collars. He mentioned that Wahb ibn Munabbih had related that there was a worshipper among the Children of Israel who placed a collar around his neck—one of the unsubstantiated tales about the Children of Israel.

I made these and similar points forcefully.

The emirs and the people asked me about this, and I said, “Because they have tricks for handling fire, using preparations made from such things as frog fat, bitter-orange peel, and talc.”

and I kept urging him to get up and do it. He reached out as though to take off his shirt, but I said, “Not until you have washed in hot water and vinegar.” He then put on their customary show, saying, “Whoever loves the emir, let him bring some wood”—or he said, “a bundle of firewood.”

I said, “This will only prolong matters and disperse the gathering, without achieving anything. Instead, let a lamp be lit, and after washing I will put my finger and yours into its flame. inside, and we entered. They had asked to repent of their past conduct, and the emir asked me what I required of them. I replied:

“That they follow the Book and the Sunnah. For example, no one should believe that he is not obliged to follow them, that anyone may depart from their rulings, or anything of that kind; nor should he believe that it is permissible to follow a path contrary to any of their rulings, or hold similar views constituting departures from the Book and the Sunnah that entail disbelief. Departures may also warrant execution without constituting disbelief, or warrant fighting a group that refuses compliance without warranting the execution of an individual under one’s control.”

They said, “We are committed to the Book and the Sunnah. Do you object to anything about us besides the collars? We will take them off.”

I replied, “The collars and other such things are not the particular point at issue. The purpose is for all Muslims to obey Allah and His Messenger, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace.”

The emir said, “What, then, does the Book and the Sunnah require of them?”

I replied, “The rulings of the Book and the Sunnah are too numerous to mention in this gathering. What is required, however, is that they make a general commitment to abide by them, and whoever departs from them is to be beheaded”—he repeated this and gestured towards the square.

The intention was that this should be a general ruling applying to everyone. This was a widely known public gathering that had attracted considerable attention, so it would become firmly established among the soldiers, administrative officials, scholars, devout worshippers, these men, and those in authority that whoever departed from the Book and the Sunnah would be beheaded.

---

## Page 5814

I said:

“This includes performing the five daily prayers at their appointed times, as Allah and His Messenger commanded. Some of these men do not pray, while others speak during their prayers. Indeed, yesterday, on Friday afternoon, after they had complained about me, one of them began saying during the prayer itself: ‘O my master Ahmad! Something for Allah’s sake!’ Besides invalidating the prayer, this constitutes associating partners with Allah and invoking someone other than Him while communing with Him—the very communion in which He commanded us to say:

‘You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.’

“This happened yesterday in the presence of their shaykh. When the Muslims objected, the man who said it was told to seek forgiveness, as is their custom with minor sins. Yet their shaykh did not tell him to repeat the prayer. They also shout very loudly during prayer, which is reprehensible and invalidates it.”

He said, “This overcomes them just as sneezing does.”

I replied, “Sneezing is from Allah: Allah loves sneezing and dislikes yawning, and a person cannot prevent it. This shouting, however, is from Satan. They do it deliberately and contrive it, and they are capable of suppressing it.”

After the gathering, someone well acquainted with them told me that during prayer they do things that neither Jews nor Christians do. For example, one says, “I am on the belly of the imam’s wife,” while another says such-and-such about the imam, and other vile remarks of this kind. He also told me that when someone rebukes them for abandoning prayer, they take turns praying. I know that they are allied with devils; they are not

---

## Page 5815

overcome by it as a man may sometimes be overcome by a cry or by weeping, during prayer or otherwise. When they professed adherence to the Quran and Sunnah, while their crowds in the square were displaying their states through their satanic cries and movements, I asked him, “Is this in accordance with the Quran and Sunnah?”

He replied, “This is from Allah—a state that comes upon them.”

I said, “This is from Satan, the accursed. Neither Allah nor His Messenger—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—commanded it, nor does Allah or His Messenger love it.”

He said, “No movement, nor this or that, occurs in the heavens or the earth except by His will and volition.”

I replied, “That concerns divine decree and predestination. Likewise, all the disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience in the world occur by His will and volition. That gives no one any justification for committing them. Rather, these are things Satan has made alluring and the Most Merciful abhors.”

He asked, “Then what will put an end to these states?”

I replied, “These whips sanctioned by the Sacred Law.”

The emir was delighted and laughed, saying, “Yes, by Allah! Whips sanctioned by the Sacred Law will put an end to these satanic states—as has happened to more than one person. Whoever will not submit to the religion through whips sanctioned by the Sacred Law must face the swords of Muhammad.”

I took hold of the emir’s sword and said, “This man is the deputy and servant of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and this sword is the sword of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Whoever departs from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, we shall strike with the sword of Allah.” The emir repeated

---

## Page 5816

these words, and some of them began saying, “Are Jews and Christians tolerated, while we are not?”

I replied, “Jews and Christians are permitted, upon payment of the jizya tax, to retain their religion privately within their homes. But a religious innovator is not permitted to persist in his innovation.” This left them unable to reply.

The truth of the matter is that anyone who openly displays wrongdoing in the abode of Islam is not permitted to continue doing so. Whoever advocates a religious innovation and openly practises it is not allowed to persist, nor is anyone who openly displays wickedness. Likewise, non-Muslims under the covenant of protection are not permitted to display publicly the objectionable practices of their religion. As for others, anyone who is Muslim must fulfil the obligations of Islam and abstain from what it forbids. Anyone who is neither Muslim nor under the covenant of protection is either an apostate, a polytheist, or a heretic whose heresy is manifest.

I also mentioned the condemnation of religious innovators, saying: Muslim narrated in his Sahīh, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Sādiq, from his father Abū Ja‘far al-Bāqir, from Jābir ibn ‘Abd Allāh, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say in his sermons:

“The truest speech is the speech of Allah, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad. The worst matters are those newly introduced into religion, and every religious innovation is misguidance.”

The Sunan collections also report from al-‘Irbād ibn Sāriya, who said:

“The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon to us that brought tears to our eyes and made our hearts tremble. Someone said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, this seems like a farewell exhortation. What, then, do you enjoin upon us?’ He replied, ‘I enjoin you to listen and obey. Whoever among you lives on after me will see much discord. You must therefore adhere to my Sunnah and the sunnah of the upright and rightly guided caliphs

---

## Page 5817

after me. Hold fast to it and cling to it with your very teeth. Beware of newly introduced matters in religion, for every newly introduced matter is a religious innovation, and every religious innovation is misguidance.’” Another version adds: “And all misguidance leads to the Fire.”

He said to me, “Religious innovation is like illicit sexual intercourse,” and related a hadith condemning illicit sexual intercourse. I replied, “This hadith is falsely attributed to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace. Illicit sexual intercourse is a sin, whereas religious innovation is worse than sin. As Sufyān al-Thawrī said, ‘Religious innovation is dearer to Iblīs than sin, for people repent of sin but do not repent of religious innovation.’”

Some of them had said, “We bring people to repentance.” I asked, “What do you make them repent of?”

They replied, “Highway robbery, theft, and the like.”

I said, “Their condition before you brought them to repentance was better than their condition afterward. They were sinners who believed that what they were doing was forbidden, hoped for Allah’s mercy, and repented to Him or intended to repent. But by bringing them to repentance, you have made them misguided polytheists who have departed from the law of Islam, loving what Allah hates and hating what Allah loves.” I explained that these religious innovations which they and others practise are worse than sins.

Addressing the emir and those present, I said, “As for sins, consider what al-Bukhārī narrated in his Sahīh from ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb:

“A man called Himār used to drink wine and would make the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, laugh. Whenever he was brought before the Prophet, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace, he would have him flogged with the prescribed punishment. Once, a man cursed him, saying:

## Page 5818

‘May Allah curse him! How often he is brought before the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace!’ The Prophet, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Do not curse him, for he loves Allah and His Messenger.’”

I said: Here was a man who frequently drank wine. Yet because his beliefs were sound and he loved Allah and His Messenger, the Prophet, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace, testified to this and forbade cursing him.

As for the religious innovator, consider the report recorded by al-Bukhārī and Muslim in their two Sahīhs, from ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib, Abū Sa‘īd al-Khudrī, and others—with portions of their narrations combined:

“The Prophet, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace, was distributing some goods when a man approached him with a prominent brow, a thick beard, a shaved head, and a mark of prostration between his eyes. He said what he said, whereupon the Prophet, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace, declared: ‘From this man’s stock will emerge people whose prayer will make any of you consider his own prayer insignificant, whose fasting will make him consider his own fasting insignificant, and whose recitation will make him consider his own recitation insignificant. They recite the Quran, but it does not pass beyond their throats. They pass out of Islam as an arrow passes through its quarry. If I encounter them, I will certainly kill them as ‘Ād were killed.’”

Another version states:

“If those who fight them knew what Muhammad has promised them, they would cease doing deeds.”

Another version states:

“They are the worst of those slain beneath the sky, while the best of those slain are those whom they kill.”

I said: Despite their abundant prayer, fasting, and recitation, and their devotion to worship and asceticism, the Prophet, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace, commanded that they be killed. ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib and those with him from among the Companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, killed them

---

## Page 5819

because they had departed from the Prophet’s Sunnah and his prescribed way. I believe I also mentioned al-Shāfi‘ī’s statement:

“For a servant to be afflicted with every sin other than associating partners with Allah is better than being afflicted with any of these deviant doctrines.”

When the ugliness of religious innovations in Islam became clear—that they are a greater wrong than fornication, theft, and drinking wine, and that these people practised reprehensible innovations, making their condition worse than that of the fornicator, thief, and wine-drinker—their shaykh, ‘Abd Allāh, began saying:

“Our master, do not assail this august company”—meaning the followers of Ahmad ibn al-Rifā‘ī.

I rebuked him harshly:

He said, “Our master, the Sufis will burn you with their hearts.”

I replied, “Just as the Rāfidah burned me when I intended to ascend to their mountain! Everyone began warning me about them and their evil, while their followers said that they had a secret between themselves and Allah. Yet Allah granted me victory and helped me against them.”

The commanders present already knew the blessings of what Allah had facilitated in the campaign against the Rāfidah in the mountain.

I said to them:

“You who resemble the Rāfidah! You house of lies!”

For their extremism, their association of partners with Allah, and their departure from the prescribed religious law give them some of the same characteristics as the Rāfidah; and their lying is such that they may approach the Rāfidah in this respect or equal them

or even surpass them, for they are among the most deceitful groups. It has even been said of them:
