## Page 5821

Shaykh al-Islām and defender of the Sunnah, peerless in his age and an ocean of knowledge, one of the remaining masters of independent legal reasoning and an authority for later generations, the crown of those who know Allah and the exemplar of discerning scholars, the scholar to whom seekers journey and the choicest of those firmly grounded in knowledge, the leader of ascetics and the ideal of those who strive, the luminous and authoritative imam, the godly scholar qualified for independent legal reasoning, Taqī al-Dīn Abū al-Abbās Ahmad ibn Abd al-Halīm ibn Abd al-Salām ibn Taymiyyah al-Harrānī—may Allah preserve his exalted standing in this world and the next, and grant him ascent to the summit of perfection, joyful at heart and wholly content—was asked:

“Concerning al-Murshidah (The Guide): how did it originate and come to be composed? Is it permissible to read it or not?”

He replied—may Allah Most High have mercy on him:

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Its origins are as follows: it was composed by Abū Abd Allāh Muhammad ibn Abd Allāh ibn al-Tūmart, who assumed the title of al-Mahdī. He had emerged in the Maghreb in the early fifth century AH, some two hundred years ago. He had travelled to Iraq and acquired some knowledge, and he possessed a measure of asceticism and devotion to worship. When he returned to the Maghreb, he went up into its mountains, to a group of Berbers

---

## Page 5822

and others—ignorant people who knew of the religion of Islam only what Allah willed. He taught them prayer, zakāh, fasting, and other prescribed duties of Islam. He considered it permissible to perform various deceptive tricks before them in order to call them to the religion. He would go to graveyards and bury people there, having secretly arranged with them to speak to him when he called them and to testify to whatever he requested. For example, they would testify that he was the Mahdī foretold by the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, whose name would match the Messenger’s name and whose father’s name would match that of the Messenger’s father; that he would fill the earth with equity and justice just as it had been filled with oppression and injustice; and that whoever followed him would prosper, while whoever opposed him would lose, and other such statements.

Once those Berbers believed that the dead spoke to him and testified on his behalf in this way, their faith in him and obedience to his commands grew stronger. He would then collapse the graves upon those buried inside, so that they would die and not expose his deception. He believed that it was permissible to shed their blood even apart from this, and that he was entitled to display this falsehood so that those ignorant people would support and follow him.

Those in the Maghreb and the East who recorded accounts of his life related various stories of this kind about him. They are well known among those familiar with his circumstances.

Among the stories they relate about him is that he secretly arranged with a man to feign madness. This man was a scholar who had memorized the Quran, hadith, and jurisprudence. He presented himself as mad, and people knew him only as a madman. Then one morning he appeared perfectly sane, reciting the Quran, hadith, and jurisprudence. He claimed that he had learned all this in a dream and had been cured of what had afflicted him

---

## Page 5823

, and it is also reported that he told them that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had taught him this. They thus came to think highly of that man.

It is also related that they had a day they called the Day of Distinction, on which he supposedly distinguished between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. Anyone they knew to be one of their allies they counted among the people of Paradise and spared his life; anyone they knew to be one of their enemies they counted among the people of the Fire and deemed it lawful to kill.

He deemed it lawful to shed the blood of many thousands of Mālikīs in the Maghreb who adhered to the Book and the Sunnah, following the school of Mālik and the people of Medina. They studied the Quran, hadith—including the two Sahīh collections, al-Muwatta’, and other works—and jurisprudence according to the school of the people of Medina. Yet he claimed that they likened Allah to His creation and attributed a body to Him, although they did not hold such views. Nor is any follower of Mālik known to have openly professed that Allah resembles His creation or has a body.

On the strength of this interpretation and similar ones, he also deemed it lawful to seize their property and commit other forbidden acts. This resembled the violations against Ahl al-Sunnah wa-l-Jamā‘ah that the Jahmiyyah, who denied the divine attributes—including the philosophers, the Mu‘tazilah, and all other deniers of the attributes—deemed lawful when they subjected people to an inquisition during “the caliphate of al-Ma’mūn.” They openly proclaimed that the Quran was created and that Allah would not be seen in the Hereafter. They denied that Allah has knowledge, power, speech, will, or any other attributes subsisting in His essence.

Anyone who agreed with them in this denial of the attributes had his life and property protected by them. They appointed him to public offices, granted him a stipend from the public treasury, accepted his testimony, and ransomed him from

---

## Page 5824

captivity. Anyone who did not agree with them that the Quran was created, or with the other innovations that followed from this, they killed, imprisoned, beat, or denied a stipend from the public treasury. They would not appoint him to any public office, accept his testimony, or ransom him from the disbelievers.

They would say, “This man likens Allah to His creation; this man attributes a body to Him,” because he said that Allah would be seen in the Hereafter, that the Quran was the speech of Allah, uncreated, that Allah rose over the Throne, and similar things. This inquisition against the Muslims continued for ten-odd years, during the latter part of al-Ma’mūn’s caliphate and the caliphates of his brother al-Mu‘tasim and al-Wāthiq ibn al-Mu‘tasim. Then Allah Most High lifted this affliction from the community during the reign of al-Mutawakkil ‘alā Allāh, whose descendants Allah made to constitute most of the Abbasid caliphs, rather than the descendants of those who had subjected Ahl al-Sunnah to the inquisition. Al-Mutawakkil ordered that the inquisition be ended, that the Book and the Sunnah be openly proclaimed, and that the authentic reports from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the Companions, and the Successors affirming the divine attributes and rejecting their denial be transmitted.

Those Jahmiyyah who denied the divine attributes had gone so far in altering the religion that they would write on the coverings of the Kaaba, “There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise,” rather than saying, “And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.” They would also test people with the words of Allah Most High:

“There is nothing like unto Him.”

If they continued, “And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing,” they would rebuke them.

The position of the early generations of this community and its imams is that Allah is to be described as He has described Himself and as His Messenger has described Him, without distortion or denial, and without

---

## Page 5825

specifying how His attributes are or likening them to those of creation. They do not deny of Allah what He has affirmed of Himself, nor do they liken His attributes to those of His creation. Rather, they know that nothing is like Allah—in His essence, His attributes, or His actions. Just as His essence does not resemble other essences, His attributes do not resemble other attributes. Allah Most High sent the messengers, who described Him through detailed affirmation and general negation.

The enemies of the messengers—the Jahmiyyah, the philosophers, and others like them—described Him through detailed negation and general affirmation.

For Allah, Glorified and Exalted, has stated in His Book that He knows all things; that He has power over all things; that He is the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all; that He is the Almighty, the All-Wise; that He is the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful; and that He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. He has stated that He loves the God-fearing, those who do good, and the patient; that He does not love corruption and does not approve of disbelief for His servants; that He is pleased with the believers and they are pleased with Him; that He is angry with the disbelievers and curses them; that good words ascend to Him and righteous deeds raise them; that He spoke directly to Moses; and that the Trustworthy Spirit brought the Quran down from Allah to His Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

As He says:

“Say, ‘The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth.’”

The Holy Spirit is Gabriel, as He says in another verse:

“Say, ‘Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel—it is he who brought it down upon your heart by Allah’s permission, confirming what came before it.’”

And He Most High says:

“The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart, so that you may be one of the warners.”

And He Most High says:

“On that Day, some faces will be radiant, looking at their Lord.”

And He Most High says:

“For those who do good is the finest reward, and more.”

---

## Page 5826

And it is authentically reported in Sahīh Muslim, on the authority of Suhayb, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, a caller will announce, ‘O people of Paradise, Allah has made you a promise that He wishes to fulfil for you.’ They will say, ‘What is it? Has He not brightened our faces, made our scales heavy, admitted us to Paradise, and protected us from the Fire?’” He continued, “Then the veil will be lifted, and they will look upon Him. He will have given them nothing dearer to them than looking upon Him; this is the ‘more.’”

It has also been widely transmitted from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the authentic hadith collections that he said:

“You will see your Lord just as you see the moon on the night when it is full, having no difficulty seeing Him.”

And that the people said, “O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?” He said, “Do you have any difficulty seeing the sun in a clear sky, with no clouds obscuring it?” They said, “No.” He said, “Do you have any difficulty seeing the moon in a clear sky, with no clouds obscuring it?” They said, “No.” He said, “You will indeed see your Lord just as you see the sun and the moon.”

Thus he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, likened the act of seeing to the act of seeing; he did not liken the One seen to the things seen. For the servants cannot encompass Allah in knowledge, nor can their vision comprehend Him. As He Most High says:

“Vision does not comprehend Him, but He comprehends all vision.”

A number of the early generations and scholars have stated that “comprehension” means encompassing. Thus the servants will see Allah Most High with their own eyes, but they will not encompass Him. These and similar matters are among those that Allah and His Messenger have told us.

And He Most High says by way of negation:

“There is nothing like Him.”

“So do not set up rivals to Allah.”

---

## Page 5827

“Do you know of any equal to Him?”

“And there is none comparable to Him.”

In these verses, He makes clear that Allah has no equal, no rival, no likeness, and no peer.

Whoever says, “Allah’s knowledge is like my knowledge, His power is like my power, His speech is like my speech, His will, love, pleasure, and anger are like my will, love, pleasure, and anger, His rising over the Throne is like my rising, His descent is like my descent, or His coming is like my coming,” or anything similar, has likened Allah to His creation and made Him their equal. Exalted is Allah above what they say! Such a person is misguided, wicked, and an advocate of falsehood—indeed, a disbeliever.

Whoever says, “Allah has no knowledge, power, speech, will, hearing, sight, love, pleasure, anger, rising over the Throne, coming, or descent,” has denied Allah’s most beautiful names and most exalted attributes and deviated concerning His names and signs. Such a person is misguided, wicked, and an advocate of falsehood—indeed, a disbeliever.

Rather, the position of the leading scholars and the early generations is to affirm the attributes while rejecting any likeness to created beings: affirmation without likening Him to creation, and declaring Him free of imperfection without denying His attributes. As Nu'aym ibn Hammād al-Khuzā'ī, al-Bukhārī’s teacher, said:

“Whoever likens Allah to His creation has disbelieved, and whoever denies what Allah has described Himself with has disbelieved. Nothing with which Allah has described Himself, or His Messenger has described Him, constitutes likening Him to creation.”

What further clarifies this is that Allah Most High has told us that in Paradise there are water, milk, wine, honey, meat, fruit, silk, gold, silver, and other things. Ibn 'Abbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said, “Of what is in Paradise, nothing is found in this world but the names.” Thus, if

---

## Page 5828

the created things in Paradise share names with the created things in this world, while their realities are not alike, how could the Creator be like a created being merely because He shares a name with it?

Allah Most High has described Himself as All-Hearing and All-Seeing, and has described the human being as hearing and seeing; yet the one is not like the other. He has described Himself as living, and some of His servants as living; yet the one is not like the other. He has described Himself as compassionate and merciful, and His Prophet as compassionate and merciful; yet the one is not like the other. He has described Himself as knowing and forbearing, and some of His servants as knowing and forbearing; yet the one is not like the other. He has called Himself the King, and has called some of His servants kings; yet the one is not like the other.

Such examples abound in the Quran and Sunnah. This, then, was the position of the early generations of the Muslim community and its leading scholars, including the imams of the schools of law, such as Abū Hanīfah, Mālik, al-Shāfi‘ī, Ahmad, and others: affirmation without likening Him to creation, and declaring Him free of imperfection without denying His attributes. They neither adopted the position of those who deny His attributes nor that of those who liken the Creator to created beings. This is the way of the messengers and those who believe in them.

As for the philosophers and others like them who oppose the messengers—may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon them—they describe the Lord Most High through “negative attributes”: He is not this, not that, not such-and-such. They do not describe Him with any affirmative attributes, but only through negations that could equally describe what does not exist. Thus, their description corresponds to the nonexistent, so there remains no

---

## Page 5829

distinction between what they affirm and what does not exist. Yet they say, “He exists; He is not nonexistent.” Thus they contradict themselves, affirming Him in one respect and denying Him in another.

They also say, “He is absolute existence, distinguished by no attribute.” Yet people know that what is absolute cannot exist in reality, for nothing that exists is absolute, without any particular identity or distinction from anything else. Such a thing exists only in a person’s mental conceptions: one conceives of something absolute, even though it has no reality outside the mind. Thus these philosophizing Jahmīs who deny the divine attributes do not acknowledge the Creator—glorified and exalted is He—as existing apart from His creation. Rather, they either make Him an absolute conceived in people’s minds, make Him indwell created things, or say that He is the very existence of created things.

It is known that Allah existed before He created His creatures. When He created them, He did not enter into them, nor did He bring them into Himself. Nothing of His essence is within His creatures, and nothing of His creatures is within His essence. This is what the Quran and Sunnah indicate, and what the early generations of the Muslim community and its leading scholars unanimously affirmed.

The Jahmī deniers of the divine attributes among the philosophers, the Mu‘tazilah, and others—who subjected the Muslims to the ordeal mentioned earlier—held this misguided position. When Allah Most High granted the people of the Sunnah and the community ascendancy and victory, this denial remained in the hearts of many of their followers. They consequently began to appear at times alongside the esotericist Qarmatian Rāfidah, at times alongside the Jahmī proponents of union between God and creation, and at times to agree with them

---

## Page 5830

in holding that He is absolute existence, going no further than this. This was also the belief of the author of al-Murshidah (The Guide), as he explicitly stated in a lengthy book in which he explained his position on this matter. There he stated that Allah Most High is absolute existence, as Ibn Sīnā, Ibn Sab‘īn, and others like them maintain.

For this reason, his al-Murshidah does not mention the belief set forth by the leading scholars of knowledge and religion among the people of the Sunnah and the community: scholars of hadith, jurisprudence, Sufism, speculative theology, and others among the followers of the four imams and beyond. This belief is stated by the leading Hanafī, Mālikī, Shāfi‘ī, and Hanbalī scholars; the speculative theologians among the Kullābīs, Ash‘arīs, Karrāmīs, and others; the masters of Sufism and asceticism; and the scholars of hadith. All of them agree that Allah Most High is living, knows by His knowledge, and is powerful by His power.

As Allah Most High says:

“And they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills.”

And He says:

“But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you: He sent it down with His knowledge.”

And He says:

“No female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge.”

And He says:

“Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength?”

And He says:

“And the heaven We built with strength”—that is, with power.

In the Sahīh collection, it is reported: “The Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—used to teach his Companions to seek Allah’s guidance in all matters, just as he would teach them a surah of the Quran. He would say:

---

## Page 5831

‘When any of you intends to undertake a matter, let him pray two units of prayer other than the obligatory prayer. Then let him say:

O Allah, I seek Your guidance through Your knowledge, and I seek ability through Your power, and I ask You of Your immense bounty. You have power, and I have none; You know, and I do not; and You are the Knower of all unseen things. O Allah, if You know that this matter—and he should name it—is good for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affairs, then decree it for me, make it easy for me, and bless it for me. But if You know that this matter is bad for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affairs, then turn it away from me and turn me away from it. Decree what is good for me wherever it may be, then make me content with it.’”

The four imams and all the others mentioned agree that Allah Most High will be seen in the Hereafter and that the Quran is the speech of Allah. Yet the author of al-Murshidah mentions none of the affirmations upheld by the various groups among the people of the Sunnah and the community. Nor does he mention belief in the prophethood of the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—or in the Last Day and what the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—reported concerning Paradise and Hell, resurrection and reckoning, the trial of the grave, the Cistern, and the Prophet’s intercession—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—for those guilty of major sins. All these fundamentals are agreed upon among the people of the Sunnah and the community, and their scholars customarily include them in concise statements of creed. Instead, he restricted its contents to what accords with his foundational position: that Allah is absolute existence. This is the position of the philosophers and the Jahmīs

## Page 5832

and the Shia and others like them, whose views the various groups of the people of the Sunnah and the community—including the adherents of the four schools and others—have unanimously rejected as false, judging them to be misguided.

In it, he presented the statements of those who deny the divine attributes, without mentioning a single affirmative attribute of Allah Most High. At its beginning, he claimed that every legally accountable person is obliged to know these things. Yet the imams agree that Muslims are obliged only to fulfil what Allah and His Messenger have made obligatory. No one may impose upon Muslims anything that Allah and His Messenger have not made obligatory. Some of his statements concern matters mentioned by Allah and His Messenger, which must therefore be believed. Others have not been mentioned by Allah, His Messenger, or any of the early generations and imams. People are therefore not obliged to profess what Allah has not obliged them to profess.

A person may make a statement that is true, yet not everyone is obliged to profess it, nor may he oblige people to do so. How much more objectionable is this when the statement contains falsehood? The negations he sets out contain both truth and falsehood: the truth must be followed, and the falsehood must be avoided. We have discussed this at length in a substantial book.

We have also explained why he called his followers al-Muwahhidūn (“those who affirm Allah’s oneness”). This is among the things Muslims have objected to, for the entire community of Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—affirms Allah’s oneness, and none of those who affirm His oneness will remain in the Fire forever.

## Page 5847

Mu‘ādh, tell me: if you passed by my grave, would you prostrate before it?” He replied, “No.” He said, “Prostration is proper only for Allah”—or words to that effect.

If it is impermissible to prostrate before the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, whether alive or dead, or before his grave, how could it be permissible to prostrate before anyone else?

For prostration may only be performed in a prescribed manner: prostration during prayer, prostration for forgetfulness, prostration upon recitation, and—according to one of the two scholarly views—prostration of gratitude.

As for prostrating immediately after prayer without a reason, the scholars have disapproved of it. Rather, this is like those who prostrate to the sun at sunrise and sunset, or to certain stars and idols, and say, “It is for Allah.”

severe punishment for the perpetrator, sufficient to deter him from such corruption, especially if they involve the children in acts of indecency and other wrongdoing. Section

As for “vows to the dead”—whether prophets, shaykhs, or others—or to their graves or those residing at their graves, such vows constitute polytheism and disobedience to Allah Most High, whether what is vowed is financial support, gold, or anything else. This resembles making vows to churches, monks, and temples of idols.

It is established in the Sahīh that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Whoever vows to obey Allah must obey Him, and whoever vows to disobey Allah must not disobey Him.”

The scholars agree that a vow to commit disobedience must not be fulfilled. Rather, according to one of the two scholarly opinions, the person who made it must offer the expiation for an oath. This applies when the vow is made to Allah. If, however, the vow is made to someone other than Allah, it is like swearing by someone other than Allah, and this is polytheism. The person must therefore seek Allah’s forgiveness for it; such a vow must not be fulfilled, and no expiation is due. Whoever gives money in charity to the poor and devout will have his reward with the Lord of the worlds.

---

## Page 5850

“It brings no good; it merely extracts something from the miser.”

If a person does make a vow, he must fulfill whatever it entails of obedience to Allah, such as prayer, charity, fasting, and pilgrimage, but not what does not constitute obedience to Allah Most High.

Whoever does not desist from this must receive a severe punishment that deters him and others like him who persist in corruption and defiance.

## Page 5851

He also said:

“Whoever swears by anyone other than Allah has associated partners with Him.”

Thus, whoever swears by his shaykh, his shaykh’s tomb, his life, or his right over Allah; by kings, the sultan’s favor, the sword, or the Kaaba; by his father, his father’s tomb, or anything similar—such swearing is prohibited, and his oath is not binding, by agreement of the Muslims.

Section

As for someone saying to a person who reproves him, “You are a follower of the religious law,” this is a correct statement. If, however, he means by this that he does not follow the religious law, or is not obliged to follow it, and that “I am not bound to follow it,” then the term “religious law” has come to have three meanings in common usage: the revealed law, the interpreted law, and the altered law.

---

## Page 5852

As for the revealed law, it is what is established from the Messenger in the Quran and Sunnah. All generations, earlier and later, must follow this law, and the best of Allah’s allies are those who follow it most completely. Whoever does not commit himself to this law, impugns it, or considers it permissible for anyone to depart from it is called upon to repent; if he repents, well and good; otherwise, he is put to death.

As for the interpreted law, it consists of rulings that scholars have reached through independent reasoning. It is permissible to follow one of the imams in such matters, but people are not obliged to adhere to the position of any particular imam.

As for the altered law, it consists of fabricated hadiths, distorted interpretations, misleading innovations introduced into the religious law that are not part of it, and judging by other than what Allah has revealed. It is not permissible for anyone to follow these or anything similar.

Judges rule only on the basis of outward evidence, while Allah Most High deals with what is hidden within. A judge’s ruling does not change the true nature of things. It is authentically reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“You bring your disputes before me, and some of you may be more eloquent in presenting their case than others. I judge only on the basis of what I hear. If I award anyone something belonging to his brother, he must not take it, for I am only allotting him a piece of the Fire.”

These are the words of the leader of judges and the master of Adam’s descendants.

---

## Page 5853

He, peace and blessings be upon him, also said:

“When a judge exercises independent judgment and reaches the correct decision, he has two rewards; when he exercises independent judgment but errs, he has one reward.”

He also said:

“Judges are of three kinds: two are in the Fire and one is in Paradise. A man who knows the truth and judges accordingly is in Paradise. A man who judges between people in ignorance is in the Fire. A man who knows the truth but judges contrary to it is in the Fire.”

Whoever departs from the revealed law with which Allah sent Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, imagining that he is following “reality,” resembles the polytheists who reject the messengers. The term “reality” may refer to “the reality of creation,” “reality based on religious innovation,” or “reality grounded in revealed law.”

“The reality of creation” consists in believing in divine decree and predestination, and that Allah is the Creator, Lord, and Sovereign of all things. This must be believed, but it may not be invoked as a justification. Rather, Allah has the conclusive argument against us. Whoever invokes predestination as an argument has an invalid argument, and whoever invokes predestination to excuse his sins has an unacceptable excuse.

As for “reality based on religious innovation,” it consists in pursuing the path to Allah, glorified and exalted be He, on the basis of the spiritual taste, ecstasy, love, and desire that arise in a person’s heart, without following the Book and Sunnah. This is like the way of the Christians: sometimes they worship other than Allah, and sometimes they worship without Allah’s command—like the Christians who associated partners with Allah and took their scholars

---

## Page 5854

and monks as lords besides Allah, as well as the Messiah, son of Mary, and invented monasticism. Thus they associated with Allah that for which He had sent down no authority and instituted as religion what Allah had not permitted.

As for the religion of the Muslims, it is as Allah Most High says:

“So whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and associate no one in the worship of his Lord.”

He Most High also says:

“To test you as to which of you is best in deeds.”

Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyād said: “The most sincere and the most correct.” They asked: “What is meant by the most sincere and the most correct?”

He said: “If a deed is sincere but not correct, it will not be accepted; and if it is correct but not sincere, it will not be accepted. It must be both sincere and correct. Sincerity means that it is done for Allah, and correctness means that it accords with the Sunnah.”

For this reason, ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb used to say in his supplication:

“O Allah, make all my deeds righteous, make them purely for Your sake, and let no one else have any share in them.”

As for “reality grounded in revealed law,” it consists in putting into practice what Allah and His Messenger have prescribed, such as sincerity towards Allah, reliance upon Allah, fear of Allah, gratitude to Allah, patience with Allah’s judgment, love for Allah and His Messenger, hatred for the sake of Allah and His Messenger, and other things that Allah and His Messenger love. These are the realities of the people of faith and the path of those endowed with spiritual knowledge.

---

## Page 5855

Section

Enjoining what is right—the truth with which Allah sent His Messenger—and forbidding what is wrong—all forms of religious innovation and wickedness that oppose that truth—are indeed among the greatest obligations and finest acts of obedience. Indeed, this is the path of the religious leaders and spiritual masters whose example we follow in this regard.

Allah Most High says:

“Let there be among you a group who call to goodness, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong. It is they who will be successful.”

This is the verse cited as evidence that spiritual masters are to be followed in matters of religion. Whoever does not enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong is neither a spiritual master nor someone whose example should be followed.

Section

As for wearing the robe that some spiritual masters confer upon their disciples, this practice has no basis established by valid evidence from the Quran and Sunnah. Neither the early spiritual masters nor most of the later ones used to clothe their disciples in it. However, a group of

---

## Page 5856

later spiritual masters approved of it and regarded it as commendable. Some have cited as evidence the report that “the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, clothed Umm Khālid bint Khālid ibn Sa‘īd ibn al-‘Ās in a garment and said to her, ‘Sinnā!’” Sinnā means “beautiful” in the language of Abyssinia. She had been born in Abyssinia, which is why he addressed her in that language. They also cited the hadith concerning “the cloak that a woman wove for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. One of the Companions asked him for it, and he gave it to him. The Companion said, ‘I wanted it to be my shroud.’”

Neither of these two hadiths provides evidence for the manner in which they practise this. Giving someone clothing to wear is like giving him anything else that benefits him. Taking a garment from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to seek its blessing is like taking some of his hair to seek its blessing. This is not the same as wearing a garment or cap as an expression of following someone and taking him as an example. Rather, in some respects, the practice resembles the robes of honour that kings bestow upon those whom they appoint to office, serving as insignia and marks of authority and distinction. Hence they describe this as an honour. At most, this and similar practices may be classed as permissible acts. If accompanied by a righteous intention, they become commendable on that account. But to regard this as a sunnah and a path to Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is not justified.

As for a group’s affiliation with a particular spiritual master, there is no doubt that people need someone from whom to learn faith and the Quran, just as the Companions learned them from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Successors learned them from the Companions. It is through this that one follows the forerunners

---

## Page 5857

who came first, faithfully following their example. Just as a person has someone to teach him the Quran and similar subjects, so too he has someone to teach him the inward and outward aspects of religion. This need not be confined to any particular person, nor does it require affiliation with a particular spiritual master. Anyone who imparts religious benefit to another is his teacher in that respect. Likewise, any deceased person whose sayings, deeds, or legacy reach someone and benefit him in his religion is his teacher in that respect. Thus, the earlier generations of this community are the teachers of those who succeed them, generation after generation. No one may affiliate himself with a spiritual master and make following him the basis of loyalty and enmity.

Rather, he must show loyalty to all people of faith and all who are known for piety, whether spiritual masters or others. He must not single anyone out for greater loyalty unless that person’s greater faith and piety become apparent to him. He should therefore give precedence to those whom Allah Most High and His Messenger have given precedence, and favour those whom Allah and His Messenger have favoured. Allah Most High says:

“O mankind, indeed We have created you from a male and a female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.”

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“No Arab has any superiority over a non-Arab, nor any non-Arab over an Arab; no black person has any superiority over a white person, nor any white person over a black person, except through piety.”

---

## Page 5858

Section

As for someone saying, “You belong to such-and-such a spiritual master, and he is your master in this world and the Hereafter,” this is a reprehensible innovation, both because he has devoted himself to someone other than Allah and because the statement “your master in this world and the Hereafter” has no basis in reality.

If he means that they will be together in Paradise, that is for Allah to decide, not him. If he means that the master’s intercession on his behalf will be accepted, no one intercedes for another except by Allah Most High’s permission. If He permits his intercession on that person’s behalf, it will be accepted; otherwise, it will not. Merely saying, “You are my spiritual master in the Hereafter,” does not make him an intercessor for the speaker—and this is assuming that the master is among those entitled to intercede. It has already been explained that the foremost of the messengers and of all creation will not intercede until Allah permits him to do so, after others have declined. How many claim to be spiritual masters, yet have deficiencies in knowledge and faith known only to Allah Most High!

As for the saying:

“If any of you expected good from a stone, Allah would benefit him through it,”

this is a saying of polytheists and fabricators of lies. Idol-worshippers expected good from their idols, yet both they and their idols became fuel for Hell, as Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, you and what

---

## Page 5859

you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; you will enter it.”

But the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Allah Most High says: ‘I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself. If he remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than theirs. If he draws near to Me by a handspan, I draw near to him by an arm’s length. If he draws near to Me by an arm’s length, I draw near to him by an armspan. If he comes to Me walking, I come to him running.’”

Whoever can find guidance without affiliating himself with a particular spiritual master has no need to do so. Such affiliation is not recommended for him; rather, it is discouraged. But if he cannot worship Allah as He has commanded except through such affiliation—for example, if he lives somewhere where guidance, knowledge, faith, and religious practice are weak, and those who would teach and discipline him will do so only if he affiliates himself with their master—or if affiliation with a master would increase his religious commitment and knowledge, then he should do whatever is best for his religion. Such a situation generally arises only through his own negligence; otherwise, if he sought guidance in the proper way, he would find it.

As for affiliation that divides Muslims, abandoning communal unity and concord for division, following the path of innovation, and departing from the Sunnah and adherence to it, this is prohibited. Whoever does so incurs sin and thereby departs from obedience to Allah and His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him.

---

## Page 5860

Section

As for the statement, “Allah is pleased when the spiritual masters are pleased and angry when they are angry,” this does not apply to all spiritual masters, nor is it exclusive to them. Rather, whoever is in accord with Allah—pleased with what pleases Allah and angered by what angers Allah—Allah is pleased when he is pleased and angry when he is angry, whether he is a spiritual master or someone else. Any spiritual master who is not like this does not possess this quality.

An example is what the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Abū Bakr al-Siddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, following an exchange between him and Suhayb, Khabbāb, Bilāl, and others concerning Abū Sufyān ibn Harb. Abū Sufyān had passed by them, and they said:

“The swords have not taken their full toll on Allah’s enemy.”

Abū Bakr said, “Do you say this about the chief of Quraysh?” He then went to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and told him what had happened. The Prophet said:

“Perhaps you have angered them, Abū Bakr. If you have angered them, you have indeed angered your Lord”—or words to that effect.

The narrator said: Abū Bakr then went out to them and asked, “My brothers, have I angered you?”

They replied, “No; may Allah forgive you, Abū Bakr.”

Their anger was for Allah’s sake.

In Sahīh al-Bukhārī, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is reported to have said:

“He says

---

## Page 5861

—Allah Most High—‘Whoever shows enmity to a close servant of Mine has challenged Me to war. Nothing by which My servant draws near to Me compares to what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts of worship until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he grasps, and his foot with which he walks. Through Me he hears, through Me he sees, through Me he grasps, and through Me he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give him, and if he seeks My protection, I will surely protect him. I do not hesitate over anything I do as I hesitate over taking the soul of My believing servant: he dislikes death, and I dislike causing him distress, yet he must face it.’”

Allah loves this believer who draws near to Him through voluntary acts after fulfilling the obligatory duties, because he has done what Allah loves; the recompense corresponds to the deed.

Allah Most High says:

“Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him.”

In truth, the servant at whose pleasure Allah is pleased, and at whose anger He is angry, is himself pleased with what pleases Allah and angered by what angers Him. Let these two serve as examples of someone who loves what Allah loves, hates what Allah hates, is pleased with what Allah is pleased with because it pleases Allah, and is angered by what angers Him. Yet no human being can maintain this continually. Even the most perfect of creation must sometimes feel ordinary human anger and pleasure. Hence the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said in an authentic hadith:

“O Allah, I am only human and become angry as humans do. So any Muslim whom I have insulted or cursed, though he did not deserve it—make that a blessing and a purification for him, and a means of drawing him near to You on the Day of Resurrection.”

---

## Page 5862

The Prophet’s words to Abu Bakr, peace and blessings be upon him—“If you have angered them, you have indeed angered your Lord”—concerned a particular incident: Abu Bakr’s anger was on account of Abu Sufyān, whereas their anger was for Allah’s sake. Otherwise, Abu Bakr’s rank is higher than that.

In sum, religious teachers, rulers, and others are to be obeyed when they command obedience to Allah and His Messenger. If they command anything contrary to that, they are not to be obeyed, for no created being may be obeyed in disobedience to the Creator. No one is infallible except the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. This applies to a religious teacher whose knowledge and practice of the religion are established. As for someone whose religious innovation or wickedness is manifest, it is more necessary to denounce his innovation and wickedness than to obey his commands. Yet if he or anyone else commands what Allah and His Messenger have commanded, obedience to Allah and His Messenger is obligatory. Such obedience is incumbent upon everyone in every circumstance, whoever may be enjoining it.

Section: (*)

As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, “A person will be with those whom he loves,” it is among the most authentic hadiths.

Anas said:
“After embracing Islam, nothing brought the Muslims as much joy as this hadith. I love the Messenger of Allah, Abu Bakr, and ‘Umar, and I hope to be gathered

## Page 5863

with them, even though my deeds do not equal theirs.”

Likewise, “The strongest bonds of Islam are loving for Allah’s sake and hating for Allah’s sake.” However, this requires a person to love what Allah loves and those who love Allah. Thus, one loves all of Allah’s prophets because Allah loves them, and loves everyone known to have died in faith and piety, for these are Allah’s close friends, and Allah loves them. These include those whom the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, testified would enter Paradise, as well as others who participated at Badr and took the Pledge of Divine Pleasure.

Whoever the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, testified would enter Paradise, we likewise testify will enter Paradise. As for someone for whom he gave no such testimony, a group of scholars said: “We do not testify that he will enter Paradise, nor do we testify that Allah loves him.”

Another group said: “Rather, if a person’s faith and piety become widely known and the Muslims agree in praising him, we testify that he will enter Paradise. Such people include ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Azīz, al-Hasan al-Basrī, Sufyān al-Thawrī, Abu Hanīfah, Mālik, al-Shāfi‘ī, Ahmad, al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyād, Abu Sulaymān al-Dārānī, Ma‘rūf al-Karkhī, ‘Abd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak—may Allah be pleased with them—and others.”

For it is related in al-Sahīh:

“A funeral procession passed by the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the people spoke well of the deceased. He said, ‘It is assured! It is assured!’ Another funeral procession passed by, and they spoke ill of the deceased. He said, ‘It is assured! It is assured!’

“They asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, what do you mean by saying, “It is assured! It is assured”?’

“He said, ‘You spoke well of this deceased person, so I said that Paradise was assured for them. You spoke ill of the other deceased person, so I said that the Fire was assured for them.’

“He was asked:

---

## Page 5864

‘On what grounds, O Messenger of Allah?’

He replied, ‘On account of the good and bad testimony.’”

Once this is understood, many of those renowned as shaykhs in these times may have such ignorance, misguidance, disobedience, and sins as would prevent people from bearing such testimony on their behalf. Indeed, they may include hypocrites and openly sinful people, just as they include Allah’s pious close friends, His righteous servants, and His successful party. Likewise, both kinds are found among those who are not shaykhs—in Paradise—and among merchants, farmers, and other such groups.

Since this is so, whoever seeks to be gathered with a shaykh whose ultimate fate he does not know is misguided. Rather, he must hold to what he knows and ask Allah to gather him with His Prophet and His righteous servants. As Allah Most High says:

“But if you both support one another against him, then surely Allah is his Protector, as are Gabriel and the righteous believers.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Your only allies are Allah, His Messenger, and the believers—those who establish prayer, give zakah, and bow in worship.”

“Whoever takes Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as allies—surely it is the party of Allah that will prevail.”

Accordingly, whoever loves a shaykh who contravenes the Sharia will be with him; if that shaykh enters the Fire, he will be with him.

It is well known that shaykhs who contravene the Book and the Sunnah are people of misguidance and ignorance. Whoever is with them will therefore share the fate of the people of misguidance and ignorance. As for those who are among Allah’s pious close friends, such as Abu Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Uthmān

---

## Page 5865

and ‘Alī and others—loving them is among the firmest bonds of faith and the greatest good deeds of the pious. Even if someone loves a man because of the goodness he sees in him, which Allah and His Messenger love, Allah will reward him for loving what Allah and His Messenger love, even though he does not know that man’s true inward state. The foundation is love of Allah and love of what Allah loves. Whoever loves Allah and loves what Allah loves is among Allah’s close friends.

Many people claim such love without truly living up to it. Allah Most High says:

“Say, ‘If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins.’”

One of the early generations said: “Some people during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, claimed that they loved Allah, so Allah revealed this verse.”

Loving Allah, His Messenger, and His pious servants requires doing what Allah loves and abandoning what He dislikes. People differ greatly in this: whoever has a greater share of it has a higher rank with Allah.

As for someone who loves another out of personal desire—for some worldly benefit he obtains from him, a need that person fulfils for him, money he gains through him, partisan attachment to him, or similar things—this is not love for Allah’s sake. Rather, it is love driven by one’s own desires. It is this love that leads those who harbour it into disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience.

How many people claim to love shaykhs for Allah’s sake! If they truly loved them for Allah’s sake, they would obey Allah, the One

---

## Page 5866

for whose sake they loved them. When someone is loved for the sake of another, love for him is subordinate to love for that other. How can someone who does not love Allah love anyone for Allah’s sake? And how can someone love Allah while turning away from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and from Allah’s path?

How many people love shaykhs, kings, or others and take them as rivals to Allah, loving them as they love Allah! The difference between loving for Allah’s sake and loving others alongside Allah is clear. Those who associate partners with Allah take rivals whom they love as they love Allah, whereas those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah. The people of faith love in this way because the foundation of their love is love of Allah. Whoever loves Allah loves those who love Him and those whom Allah loves. The beloved of one’s beloved is also beloved, and whoever is beloved to Allah loves Allah. Thus, whoever loves Allah is loved by those who love Allah.

As for those who associate partners with Allah, they take rivals or intercessors whom they invoke besides Allah. Allah Most High says:

“You have certainly come to Us alone, just as We created you the first time, leaving behind all that We bestowed upon you. We do not see with you those intercessors of yours whom you claimed were Allah’s partners in your affairs. The ties between you have been severed, and all that you used to claim has vanished from you.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Why should I not worship the One who created me, and to whom you will be returned?”

“Should I take gods besides Him? If the Most Merciful intends harm for me, their intercession will avail me nothing, nor can they rescue me.”

“I would then indeed be

in manifest error.”

“I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me.”

Allah Most High says:

Allah Most High also says:

“It is not for any human being to whom Allah has given the Scripture, judgment, and prophethood to then say to people, ‘Worship me instead of Allah.’ Rather, ‘Be devoted servants of the Lord through your teaching of the Scripture and through your study of it.’

“Nor would he command you to take the angels and prophets as lords. Would he command you to disbelieve after you have submitted to Allah?”

Allah Most High sent the messengers and revealed the Scriptures so that all religion would be devoted to Allah alone. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in an authentic hadith:

“We prophets share one religion.”

Thus, the religion is one, even though the prescribed laws and ways differ. Allah Most High says:

“We never sent a messenger before you without revealing to him: ‘There is no god but Me, so worship Me.’”

He Most High also says:

“Ask those of Our messengers whom We sent before you: Did We appoint any gods besides the Most Merciful to be worshipped?”

Allah Most High also says:

“We certainly sent a messenger to every nation, saying, ‘Worship Allah and shun false objects of worship.’”

Ever since Allah sent Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, He accepts from anyone whom the call has reached only the religion with which He sent him. His call extends to all created beings. Allah Most High says:

“We have sent you only to all mankind.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“No Jew or Christian of this community hears of me and then fails to believe

## Page 5868

in me without entering the Fire.”

Allah Most High says:

“My mercy encompasses all things. I shall ordain it for those who are mindful of Me, give zakat, and believe in Our signs.”

“Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find described in the Torah and the Gospel they possess. He commands them to do what is right and forbids them to do what is wrong, makes good things lawful for them and foul things unlawful, and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that bound them. Those who believe in him, honour him, support him, and follow the light sent down with him—it is they who will prosper.”

“Say, ‘O mankind, I am the Messenger of Allah to you all. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no god but Him; He gives life and causes death. All creation must therefore follow Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, worshipping Allah alone and worshipping Him according to the law of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and no other. Allah Most High says:

“Then We set you upon a prescribed way in matters of religion, so follow it, and do not follow the desires of those who do not know.”

“They can be of no help to you against Allah. The wrongdoers are allies of one another, whereas Allah is the Protector of those who are mindful of Him.”

They must unite upon this and not become divided, as is established in an authentic hadith from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Allah is pleased that you do three things: worship Him without associating anything with Him; hold fast, all together, to the rope of Allah and do not become divided; and offer sincere counsel to those whom Allah has placed in charge of your affairs.”

Worship of Allah entails perfect love for Allah and utter humility before Him. Thus, the foundation and basis of religion entail that Allah be

---

## Page 5869

the One who is worshipped, whom hearts love and fear, with no god for them besides Him. A god is that which hearts worship with love, reverence, hope, fear, veneration, exaltation, and the like.

Allah, glorified be He, sent the messengers with the message that there is no god but Him, so that through loving Him, hearts are freed from loving anything besides Him; through hoping in Him, from hoping in anything besides Him; through asking Him, from asking anything besides Him; through acting for His sake, from acting for the sake of anything besides Him; and through seeking His help, from seeking help from anything besides Him. Thus, at the centre of al-Fātihah are the words:

“You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in an authentic hadith:

“Allah Most High says: ‘I have divided prayer between Myself and My servant into two halves.’ When he says, ‘All praise is for Allah, Lord of all worlds,’ Allah says, ‘My servant has praised Me.’ When he says, ‘The Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful,’ He says, ‘My servant has extolled Me.’ When he says, ‘Master of the Day of Judgment,’ He says, ‘My servant has glorified Me.’ When he says, ‘You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help,’ He says, ‘This verse is divided into two halves between Myself and My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks for.’ When he says, ‘Guide us to the straight path—the path of those You have blessed, not those who have incurred Your anger, nor those who have gone astray,’ He says, ‘These are for My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks for.’”

Thus, at the centre of the surah are the words:

“You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.”

Religion, then, is to worship none but Allah and seek help from none but Him. The angels, the prophets, and all others are servants of Allah, as He Most High says:

“The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels brought near to Him. And whoever

---

## Page 5870

disdains His worship and grows arrogant—He will gather them all to Himself.”

“As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full and increase them out of His bounty. But those who disdain and grow arrogant, He will punish with a painful punishment, and they will find no protector or helper besides Allah.”

Love for the sake of someone other than Allah is exemplified by the Christians’ love for the Messiah, the Jews’ love for Moses, the Rāfidah’s love for ʿAlī, and the extremists’ love for their shaykhs and imams. Such is the case of someone who gives his allegiance to one shaykh or imam but recoils from another of similar or equal standing. This resembles the conduct of those People of the Book who believed in some messengers and disbelieved in others; of the Rāfidah, who give their allegiance to some Companions and show hostility towards others; and of partisans among those affiliated with jurisprudence and asceticism, who give their allegiance to some shaykhs and imams but not others. The true believer, however, gives his allegiance to all the people of faith. Allah Most High says:

“The believers are but brothers.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“One believer to another is like a building, each part strengthening the other.”

And he interlaced his fingers. He also said:

“The believers, in their mutual love and compassion, are like a body: when one limb suffers, the rest of the body responds with fever and sleeplessness.”

And he, peace be upon him, said:

“Do not sever ties with one another or turn your backs on one another. Be brothers, O servants of Allah.”

The distinction between love for Allah’s sake and love for the sake of someone other than Allah is further illustrated by the fact that Abū Bakr loved the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sincerely for Allah’s sake, whereas his uncle Abū Tālib loved and supported him out of his own inclination, not for Allah’s sake. Allah therefore accepted Abū Bakr’s deeds and revealed concerning him:

“But the most God-fearing will be kept away from it—he who

---

## Page 5871

gives his wealth to purify himself, not to repay anyone for a favour received, but only seeking the Face of his Lord Most High. And he will surely be pleased.”

As for Abū Tālib, Allah did not accept his deeds; rather, He cast him into the Fire, because he associated partners with Allah and acted for the sake of someone other than Him. Abū Bakr did not seek his reward from any created being, whether the Prophet or anyone else. Rather, he believed in him, loved him, protected him, and supported him with his person and wealth, seeking thereby to draw nearer to Allah and seeking his reward from Allah.

His Messenger conveys Allah’s commands and prohibitions, His promises and warnings. Allah Most High says:

“Your duty is only to convey the message, and Ours is to call them to account.”

Allah is the One who creates and provides, gives and withholds, lowers and raises, honours and humiliates. Glorified is He, the originator of all causes, the Lord and Sovereign of everything. The means that people employ, if commanded or permitted by Allah, may be pursued. But whatever is prohibited outright, or constitutes a religious innovation that Allah has not authorized, must not be pursued.

Allah Most High says:

“Say: ‘Call upon those whom you claim to be gods besides Allah. They possess not an atom’s weight in the heavens or on earth, nor do they have any share in either, nor does He have any helper among them.’ Intercession does not avail with Him except for one to whom He gives permission.”

Glorified is He, He has made clear the error of those who invoke created beings—angels, prophets, or others—by explaining that created beings possess not an atom’s weight in the heavens or on earth. He then made clear that they have no share in either, and then that He has no helper or supporter among them. For those who associate partners with Allah liken the Creator to created beings.

As some of them say:

“If there is

---

## Page 5872

something you need, appeal to Shaykh So-and-so, for you will find him; or take a few steps towards his tomb and call out to him, ‘O shaykh!’ He will fulfil your need.” This is an error, and doing so is unlawful. Although some who invoke others besides Allah occasionally see the form of the one they invoke, that is a devil who has assumed that form before them. Such things have happened to many people. Similar to this is the statement made by some ignorant followers of Shaykh Adī and others: “Any provision that does not come through the shaykh’s hands, I do not want.” It is astonishing that someone of sound mind should appeal to a dead person and seek his aid, yet not seek the aid of the Ever-Living who never dies. The delusion grows stronger in his mind that, had he not sought the dead shaykh’s aid, his need would not have been fulfilled. Doing this is forbidden.

One of them says: “If you need something from a king, you seek access to him through his aides; likewise, one seeks access to Him through the shaykhs.” These are the words of people of polytheism and misguidance. A king does not know the needs of his subjects, cannot fulfil them unaided, and only wishes to do so for some benefit he gains thereby. Allah, however, knows all things: He knows what is secret and what is still more hidden, and He has power over all things. All causes proceed from Him and return to Him. Every cause is itself dependent on other causes and subject to counteracting factors. Fire burns only when the object is susceptible to burning; thus it does not burn the salamander. If Allah wills, He prevents its effect, as He did for Abraham, peace be upon him.

---

## Page 5873

As for the Lord’s will, it depends on no one besides Him, and nothing can thwart it. Whatever Allah wills comes to pass, and whatever He does not will does not come to pass.

He, glorified be He, is more merciful to His servants than a mother is to her child. He shows them kindness and mercy and relieves their distress, although He has no need of them and they are utterly dependent on Him:

“There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.”

The Lord has thus ruled out all these possibilities, leaving only intercession. He says:

“Intercession does not benefit with Him except for those to whom He gives permission.”

And He says:

“Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?”

He is the One who permits intercession, and He is the One who accepts it; it all comes from Him alone. The more sincere a person’s devotion to Allah, the nearer he is to receiving the Messenger’s intercession. Abū Hurayrah asked him: “Who will be most blessed by your intercession, O Messenger of Allah?” He replied: “Whoever says, ‘There is no god worthy of worship except Allah,’ seeking thereby Allah’s Countenance.”

As for those who place their trust in someone besides Allah Most High to intercede for them, and attach themselves to that person, they are of the same kind as the polytheists who took intercessors besides Allah Most High. Allah Most High says:

“Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah? Say, ‘Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?’”

“Say, ‘All intercession belongs to Allah.’”

Allah Most High also says:

“Then He rose over the Throne. You have no protector or intercessor besides Him.”

And He says:

“Say, ‘Call upon those whom you claim to be gods besides Him. They have no power to remove your distress or to shift it elsewhere.’”

“Those whom they invoke themselves seek

---

## Page 5874

the means of drawing near to their Lord, each seeking to be closest to Him. They hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, your Lord’s punishment is ever to be feared.”

A group of the early generations said:

Some people used to invoke the Messiah, Ezra, and the angels. Allah Most High explained that these angels and prophets are His servants, just as those who invoke them are His servants. These angels and prophets seek nearness to Allah, hope for His mercy, and fear His punishment.

The polytheists took rivals alongside Allah, loving them as they loved Allah, and took intercessors to intercede for them with Allah. Their love for these beings and their association of them with Allah are akin to the Christians’ love for the Messiah and their association of him with Allah.

The believers, however, are stronger in their love for Allah. They worship Allah alone and do not set up anything alongside Him that they love as they love Him—neither His prophets nor anyone else. Rather, they love what He loves out of their love for Allah. They devote their religion sincerely to Allah and know that no one can intercede for them except by Allah’s permission.

Thus, they love Allah’s servant and Messenger, Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, out of their love for Allah. They know that he is Allah’s servant who conveys His message, so they obey his commands and believe what he tells them. They place their hope in none but Allah, fear none but Allah, and ask none but Allah. His intercession for those on whose behalf he intercedes is only by Allah’s permission. Neither our hope in the intercessor nor our fear of him benefits us. What benefits us is our worship of Allah alone, our sincere devotion to Him, and our reliance upon Him, for He is the One who grants the intercessor permission. A Muslim must therefore distinguish between the love and religion of the believers and the love of the Christians

---

## Page 5875

and the polytheists and their religion. He must follow the people of monotheism and faith and avoid resembling the polytheists and worshippers of the cross.

“Whoever possesses three qualities will taste the sweetness of faith: that Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than everything else; that he loves a person only for Allah’s sake; and that he hates to return to disbelief after Allah has saved him from it as much as he hates to be cast into the Fire.”

Allah Most High said:

“Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your relatives, the wealth you have acquired, the trade whose decline you fear, and the homes you cherish are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until Allah brings about His command. This is a vast subject. The religion of Islam is founded upon this principle, and the Quran revolves around it.

## Page 5876

Shaykh al-Islām—may Allah sanctify his soul—was asked about a group who had joined together in various corrupt practices, each clinging to some justification and relying on an opinion that had been expressed. Among them was someone devoted to attending forbidden musical gatherings featuring frame drums fitted with jingles and the pipes commonly used in our time. Beardless youths and women attend these gatherings. He justifies this by claiming that attending musical gatherings is permissible according to al-Shāfiʿī and other imams.

He replied:

As for musical gatherings involving singing, pipes, and jingling frame drums, the imams of the religion agree that these do not constitute acts of devotion or obedience to Allah. Indeed, even when such gatherings do not take this form, but involve singing, hand-clapping, beating with a stick, dancing, and the like—although these activities include what is permissible, what is disliked, what is prohibited, or what is permissible for women but not for men—the imams of the religion do not dispute that they do not constitute acts of devotion, obedience, or worship. Nor did any of the Companions, the Successors, the imams of the religion, or other religious shaykhs

---

## Page 5877

attend such musical gatherings, whether in the Hijaz, Egypt, Syria, Iraq, or Khurasan—not in the time of the Companions, the Successors, or their followers.

Rather, this arose later. Some people would gather for this purpose, calling the practice of striking small bells and similar objects with a stick “taghbīr.”

Al-Hasan ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Harrānī said: “I heard al-Shāfiʿī say: ‘I left behind in Baghdad something introduced by heretics, which they call taghbīr, through which they turn people away from the Quran.’”

This reflects al-Shāfiʿī’s profound understanding and knowledge of the religion. When the heart becomes accustomed to listening to poems and verses and takes pleasure in them, it develops an aversion to listening to the Quran and its verses. It thus contents itself with listening to Satan and dispenses with listening to the Most Merciful.

It is authentically reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“He is not one of us who does not recite the Quran melodiously.”

Al-Shāfiʿī, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and others explained this as referring to the voice: one beautifies the Quran with one’s voice and recites it melodiously, without objectionable musical intonation. Ibn ʿUyaynah, Abū ʿUbayd, and others explained it as finding sufficiency in the Quran. Although this conveys a sound meaning, the first interpretation is what the hadith indicates, for he said:

“He is not one of us who does not recite the Quran melodiously, raising his voice with it.”

A report states: “When a servant mounts a riding animal, Satan comes to him and says, ‘Sing.’ If he does not sing, he says to him, ‘Indulge in wishful thinking.’” For

---

## Page 5878

the soul generally needs something to recite melodiously. Whoever does not recite the Quran melodiously will recite poetry melodiously. Listening to the Quran is the practice of the prophets, the believers, those who know Allah, and the learned.

Allah Most High says:

“Those are the ones upon whom Allah bestowed favor among the prophets, from the descendants of Adam and from those We carried with Noah”—to the end of the verse.

He also says:

“And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger”—to the end of the verse.

He Most High says:

“Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them”—to the end of the two verses.

He says:

“Allah has sent down the best message”—to the end of the verse.

And He says:

“The believers are only those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned”—to the end of the verse.

This “listening” is what Allah has prescribed for the believers, both within prayer and outside it. When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gathered together, they would ask one of their number to recite while the others listened.

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by Abū Mūsā while he was reciting and began listening to his recitation. He said, ‘I passed by you last night while you were reciting, and I began listening to your recitation.’ He replied, ‘Had I known that you were listening, I would have made my recitation especially beautiful for you.’” That is, “I would have beautified it greatly.”

ʿUmar used to say to Abū Mūsā, “Remind us of our Lord.” He would then recite while they listened to his recitation.

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to Ibn Masʿūd, ‘Recite the Quran to me.’ He asked, ‘Should I recite it to you when it was revealed to you?’ He replied:

---

## Page 5879

‘I love to hear it from someone else.’ So I recited Sūrat al-Nisā’ to him until I reached this verse:

‘So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you as a witness against these people?’

He said, ‘That is enough.’ I looked and saw tears streaming from his eyes.”

This, then, is the listening practised by the early generations of this community and its most excellent generations. The finest spiritual masters advocate precisely this kind of listening. As for listening to poems set to melodies and gathering for that purpose, the foremost spiritual masters did not attend such gatherings: al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyād, Abraham ibn Adham, Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī, Maʿrūf al-Karkhī, al-Sarī al-Saqatī, and their counterparts among later generations, such as Shaykh ʿAbd al-Qādir, Shaykh ʿAdī ibn Musāfir, Shaykh Abū Madyan, Shaykh Abū al-Bayān, and other masters like them. They did not attend such gatherings. Some spiritual masters, including prominent ones, did attend them, but subsequently repented and abandoned the practice.

Al-Junayd—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—did not attend them towards the end of his life. He would say, “Whoever deliberately seeks out such listening falls prey to its temptation; whoever encounters it by chance finds relief in it.” That is, someone who purposefully seeks out such listening becomes captivated by it, whereas someone who hears a verse suited to his spiritual state, without deliberate purpose, finds relief in it.

Those who attended the innovated listening gatherings that al-Shāfiʿī described as an invention of the heretics did not gather with beardless youths and women, nor with jingling instruments and flutes. Their poetry encouraged renunciation of worldly attachments and softened hearts.

---

## Page 5880

As for “listening” that involves practices condemned by religion, anyone who regards it as an act of devotion must be called upon to repent; if he repents, well and good; otherwise, he is to be put to death. If, however, he is acting ignorantly on a mistaken interpretation, the error of his interpretation must be explained to him, and he must be given the knowledge that dispels his ignorance. This concerns treating it as a path to Allah.

As for whether it is forbidden for someone who engages in it for amusement and entertainment, rather than as an act of devotion to Allah, this requires further distinction. Listening that involves flutes and jingling frame drums is forbidden according to the four imams. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Salāh stated that there is no disagreement about this within the school of al-Shāfiʿī. The disagreement reported concerns only the reed pipe played on its own. Yet neither the Iraqi adherents of al-Shāfiʿī nor the earlier Khurāsānī scholars mentioned any disagreement concerning even that; it was mentioned only by the later Khurāsānī scholars.

It is established in Sahīh al-Bukhārī and elsewhere that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, spoke in condemnation of those who deem illicit sexual relations, silk, wine, and musical instruments lawful, and stated that Allah would punish them. This hadith therefore indicates that musical instruments are forbidden. According to the lexicographers, the term for musical instruments encompasses instruments of entertainment, and thus includes all these instruments.

For this reason, the jurists stated that whoever destroys them is not liable for compensation, provided that he removes what is damaged

---

## Page 5881

and unlawful. If he also destroys their monetary value, there is disagreement over this. The well-known position of Ahmad, and that of Mālik, is that no compensation is due in these cases either. The same applies when someone destroys wine jars, splits open its containers, or destroys idols made of gold—as Moses, peace be upon him, destroyed the calf made of gold—and in similar cases.

## Page 5882

He was also asked:

About someone who forms bonds of brotherhood with women and performs feats resembling sleight of hand, such as tracing patterns on cotton or a piece of cloth with lādhan or something else, or holding fire directly in his palm or between his fingers, with nothing separating his skin from it, and so forth.

As for forming bonds of brotherhood with women and displaying the feats mentioned, these are among the practices of the brethren of devils. Not one of those who perform these feats is a friend of Allah. Rather, they range between satanic states and lying imposture—states of Iblīs and settings for deception.

The underlying reality of their condition is that devils descend upon those who practise the lying and wickedness that Satan loves. When one of them abandons reason and religion and becomes one of the reckless—those who obey Satan and disobey the Most Merciful, making snorting and grunting noises like the braying of donkeys, attending listening sessions, forming bonds of brotherhood with women, taking neighbours as companions, dancing like monkeys, and pecking through the bowing and prostration in their prayers, while hating to hear the Quran and to follow the law of the Most Merciful—the devils who descend upon every sinful liar descend upon them. Among them are those whom the devils lift

---

## Page 5883

into the air; others they cause to enter fire. Some walk accompanied by a light, which makes them think that these are miracles. Some call upon the shaykh for help and address those who call upon the shaykh, so that this is thought to be a miracle granted to the shaykh. Others produce food, fruit and sweets, besides other things known to us. We also know people who have experienced these things and much more besides.

When a man repents, adheres to Islam, prays as Muslims pray, repents of what the Lord of all worlds has forbidden, and replaces listening to Satan with listening to the Quran, those satanic states disappear. If his faith grows strong, he attains the spiritual stations of the righteous; otherwise, it suffices him to be among the people of the Garden of Bliss. This is clear: a Muslim knows that these states are satanic, not miracles granted to people of faith.

## Page 5884

He was also asked about a group of people who had gathered to engage in various forms of corruption. Among them were those who said that the ultimate goal of spiritual realization and the perfection of treading the path consist in abandoning religious obligations. Thus, if one of them is required to pray, he stands up and says, “We have left the Presence and now stand at the door.”
