As for anyone who regards freedom from religious obligations as the perfection of spiritual realization, this is the doctrine of the heretics among the Qarmatians, the Bātiniyyah, and similar heretics who claim affiliation with learning, asceticism, Sufism, or ascetic practice. One of them says, “A servant performs deeds until he attains knowledge of Allah; once he attains it, religious obligations no longer apply to him.” Whoever says this is an unbeliever and an apostate, according to the consensus of the leading scholars of Islam. They agree that the commands and prohibitions remain binding upon every sane person who has reached puberty until death. Allah Most High says:

“And worship your Lord until certainty comes to you.”

Al-Hasan al-Basrī said, “Allah has appointed no end to the believer’s deeds short of death,” and he recited this verse. Here, “certainty” refers to what comes after death, as Allah Most High says in the other passage:

“And we used to deny the Day of Judgment,”

“Until certainty came to us.”

The same meaning occurs in the words of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in

---

## Page 5885

the authentic hadith, on the death of ʿUthmān ibn Mazʿūn: “As for ʿUthmān, certainty has come to him from his Lord.”

Al-Junayd ibn Muhammad—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—was asked about someone who says that he has advanced along the path of righteousness to the point that deeds are no longer required of him. He replied, “Unlawful sexual intercourse, theft, and drinking wine are better than what these people say.” Al-Junayd—may Allah have mercy on him—spoke the truth: those are major sins, whereas this is unbelief and hypocrisy, and major sins are better than unbelief and hypocrisy.

When one of these people says, “We have left the Presence and come to the door,” these are true words intended to convey falsehood. They have indeed left Satan’s presence and come to the door of the Most Merciful. It is related, for example, that one of their shaykhs was attending a gathering for devotional listening. When the caller gave the call to prayer, he rose to pray and said, “We were in the Presence, but now we have come to the door.” There is no doubt that he was in Satan’s presence and then came to the door of the Most Merciful. But the claim that he was in Allah’s presence and then came to His door is untenable for anyone who believes in Allah and His Messenger. It is authentically established that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“A servant is nearest to his Lord when he is prostrating.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, also said:

“Be steadfast, though you will never attain complete steadfastness. Know that the best of your deeds is prayer, and that none but a believer consistently maintains his ablution.”

In an authentic hadith, Ibn Masʿūd relates concerning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “He

---

## Page 5886

was asked, ‘Which deeds are best?’ He replied, ‘Prayer at its appointed times.’”

In another hadith, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The first deed for which a servant will be brought to account is his prayer.”

Prayer was the last thing the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, enjoined upon his community. He used to say:

“Prayer has been made the delight of my eyes.”

He also used to say:

“Give us comfort through prayer, O Bilāl.”

He did not say, “Give us relief from it.” Whoever does not find delight and comfort of heart in prayer is deficient in faith. Allah Most High says:

“And seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The foundation of the matter is Islam, its pillar is prayer, and its highest peak is jihad in the path of Allah.”

This is a vast subject that no one who believes in Allah and His Messenger can deny.

## Page 5887

Shaykh al-Islām, Shaykh Taqī al-Dīn Ahmad ibn Taymiyyah—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

About the practices introduced by ascetic Sufi mendicants and religious devotees: keeping company with young men; establishing bonds of brotherhood with women; holding dispute proceedings; lowering their heads before one another; consuming one another’s wealth without right; hoisting an offender up from beneath his feet and beating him unjustly; standing bareheaded and bent forward as though bowing in prayer; placing sandals on their heads; wearing woollen and patched garments; using prayer rugs and prayer beads; and consuming hashish. When a beardless youth comes to them, they require him to have one of them as his companion and demand his companionship. Is this permissible? Has it been transmitted from the Companions?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. As for keeping company with beardless youths by singling one of them out for an exclusive attachment—as these people do—along with such practices as being alone with a handsome beardless youth, having him spend the night with a man, and the like, this is among the most heinous wrongs according to Muslims, Jews, Christians, and others.

The prohibition of sodomy is necessarily known in the religion of Islam and in the religions of all nations after the people of Lot. Thus Allah has made clear in His Book that no one in all the worlds committed it before the people of Lot. And Allah punished

---

## Page 5888

those who regarded it as lawful with a punishment unlike any He inflicted upon other nations: He obliterated their sight, overturned their cities, turning them upside down, and followed this with stones from heaven.

For this reason, Islamic law prescribes that a sexual offence carrying the death penalty be punished by stoning. Thus the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stoned the two Jews, Māʿiz ibn Mālik al-Aslamī, the Ghāmidī woman, and others. His rightly guided successors also carried out stoning after him. Allah prescribed stoning for the people of the Torah and the Quran. The Sunan collections report that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever you find committing the act of the people of Lot, kill both the one who performs it and the one upon whom it is performed.”

The Companions therefore agreed that both should be put to death, although they differed over the manner of execution. Some said that the offender should be stoned; others said that he should be thrown from the highest wall in the town and then pelted with stones; still others said that he should be burned with fire. Accordingly, the majority of the early generations and jurists held that both should be stoned, whether or not they had previously consummated a marriage, whether they were free or enslaved, or whether one was enslaved to the other. Muslims have agreed that anyone who regards this act as lawful, whether with a slave or anyone else, is an unbeliever and an apostate.

Likewise, the acts leading to this indecency—kissing a beardless youth, touching him, or looking at him for pleasure—are forbidden by Muslim consensus, just as they are with a woman outside the prohibited degrees of marriage. As established in the authentic hadith collection, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The two eyes

---

## Page 5889

commit adultery, and their adultery is looking. The ear commits adultery, and its adultery is listening. The hand commits adultery, and its adultery is grasping. The foot commits adultery, and its adultery is walking. The heart yearns and desires, and the private parts either confirm this or deny it.” If someone who regards what Allah has forbidden as lawful is an unbeliever, then what of someone who makes it a means of drawing near to Allah Most High and a path to Him?

Allah Most High says:

“When they commit an indecency, they say, ‘We found our forefathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it.’ Say, ‘Allah does not command indecency. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?’”

The occasion for the revelation of this verse was that the Arabs, apart from the Hums, used to circumambulate the House naked. Allah therefore described their exposure of their private parts as an indecency and made clear that He does not command indecency. Accordingly:

“When Abū Bakr al-Siddīq performed the pilgrimage before the Farewell Pilgrimage—at a time when both Muslims and polytheists performed the pilgrimage—he proclaimed, at the command of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ‘After this year, no polytheist shall perform the pilgrimage, and no naked person shall circumambulate the House.’”

What, then, of someone who regards committing the greater indecency, or lesser acts, as lawful and makes this a form of worship and a spiritual path? Although a group of would-be philosophers, together with the misguided, perverse people who agreed with them, made infatuation with beautiful forms part of the path by which souls are purified, this is not part of the religion of the Muslims, the Jews, or the Christians. Rather, it is the religion of the polytheists, who instituted religious practices for which Allah gave no permission.

---

## Page 5890

This is so even though their followers have gone beyond what their masters and leaders instituted, adding indecencies that even monkeys would not tolerate. For it is established in Sahīh al-Bukhārī:

“During the pre-Islamic era, Abū Imrān saw a male monkey commit adultery with a female monkey, whereupon the monkeys gathered against him and stoned him.”

People in our own time have witnessed similar things among animals other than monkeys, even birds. Even if the aforementioned practice of keeping company with “beardless youths” were free of the forbidden act, it would still create a risk of it and be a cause of it. For this reason, the shaykhs who knew the path to Allah used to warn against it.

Fath al-Mawsilī said: “I met thirty of the abdāl, and whenever I parted from any of them, he would forbid me to keep company with adolescent boys.”

Maʿrūf al-Karkhī said: “They used to forbid that.”

One of the Successors said: “I fear for a young ascetic no more from a wild beast sitting beside him than I do from an adolescent boy sitting beside him.”

Sufyān al-Thawrī and Bishr al-Hāfī said: “With a woman there is one devil, and with an adolescent boy there are two.”

One of them said: “No servant falls from Allah’s favour without Allah afflicting him with the companionship of these adolescent boys.”

The temptation of forms and sounds has brought upon ascetics harm whose extent only Allah knows, so much so that even the greatest shaykhs have acknowledged it. Those among them whom Allah rescued through His mercy repented. It is well known that this amounts to following one’s desires without guidance from Allah:

“And who is more astray than one who follows his own desires without guidance from Allah?”

Whoever regards this as lawful or

---

## Page 5891

adopts it as a religious practice is astray, resembling the polytheists and Christians. Whoever does it while acknowledging that it is a sin or an act of disobedience is sinful or defiantly disobedient. Likewise, forming a bond of brotherhood with “a woman outside the permanently prohibited degrees of marriage,” such that he is alone with her and sees parts of her body that he is not entitled to see, is forbidden by Muslim consensus. Adopting this as a religion and a spiritual path is disbelief and misguidance. Money taken for condoning these people’s conduct and facilitating conversation with a beardless youth is akin to a procurer’s fee. Their demanding his companionship is akin to holding a wedding founded on fornication.

Allah, glorified be He, has permitted marriage, not promiscuity or the taking of secret lovers. A promiscuous woman commits fornication with whoever happens to be available to her; likewise, a promiscuous man commits fornication with whoever happens to be available to him. Taking a secret lover, by contrast, means that a man has a mistress or a woman has a lover. Thus, a beardless youth who becomes the lover of one of these men is akin to a woman taken as a mistress. Likewise, the fees and money taken for this are akin to a prostitute’s earnings, a procurer’s fee, and the like.

As for their “dispute proceedings,” when two men quarrel in word or deed, their case must be handled justly. Allah Most High says:

“O you who believe, stand firmly for justice as witnesses for Allah.”

And He says:

“Stand firmly for Allah as witnesses in justice.”

And He says:

“If two groups of believers fight, make peace between them. But if one of them transgresses against the other, fight the transgressing group until it returns to Allah’s command.”

The verse continues.

---

## Page 5892

It has also been reported that the two groups fought with palm stalks and sandals. Allah Most High says:

“There is no good in much of their private conversation, except for those who enjoin charity, kindness, or reconciliation between people.”

The verse continues. He also says:

“Allah commands you to return trusts to their rightful owners and, when you judge between people, to judge with justice. Excellent indeed is what Allah instructs you to do. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.”

And He says:

“The recompense for an evil deed is an evil deed like it, but whoever pardons and brings about reconciliation—his reward is with Allah.”

And He says:

“If you retaliate, then retaliate only to the extent of the injury inflicted upon you.”

The verse continues.

If two people have a dispute, their case should be examined. If it becomes clear that one has wronged the other, the wronged party has the choice between exacting retribution and pardoning, though pardoning is better. If the wrong consisted of striking or slapping him, he may strike or slap the offender just as the offender did to him, according to the overwhelming majority of the early generations and many of the leading scholars. This is also what the Sunnah establishes. Another view holds that the offender should be disciplined, but that retaliation in kind does not apply in such cases.

If the offender verbally abused him, he may respond with equivalent abuse, provided this does not violate a right belonging exclusively to Allah or wrong anyone other than the offender. Thus, if the offender cursed him or called him a dog or the like, he may say the same to him. But if the offender cursed his father, he may not curse the offender’s father, because that father has not wronged him. If the offender fabricated a lie against him, he may not fabricate a lie against the offender, because lying is forbidden as a matter of Allah’s right. Similarly, it has been stated by many

---

## Page 5893

scholars regarding retribution for bodily injuries: if someone wounds, chokes, strikes, or similarly harms another, the injured person may do the same to him. This is the sounder of the scholars’ two views, unless the act is forbidden as a matter of Allah’s right, such as committing an act of sexual indecency or forcing someone to drink wine. Most scholars have prohibited retaliation of this kind, although some have permitted responding with its equivalent.

If the wrongdoer acknowledges his wrongdoing and asks the wronged person to pardon him and seek Allah’s forgiveness for him, this is good and prescribed in Islam. As authentically reported in al-Sahīh from Abū al-Dardā’:

“There was a dispute between Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. Abū Bakr asked ʿUmar to seek forgiveness for him, but ʿUmar refused and later regretted it. He went looking for Abū Bakr and found that he had already gone to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and told him what had happened. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘May Allah forgive you, Abū Bakr.’ Then he said, ‘O people! I came to you and said, “I am the Messenger of Allah,” and you said, “You are lying,” while Abū Bakr said, “You speak the truth.” Will you then leave my companion alone for my sake?’”

If the wronged person is asked to pardon after the wrongdoer has acknowledged his wrongdoing, and he agrees, he is among those who do good and whose reward is with Allah. If, however, he insists on claiming his right, he is not a wrongdoer, though he has forgone what is better and more virtuous. No one may exclude him from those who follow the path merely on that account, as many people do. Allah Most High says:

“As for those who seek redress after being wronged, there is no blame on them.”

“Blame falls only on those who wrong people and transgress in the land without right. They will have a punishment

---

## Page 5894

that is painful.” If someone were considered to have departed from the path merely for foregoing an act of kindness that was not obligatory upon him, most of those who follow it would fall outside it. “Allah’s allies” are of two kinds: the foremost, who are brought near to Him, and the people of the right, who follow a middle course. As al-Bukhārī narrated in his Sahīh from Abū Hurayrah, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah Most High says: ‘Whoever shows enmity towards an ally of Mine has openly challenged Me to war. Nothing by which My servant draws near to Me compares with fulfilling what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary deeds until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he grasps, and his foot with which he walks. Through Me he hears, through Me he sees, through Me he grasps, and through Me he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give to him, and if he seeks My protection, I will surely protect him. I have never hesitated over anything I am going to do as I hesitate over taking the soul of My believing servant: he dislikes death, and I dislike causing him distress, yet he must undergo it.’”

Moreover, most of those who condemn someone for declining to pardon do so only out of their own desires, because the wrongdoer is their friend, heir, companion, or the like. Allah, Glorified is He, has required His servants to uphold justice in reconciliation just as He has required it in judgment. He Most High says:

“Reconcile them with justice and act equitably. Indeed, Allah loves those who act equitably.”

He has also made sincerity a condition of the reconciliation for which He grants a reward, saying:

---

## Page 5895

—exalted is He—

“Whoever does this seeking Allah’s pleasure, We shall grant him a great reward.”

For many people seek reconciliation merely to gain a reputation or to show off. Justice requires enabling the wronged person to obtain redress, then appealing to him to pardon, with the wrongdoer seeking reconciliation with him, and encouraging this. Whenever Allah Most High mentions in the Quran people’s rights whose violation brings sin upon the wrongdoer, He encourages pardon. Thus He, Glorified is He, says:

“And wounds are subject to equal retribution. But whoever waives it as an act of charity, it is an expiation for him.”

And He says:

“The recompense of an evil deed is an evil like it. But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with Allah. Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers.”

Anas reported:

“No case involving retribution was ever brought before the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, without his urging pardon.”

Seeking pardon from the wronged person does not require that the wrongdoer stand on his feet and not place his sandals on his head, or observe similar practices to which some people commit themselves. Rather, the condition is that he make himself available so that the other person may obtain his due from him. Once he has enabled the wronged person to obtain his due, he has fulfilled his obligation. The person entitled to redress then has the choice: he may pardon or exact his due.

The wronged person may shun him for three days. After those three days, however, he may no longer shun him on account of the wrong he suffered, because the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“It is not lawful for a Muslim to

---

## Page 5896

shun his brother for more than three days. When they meet, each turns away from the other; the better of the two is the one who first offers the greeting of peace.”

But if the sin concerns Allah’s rights—such as lying, acts of sexual immorality, innovations contrary to the Book and Sunnah, negligently failing to observe prayer and its obligations, or similar offences—then repentance is indispensable. Must repentance also be accompanied by demonstrable reform in one’s conduct? The scholars hold two views on this.

If they have a shaykh whom they obey, he may discipline the offender in proportion to his sin, using a measure appropriate for someone of his standing to impose on someone of the offender’s standing. This may include shunning him for a time, just as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, shunned the three who were left behind.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his rightly guided caliphs governed people in both their religious and worldly affairs. Thereafter, these responsibilities became divided: military rulers governed people’s worldly affairs and outward religious affairs, while scholars and religious shaykhs guided them in the matters of knowledge and religion for which people referred to them. These are people in authority who must be obeyed when they enjoin obedience to Allah in matters within their authority.

It is likewise in this sense that “those in authority” in His words:

“Obey Allah, and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you”

is explained as referring to military rulers—kings and their deputies—and to the people of knowledge and religion who teach people their religion and command them to obey Allah. For religion is upheld by the Book and iron, as Allah Most High says:

---

## Page 5897

“We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Book and the balance so that people may uphold justice. And We sent down iron, in which there is great might and benefits for people.”

If military rulers are unable and remiss in correcting those who follow the spiritual path, responsibility for correcting them falls upon their leaders. They may impose whatever discretionary punishment and discipline they are able to administer, if no one else undertakes it. As the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand. If he cannot, then with his tongue; and if he cannot, then with his heart. That is the weakest level of faith.”

An offender’s discretionary punishment may include banishment from his homeland for a time, just as Umar ibn al-Khattāb—may Allah be pleased with him—used to banish people for drinking wine. Likewise, Nasr ibn Hajjāj was banished to Basra for fear that women would be tempted by him. The Sunnah of Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, established banishment for unlawful sexual intercourse and the banishment of effeminate men. This is the basis for some shaykhs instructing an offender to travel.

This is a summary that requires lengthy elaboration explaining sins, repentance from them, and the conditions of repentance. Repentance is a state that accompanies the servant from the outset until the end of his life, as Allah Most High says:

“When Allah’s help and victory come, and you see people entering Allah’s religion in multitudes”—to the end of the verse.

If the servant repents and gives some of his wealth in charity to purify himself of his sin, that is good and prescribed. Allah Most High says:

“Do they not know that Allah is the One who accepts repentance

---

## Page 5898

from His servants and receives their charities.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Charity extinguishes sin as water extinguishes fire, and envy consumes good deeds as fire consumes firewood.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, also said:

“A man’s failings concerning his family, wealth, and children are expiated by prayer, fasting, charity, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong.”

Kaʿb ibn Mālik said, “Part of my repentance is to give up my wealth in charity.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, replied, “Keep some of your wealth; that is better for you.”

However, he may not be compelled to give charity, nor is he obliged to give away his clothing or anything else. Nor may anyone demand his repentance with the intention of appropriating his wealth, especially if he is subjected to undue pressure and accused of a sin he has not committed. This would remain lying, injustice, and the wrongful consumption of wealth.

The charity he gives need not be spent on food for them to eat. Rather, the choice is his to direct it wherever it will be most beneficial and most in keeping with obedience to Allah and His Messenger. What should be done is to identify the person most deserving of that charity and give it to him. As for making the preparation of food and the hosting of a meal part of repentance, this is an innovation. People continually repented during the time of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions without this innovation.

---

## Page 5899

As for expressing gratitude by giving away some of one’s wealth, such as clothing or something else, in thanks to Allah for His blessings—whether repentance, setting matters right, or the like—this is good and prescribed. When the bearer of good news came to Ka'b ibn Mālik to tell him that Allah had accepted his repentance, he gave him the garment he was wearing and borrowed another garment in which to go to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

However, singling out clothing or anything else as a prescribed expression of gratitude is also an innovation. If someone does this occasionally, it is good. Nothing should be made obligatory or recommended unless Allah and His Messenger have made it obligatory or recommended, and nothing should be condemned except what Allah and His Messenger disapprove of. No religious practice is legitimate except what Allah has prescribed, and nothing is forbidden except what Allah has forbidden.

Beating a man on the soles of his feet is a form of discretionary punishment. If he has committed an offence that warrants such punishment according to Allah’s religion, and the person disciplining him is qualified to do so, then it is justified.

As for baring the head and bowing, these are not part of the Sunnah. They are taken from the customs of certain kings and from pre-Islamic ignorance. No created being may ask others to bare their heads or bow before him. Bowing is for Allah alone in prayer, and heads are bared for Allah while in the state of pilgrimage consecration.

As for “wearing wool,” the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wore a woollen robe while travelling. Hence al-Awzā'ī said:

“Wearing wool while travelling is a Sunnah, but wearing it while resident is an innovation.”

---

## Page 5900

What this means is that constantly wearing it while resident is an innovation, as we have related from Muhammad ibn Sīrīn. When he heard that some people deliberately chose to wear wool, he said:

“I think these people have heard that the Messiah used to wear wool, so they wear it for that reason. Yet our Prophet’s way is dearer to us than anyone else’s.”

It is reported in the Sunan collections that “the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to attend Friday prayer wearing wool.” Another hadith states:

“Some people came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, clad in striped cloaks.”

These cloaks were made of wool. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, also wore cotton and other fabrics. The point is that treating the wearing of wool as an act of worship and a path to Allah is an innovation. Wearing it out of need and for its practical benefit, however—for a poor person because nothing else is available, or because he does not wear anything else, and similar reasons—is good and prescribed.

Refusing to wear it altogether is blameworthy, especially in the case of someone who professes to wear it out of pride and arrogance: Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection. For it is established in the authentic hadith collection that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever lets his waist-wrapper trail out of arrogance, Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection.”

He also said:

“While a man was letting his waist-wrapper trail out of arrogance, the earth swallowed him up, and he will continue sinking through it until the Day of Resurrection.”

They used to disapprove of both extremes of conspicuous dress: the luxurious and the shabby. No one may make anything part of religion or the path to Allah unless Allah and His Messenger have prescribed it, especially when imposing such restrictions corrupts both religious and worldly affairs. For

---

## Page 5901

wearing wool and patching garments when needed are commendable practices of the early generations. Refusing to do so altogether is blameworthy. But someone who deliberately takes an intact garment, tears it, then patches it with scraps, and wears fine wool superior to cotton and linen, combines two forms of corruption.

As for religion, he imagines that restricting oneself to patched clothing and wool is part of religion. Then he seeks to display its outward appearance without its substance, spending more on this than would be spent on intact cotton garments. This is contrary to asceticism. There is also the waste of wealth through destroying it and spending it on what brings no benefit, either in religion or in worldly life.

---

## Page 5902

What do the eminent scholars, the imams of Islam and heirs of the prophets—peace be upon them—say about the nature of “the listening practice of the righteous”? May Allah be pleased with these scholars and grant them contentment. What is this practice? Is listening to poems set to melody and accompanied by musical instruments an act of devotion and obedience, or not? Is it permissible or not?

Shaykh al-Islām Taqī al-Dīn Ahmad ibn Taymiyyah—may Allah be pleased with him—replied:

Praise be to Allah, Lord of all worlds. I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. May Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace.

The foundation of this “question” is to distinguish between listening that brings religious benefit and listening that is permitted to alleviate hardship: between listening to draw near to Allah and listening for amusement. As for the listening that Allah Most High prescribed for His servants, and for which the early generations of this ummah—the Companions, the Successors, and their successors—would gather for the rectification of their hearts and the purification of

---

## Page 5903

their souls—it is listening to the verses of Allah Most High. This is the listening of the prophets, the believers, and those endowed with knowledge and spiritual insight.

After mentioning the prophets whom He named, Allah Most High said:

“Those were the ones whom Allah favoured among the prophets, from the descendants of Adam, from those We carried with Noah, from the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and from those We guided and chose. Whenever the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell down in prostration and weeping.”

He also said:

“The believers are only those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned, whose faith increases when His verses are recited to them, and who put their trust in their Lord.”

Allah Most High said:

“Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall upon their faces in prostration, saying, ‘Glory be to our Lord! Surely the promise of our Lord will be fulfilled.’ And they fall upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility.”

Allah Most High said:

“When they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized.”

It is this listening that Allah Most High has commanded, as He said:

“When the Quran is recited, listen to it attentively and remain silent, so that you may receive mercy.”

He praised those who listen in this way, as in His words:

“So give glad tidings to My servants who listen to what is said and follow the best of it.”

He said in another verse:

“Have they not reflected upon the Word, or has something come to them that did not come to their forefathers?”

The Word upon which they were commanded to reflect is the very Word to which they were commanded to listen.

Allah Most High also said:

“Do they not, then, reflect upon the Quran, or do hearts have

---

## Page 5904

locks upon them?”

Allah Most High said:

“A blessed Book which We have sent down to you, so that they may reflect upon its verses.”

Just as He praised this listening, He condemned those who turn away from it. Allah Most High said:

“When Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly, as though he had not heard them, as though there were deafness in his ears.”

Allah Most High said:

“Those who disbelieve say, ‘Do not listen to this Quran, and make noise during its recitation, so that you may prevail.’”

Allah Most High said:

“The Messenger said, ‘My Lord, my people have indeed abandoned this Quran.’ Thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. But your Lord is sufficient as a guide and helper.”

Allah Most High said:

“So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them. What is the matter with them that they turn away from the Reminder, as though they were startled wild donkeys fleeing from a lion?”

Allah Most High said:

“They say, ‘Our hearts are veiled against what you call us to, there is deafness in our ears, and between us and you there is a barrier.’”

Allah Most High said:

“When you recite the Quran, We place a hidden barrier between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter. And We place coverings over their hearts, preventing them from understanding it, and deafness in their ears.”

This is the listening that Allah has prescribed for His servants in the dawn, sunset, and night prayers, and on other occasions.

The Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to gather for this listening. When they gathered, they would ask one of their number to recite while the rest listened. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say to Abū Mūsā:

---

## Page 5905

“O Abū Mūsā, remind us of our Lord.” He would then recite while they listened.

This is the listening in which the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, participated with his Companions and which he requested of them, as related in the Sahīh from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, who said:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Recite the Quran to me.’ I said, ‘Shall I recite it to you when it was revealed to you?’ He replied, ‘I love to hear it from someone else.’ So I recited Surah al-Nisāʾ to him until I reached this verse: ‘How, then, will it be when We bring a witness from every nation and bring you as a witness against these people?’ He said, ‘That is enough.’ I looked and saw tears flowing from his eyes.”

This is what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions used to listen to. As Allah Most High said:

“Allah has certainly bestowed a great favour upon the believers by sending among them a Messenger from themselves, reciting His verses to them, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom.”

“Wisdom” here is the Sunnah.

Allah Most High said:

“I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, who has made it sacred and to whom all things belong. And I have been commanded to be one of those who submit to Him.”

“And to recite the Quran. Whoever is guided is guided only for his own benefit; and whoever goes astray, say, ‘I am only one of the warners.’”

The same applies to the other messengers. Allah Most High said:

“O children of Adam, if messengers from among you come to you, relating My verses to you, then those who fear Allah and mend their ways will have no fear, nor will they grieve.”

This is the basis upon which the case will be established against them on the Day of Resurrection. As Allah Most High said:

“O company of jinn

---

## Page 5906

and humankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating My verses to you and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours? They will say, ‘We testify against ourselves.’ The worldly life deluded them, and they will testify against themselves that they were disbelievers.”

Allah Most High said:

“Those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, ‘Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting your Lord’s verses to you and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?’ They will say, ‘Yes, but the decree of punishment has come into effect against the disbelievers.’”

He has stated that whoever holds fast to this listening is rightly guided and successful, while whoever turns away from it is astray and wretched.

Allah Most High said:

“When guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer.”

“But whoever turns away from My remembrance will have a life of hardship, and We will gather him blind on the Day of Resurrection.”

“He will say, ‘My Lord, why have You gathered me blind when I used to see?’”

“He will say, ‘Just as Our verses came to you and you forgot them, so today you will be forgotten.’”

Allah Most High said:

“Whoever turns blindly away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil who becomes his companion.”

“Remembrance of Allah” sometimes means a servant’s remembrance of his Lord, and sometimes means the Reminder that Allah has sent down. As Allah Most High said:

“This is a blessed Reminder that We have sent down.”

Noah said:

“Do you wonder that a reminder has come to you from your Lord through a man from among you, so that he may warn you?”

And He said:

“They say, ‘O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, you are surely mad!’”

And He said:

“No fresh reminder comes to them from their Lord but they listen to it.”

And He said:

“Indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people.”

And He said:

“It is nothing but a reminder to all people, for whoever wills

---

## Page 5907

among you to follow the straight path.” And He said:

“We have not taught him poetry, nor is it fitting for him. It is nothing but a reminder and a clear Quran.”

This “listening” has effects upon faith, including sacred knowledge and pure spiritual states, which would take a long time to explain and describe. It also has praiseworthy bodily effects: humility of the heart, tears in the eyes, and shivering of the skin. These are mentioned in the Quran.

These qualities were present among the Companions. After their time, three further effects appeared among the Successors: agitation, screaming, fainting, and death. In sum, this listening is the foundation of faith. Allah sent Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to all creation to convey their Lord’s messages to them. Whoever hears what the Messenger conveyed, believes in it, and follows it is rightly guided and successful; whoever turns away from it is astray and wretched.

As for “listening to whistling and clapping”—meaning clapping with the hands and making sounds such as whistling—this is the listening of the polytheists that Allah Most High mentioned when He said:

“Their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping.”

He thus tells us that the polytheists treated clapping their hands and making sounds with their mouths as acts of devotion and religion. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions did not gather for this kind of listening, nor did they ever attend it. Whoever claims that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, attended such a gathering has lied

---

## Page 5908

about him, according to the consensus of those versed in his hadith and Sunnah.

As for the report mentioned by Muhammad ibn Tāhir al-Maqdisī in “The Question of Listening” and “On the Nature of Sufism,” and transmitted through him by Shaykh Abū Hafs ʿUmar al-Suhrawardī, author of ʿAwārif al-Maʿārif, it relates:

“A Bedouin recited these verses to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

‘Love’s serpent has bitten my heart;
No physician can heal it, no reciter of charms,
Except the beloved with whom I am enraptured—
With him are my healing charm and antidote.’

“He then gave expression to ecstasy until his cloak fell from his shoulders. Muʿāwiyah said to him, ‘How delightful your amusement is!’ He replied, ‘Gently, Muʿāwiyah! One who gives no expression to ecstasy when the beloved is mentioned is not noble.’”

This report is a lie and a fabrication, according to the consensus of the scholars versed in this field.

Even more blatantly false is another report in which they relate:

“When he gave the poor the glad tidings that they would enter Paradise before the rich, they gave expression to ecstasy and tore their clothes. Gabriel descended from heaven and said, ‘O Muhammad, your Lord asks for His share of these scraps of cloth.’ He took a scrap and hung it upon the Throne, and that is the zīq (collar) of the poor.”

Such reports are narrated only by people who are among the most ignorant of the life and circumstances of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his Companions, and those who came after them, and who have the least knowledge of Islam and faith.

---

## Page 5909

This resembles the account narrated by those who relate:

“The people of the Suffah fought alongside the unbelievers when the Muslims were routed at Hunayn, or on some other occasion. They said, ‘We are with Allah; whoever Allah is with, we are with him.’”

And those who relate:

“On the morning after the Ascension, the Prophet found the people of the Suffah discussing a secret that Allah had commanded him to conceal. He asked them, ‘Where did you learn this?’

“They replied, ‘Allah taught it to us.’

“He said, ‘My Lord, did You not command me not to divulge it?’

“He replied, ‘I commanded you not to divulge it, but I Myself told them about it.’”

There are similar reports narrated by groups who profess religion despite their profound ignorance of Islam. Upon these reports they build corresponding forms of hypocrisy and religious innovation.

At times they dispense with the Messenger’s mediation, claiming that they can reach Allah Most High without going by way of any of the messengers whatsoever. This is greater disbelief than that of the Jews and Christians, for the latter dispensed with the mediation of one messenger, not that of the messengers altogether. If these people dispense entirely with the messengers’ mediation for themselves, this is more grievous disbelief than that of the former.

Yet they say, “This mediation is unnecessary only for the elite, not for ordinary people.” Thus, their disbelief is greater than that of the People of the Book insofar as they dispense with all prophetic mediation for themselves in certain circumstances, whereas the disbelief of the People of the Book is greater insofar as they reject Muhammad’s mediation altogether.

Indeed, those among the People of the Book who say that he is a messenger to the unlettered but not to the People of the Book are better than these people. For the former exclude from his message those who possess a scripture, whereas these people exclude from his message those who are left with nothing but imaginings

---

## Page 5910

and whisperings and conjectures instilled in them by Satan, while they imagine themselves to be among Allah’s chosen allies, though they are among His bitterest enemies. At other times, they use these fabricated reports to justify inventions that contradict the religion of Islam, claiming that these are among the secrets of the elite, as the heretics, Qarmatians, and Bātiniyyah (esotericists) do. At still other times, they use them to justify turning away from Allah’s Book and His Prophet’s Sunnah towards their own innovations, making their religion an amusement and a game.

In short, it is necessarily known in Islam that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not prescribe for the righteous, devout worshippers, and ascetics of his community to gather to listen to poetry sung to melodies, accompanied by clapping, beating time with a stick, or playing a frame drum. Nor did he permit anyone to abandon following him and adhering to the Book and wisdom he brought, whether inwardly or outwardly, whether an ordinary person or one of the elite. However, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did permit certain forms of amusement at weddings and similar occasions, such as allowing women to play frame drums at weddings and celebrations.

As for the men of his time, none of them played a frame drum or clapped their hands. Rather, it is authentically reported that he said:

“Clapping is for women, and saying ‘Glory be to Allah’ is for men.”

He also cursed women who imitate men and men who imitate women.

Since singing, playing the frame drum, and clapping were activities performed by women, the early generations would call a man who did these things effeminate, and they called men

---

## Page 5911

who sang “effeminates.” This is well known in their statements. Related to this is the report concerning ‘Ā’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her:

“When her father—may Allah be pleased with him—visited her during the days of Eid, two young girls from the Ansār were with her, singing verses that the Ansār had exchanged on the day of Bu‘āth. Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said, ‘The devil’s pipe in the house of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had turned away from them, his noble face towards the wall. He said, ‘Leave them, Abū Bakr, for every people has a festival, and this is our festival, the people of Islam.’”

This hadith makes clear that gathering for this was not the customary practice of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions. That is why al-Siddīq called it the devil’s pipe. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, allowed the young girls to continue, explaining that it was a day of Eid. Children are permitted to play during festivals, as stated in the hadith:

“So that the polytheists may know that there is room for enjoyment in our religion.”

‘Ā’ishah had dolls with which she played, and her young female friends would come and play with her. Nothing in the hadith about the two girls states that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, deliberately listened to this. Commands and prohibitions concern listening, not merely hearing. The same applies to seeing: they concern looking deliberately, not what one happens to see involuntarily. Likewise, regarding smelling perfume, a pilgrim in ritual consecration is forbidden only to smell it deliberately. If he smells something without intending to, no blame attaches to him. The same applies to direct contact with forbidden things, as with the senses

---

## Page 5912

—five in all: hearing, sight, smell, taste, and touch. Commands and prohibitions concerning these apply only to what a person intends and does deliberately. What occurs without his choice is subject to neither command nor prohibition.

This distinction is one explanation offered for the hadith in the Sunan collections, reported from Ibn ‘Umar:

“He was with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when the Prophet heard the sound of a shepherd’s pipe. He turned away from the path and asked, ‘Can you hear it? Can you hear it?’ until the sound ceased.”

Some people say, “Assuming this hadith is authentic, he did not instruct Ibn ‘Umar to cover his ears.” One answer is that Ibn ‘Umar was young; another is that he was not deliberately listening but merely hearing, which involves no sin. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, acted as he did only to pursue what was better and more perfect. This is like someone passing along a road who hears people engaging in forbidden speech and covers his ears so as not to hear it. This is commendable, but he would not sin if he did not cover his ears—unless hearing it would harm his religion in a way that could only be prevented by covering them.

In short, this is the question of listening to singing. Many later scholars have discussed such listening: is it prohibited, disliked, or permissible? What they intend is not merely to establish that it is free of blame. Rather, they intend that it be adopted as a path to Allah, around which religious people gather to reform their hearts and awaken longing for the Beloved

---

## Page 5913

and instill fear of what is dreaded and sorrow over missing what is sought. Through it, mercy is brought down, blessings are drawn forth, the spiritual emotions of the faithful are stirred, and the contemplative experiences of those endowed with spiritual knowledge are brought into clearer view. Some even say that, for certain people—or for the spiritual elite—it is superior to listening to the Quran in several respects. They even make it sustenance for hearts, nourishment for spirits, and a guide for souls, urging them onward in their journey to Allah and encouraging them to turn to Him.

Thus, one finds that those who have become accustomed to it and nourished themselves on it neither yearn for the Quran nor rejoice in it. They do not experience, when listening to verses of revelation, what they experience when listening to verses of poetry. Rather, when they hear the Quran, they hear it with heedless hearts and tongues engaged in idle talk. Yet when they listen to whistling and clapping, their voices grow hushed, their movements become still, and their hearts listen intently and partake of the drink.

Anyone who discusses this by asking, “Is it disliked or permissible?” and likens it to the songs women used to sing at festivals and celebrations has not grasped the distinction between the paths of those who suffer loss and those who attain success. And anyone who discusses this by asking, “Is it part of religion? Is it among the forms of listening practised by the God-fearing, the spiritual states of those brought near to Allah and those who follow a moderate course, the deeds of those possessed of certainty, the path of those who love Allah and are loved by Him, or the practices of those journeying to the Lord of all worlds?” speaks at a far remove from the issue. He is like someone who is asked about the disputed discipline of speculative theology—“Is it praiseworthy or blameworthy?”—and begins to

---

## Page 5914

discuss speech in general and its division into nouns, verbs, and particles; or speak in praise of silence, or about Allah having permitted speech and utterance, and similar matters that do not address the unclear point under dispute.

With this understood, know that in the early era of the three favored generations, none of those distinguished by religious devotion, righteousness, asceticism, and worship—in the Hijaz, Syria, Yemen, Egypt, the Maghrib, Iraq, or Khurasan—would gather for such listening to whistling and clapping, whether accompanied by a frame drum, handclapping, or the beating of a stick. This was only introduced later, toward the end of the second century AH. When the imams encountered it, they condemned it.

Al-Shāfi'ī—may Allah be pleased with him—said: “I left behind in Baghdad something introduced by the heretics, which they call ‘taghbīr’ (devotional chanting), by which they turn people away from the Quran.”

Yazīd ibn Hārūn said: “None but an openly sinful person engages in taghbīr. And since when has there been taghbīr?”

Imam Ahmad was asked about it and said: “I dislike it; it is an innovation.”

He was asked: “Should we sit with them?”

He replied: “No.”

Likewise, the other imams of religion disapproved of it, and the foremost righteous shaykhs did not attend it. Neither Ibrāhīm ibn Adham, al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyād, Ma'rūf al-Karkhī, Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī, Ahmad ibn Abī al-Hiwārī, al-Sarī al-Saqatī, nor others like them attended it. As for those who did attend it from among the

---

## Page 5915

praiseworthy shaykhs, they abandoned it toward the end of their lives. Leading shaykhs censured its practitioners, as did 'Abd al-Qādir, Shaykh Abū al-Bayān, and others. Al-Shāfi'ī’s statement—may Allah be pleased with him—that it was introduced by heretics is the judgment of an imam well versed in the foundations of Islam. For those who originally desired and promoted this listening were none other than men suspected of heresy, such as Ibn al-Rāwandī, al-Fārābī, Ibn Sīnā, and their like.

As Abū 'Abd al-Rahmān al-Sulamī related from Ibn al-Rāwandī in his discussion of listening, he said: “The jurists differed over listening: some permitted it and others disapproved of it. I, however, deem it obligatory”—or he said, “I command it.” Thus, by commanding it, he opposed the consensus of the scholars.

Al-Fārābī was highly accomplished in singing, which they call “music,” and had a method recognized among practitioners of the art of singing. His story with Ibn Hamdān is well known: he played and made them weep, then made them laugh, then put them to sleep, and then left.

In his al-Ishārāt (Pointers), in the section “The Stations of the Gnostics,” Ibn Sīnā encouraged this listening and passionate love of beautiful forms in terms consistent with the way of his predecessors: the philosophers and the polytheistic Sabians who worshipped the stars and idols, such as Aristotle and his Greek adherents, and those who followed him, including Proclus, Themistius, and Alexander of Aphrodisias. Aristotle was the minister of Alexander son of Philip of Macedon

---

## Page 5916

, from whom the Jews and Christians reckon their dates, and who lived about three hundred years before Christ. As for “Dhū al-Qarnayn,” mentioned in the Quran as the builder of the “barrier,” he lived long before these men. The Alexander whom Aristotle served as minister reached only Khurasan and nearby lands within the Persian Empire; he did not reach the barrier. These matters are discussed at length elsewhere.

“Ibn Sīnā” devised a philosophy combining the teachings of his Greek predecessors with what he adopted from the speculative theologians who introduced religious innovations, such as the Jahmiyyah and others like them. He followed the path of the heretical Ismā'īlīs in many of their theoretical and practical matters, blending this with some Sufi teachings. In essence, his philosophy comes back to the teachings of his Ismā'īlī, Qarmatian, esotericist brethren. His family were Ismā'īlīs, followers of al-Hākim in Egypt, and lived in his time. Their religion was that of the authors of the “Epistles of the Brethren of Purity” and others like them among the leading hypocrites of the nations, who are neither Muslims, Jews, nor Christians.

Al-Fārābī had mastered Greek letters—the teachings of Aristotle and his followers among the Peripatetic philosophers—and their musical sounds, namely the art of singing. Among these groups, then, are those who favor it and regard it as a means of purifying and disciplining souls and refining character.

---

## Page 5917

As for the “upright monotheists”—the followers of the religion of Abraham, Allah’s intimate friend, whom Allah made a leader, and the adherents of Islam, the only religion Allah accepts from anyone, who follow the revealed law of Muhammad, the final Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace—none of them favors such singing or advocates it. These are the people of the Quran, faith, guidance, blessedness, sound judgment, light, and success; the people of spiritual knowledge, learning, certainty, sincerity, love for Allah, reliance upon Him, fear of Him, and penitent devotion to Him.

Yet some spiritual aspirants and others with a measure of love for Allah have attended such gatherings because of how the singing stirs them, unaware of its dangers and unacquainted with its consequences. Similarly, some jurists who believe in what the Messenger brought have embraced various philosophical teachings contrary to Islam, supposing them to be true and consistent with it, unaware of their dangers and unacquainted with their consequences.

Most people cannot fully realize the realities of religion in knowledge, spiritual state, speech, action, spiritual understanding, inward experience, and practical familiarity. The comprehensive guide, however, is to hold fast to the Quran and the Sunnah. For Allah sent Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with guidance and the religion of truth, so that He might cause it to prevail over all religion. And sufficient is Allah as a witness.

Allah Most High has said:

“Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favor upon you, and approved Islam for you as your religion.”

And Allah Most High has said: “And this is My path

---

## Page 5918

—straight—so follow it, and do not follow other paths, lest they lead you away from His path.”

‘Abd Allāh ibn Mas‘ūd said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, drew a line for us, then drew other lines to its right and left. He then said: ‘This is Allah’s path. These are other paths, each with a devil calling people to it.’ Then he recited: ‘And this is My path, which is straight, so follow it, and do not follow other paths, lest they lead you away from His path.’”

Allah Most High has also said:

“The first forerunners among the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them in righteousness—Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him.”

Thus, Allah declared His pleasure with the forerunners unconditionally, and His pleasure with those who follow them in righteousness.

‘Abd Allāh ibn Mas‘ūd said: “Allah looked into the heart of Muhammad and found his heart to be the best of His servants’ hearts, so He chose him to bear His message. Then He looked into the hearts of people after his and found the hearts of his Companions to be the best of His servants’ hearts. Whatever the believers consider good is good in Allah’s sight, and whatever they consider bad is bad in Allah’s sight.”

‘Abd Allāh ibn Mas‘ūd also said: “Whoever among you wishes to follow an example should follow those who have died, for the living cannot be considered immune to trials. Those were the Companions of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: the most righteous of this community in heart, the deepest in knowledge, and the least given to affectation. They were people whom Allah chose to accompany His Prophet and uphold His religion. So recognize what is due to them and hold fast to their guidance, for they followed straight and true guidance.”

Anyone with practical knowledge of the realities of religion and of the hearts’ spiritual states, understanding, inward experiences, and ecstasies knows that listening to whistling and handclapping brings hearts no benefit or good without also entailing harm

---

## Page 5919

and corruption outweighing that benefit. Such listening is to the spirit what wine is to the body: it acts upon souls as the intoxicating force of wine does. Hence it leaves its devotees more intoxicated than wine does: they experience pleasure without discernment, just as a wine drinker does. Indeed, what they experience is more abundant and intense than what the wine drinker experiences. It turns them away from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer more powerfully than wine does, and causes greater enmity and hatred among them than wine does, until some kill others without even touching them with a hand, but rather through the devils that attach themselves to them.

They experience satanic states in which devils descend upon them and speak through their tongues, just as a jinn speaks through the tongue of someone possessed. This may be speech resembling that of non-Arabs whose language is not understood, such as Turkish, Persian, or another language, even though the person possessed by the devil is an Arab who cannot speak that language. Rather, the speech resembles that of those who are brethren of those devils. Alternatively, it may be speech that makes no sense and has no intelligible meaning. Those who experience spiritual unveiling know this through “direct witnessing and firsthand observation.”

Those who enter fire despite their departure from the Sharia belong to this category. Devils possess such a person so completely that his body loses sensation. Indeed, someone possessed may be beaten severely, yet he does not feel it, nor

---

## Page 5920

does it leave a mark on his skin. Likewise, devils possess these people and take them into fire; they may also carry them through the air. Such a person becomes possessed by a devil only when his reason is absent, just as a devil possesses someone who suffers seizures.

In India and the Maghrib, there is a group among the Zutt whose members are called al-muslā. Such a person exposes himself to fire just as these people do. Devils possess him, and he enters the fire, flies through the air, stands on the tip of a spear’s metal butt, and performs feats even more extraordinary than theirs. They belong to the Zutt, who have no share of goodness. The jinn abduct many human beings, conceal them from people’s sight, and carry them through the air. We have dealt firsthand with instances of these matters that would take a long time to describe.

The same things are done by those lost in ecstasy and those affiliated with certain shaykhs when they experience an ecstatic state induced by listening. While listening to whistling and clapping, some rise into the air, stand on the metal butt of a spear, enter fire, or take iron heated in fire and place it against their bodies, along with other feats of this kind. Yet they do not experience this state during prayer, the remembrance of Allah, or the recitation of the Quran. These are acts of worship prescribed by the Sharia, grounded in faith and Islam, and following the prophetic way of Muhammad; they drive devils away. Those other practices, however, are innovated, polytheistic, satanic, and philosophical forms of worship that attract devils.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in an authentic hadith:

“No people gather in one of the houses of Allah, reciting the Book of Allah and studying it together, without

---

## Page 5921

mercy enveloping them, tranquillity descending upon them, the angels surrounding them, and Allah mentioning them among those with Him.”

It is also established in an authentic hadith that “when Usayd ibn Hudayr recited Surah al-Kahf, the angels descended to listen to it, like a canopy containing lamps.”

Thus, whistling and clapping incite indecency and wrongdoing and turn people away from true remembrance of Allah Most High and prayer, just as wine does. The early generations called this taghbīr (rhythmic chanting), for taghbīr involves beating a piece of hide with a stick, accompanied by the human voice chanting melodically. The voice may be accompanied by clapping one hand against the other, striking a thigh or hide with a stick, or striking one hand against the other or otherwise beating a tambourine or drum, like the Christians’ bell; or by blowing a whistle, like the Jews’ horn. Whoever engages in these amusements as a religious practice and a means of drawing near to Allah is undoubtedly misguided and ignorant.

As for engaging in them for enjoyment and amusement, the four imams held that all instruments of entertainment are forbidden. It is established in Sahīh al-Bukhārī and elsewhere that “the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, foretold that some people of his community would deem illicit sexual relations, silk, wine, and musical instruments lawful, and mentioned that they would be transformed into apes and pigs.”

Maʿāzif means instruments of entertainment, as the lexicographers explain. It is the plural of miʿzafa, an instrument that is played—that is, used to produce sound. No one among

---

## Page 5922

the followers of the imams has reported any disagreement concerning instruments of entertainment. However, some later followers of al-Shāfiʿī recorded two views regarding the reed flute, unlike stringed instruments and the like, concerning which they reported no disagreement. The Iraqi scholars, who were more knowledgeable about his school and followed it more closely, reported no disagreement concerning either. Indeed, the foremost of them in his time, Abū al-Tayyib al-Tabarī, the teacher of Abū Ishāq al-Shīrāzī, wrote a well-known work on the subject.

They did, however, discuss singing unaccompanied by instruments of entertainment: is it forbidden, disliked, or permissible? Ahmad’s followers mentioned three views within their school on this matter and reported two views from al-Shāfiʿī. They reported no disagreement on the matter from Abū Hanīfa or Mālik. Zakariyyā ibn Yahyā al-Sājī—one of the early imams who inclined towards al-Shāfiʿī’s school—stated that, among the early jurists, only Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd of Basra dissented on this matter.

What Abū ʿAbd al-Rahmān al-Sulamī, Abū al-Qāsim al-Qushayrī, and others reported from Mālik and the people of Medina on this subject is mistaken. The confusion arose only because some people of Medina used to attend gatherings of singing. This, however, was not the position of their imams and jurists. Rather, Ishāq ibn ʿĪsā al-Tibāʿ said:

“I asked Mālik about the singing in which the people of Medina allow themselves latitude. He replied, ‘Among us, only the sinful engage in it.’”

This is well known among the authors of Mālik’s school, who are more knowledgeable about his school and that of the people of Medina than a group in

---

## Page 5923

the East who have no knowledge of the jurists’ positions. Anyone who claims that Mālik played the lute has fabricated a lie against him. I draw attention to this only because the material compiled on this subject by Abū ʿAbd al-Rahmān al-Sulamī and Muhammad ibn Tāhir al-Maqdisī contains accounts and reports that someone unfamiliar with scholarship and the lives of the early Muslims might suppose to be true.

“Shaykh Abū ʿAbd al-Rahmān”—may Allah have mercy on him—possessed goodness, asceticism, religious devotion, and commitment to Sufism that prompted him to collect every saying of the shaykhs and every report he could find that served his purpose. Thus, his books contain authentic reports and transmitted sayings that are beneficial in religious matters. They also contain unsound reports and objectionable statements that harm those without the knowledge to assess them. Some scholars expressed reservations about his transmission of reports. Indeed, when al-Bayhaqī narrated from him, he would say:

“Abū ʿAbd al-Rahmān related to us from his original record of what he had heard.”

Most of the accounts narrated by Abū al-Qāsim al-Qushayrī, author of al-Risāla (The Epistle), come from him, for among al-Qushayrī’s shaykhs he had made the most extensive collection of Sufi sayings.

“Muhammad ibn Tāhir” possessed considerable merit through his knowledge of hadith and its transmitters, and he was one of the hadith masters of his time. However, many later scholars—whether specialists in hadith, ascetics, jurists, or others—would, when writing on a subject, include whatever had been narrated concerning it, sound and unsound alike, without distinguishing between them. This can be found among those who compile works on particular subjects, such as the merits of months and particular times, and the merits of deeds

---

## Page 5924

and acts of worship, the merits of individuals, and other such topics. Examples include what some have written on the merits of Rajab, and what others have written on the merits of prayers for particular days and nights: the Sunday prayer, the Monday prayer, the Tuesday prayer, the prayer on the first Friday of Rajab, the Alfiyya prayer of Rajab, prayer at the beginning of Rajab, the Alfiyya prayer of mid-Shaʿbān, spending the nights preceding the two Eids in worship, and the prayer on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ.

The best report concerning these prayers is the hadith about the prayer of glorification, narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī. Yet none of the four imams endorsed it. Indeed, Ahmad judged the hadith weak and did not recommend these prayers. As for Ibn al-Mubārak, the form of prayer reported from him differs from that attributed to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The form attributed to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, does not include a lengthy sitting after the second prostration. This conflicts with established principles, so such a prayer cannot be established on the basis of a hadith like this. Anyone who carefully considers those principles will know that it is fabricated.

These and similar reports are all fabricated lies, as the experts unanimously agree, although they appear in works such as the book of Abū Tālib, the book of Abū Hāmid, and the book of Shaykh ʿAbd al-Qādir. They also appear in works such as the dictations of Abū al-Qāsim ibn ʿAsākir and the writings of ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Kinānī, Abū ʿAlī ibn al-Bannā, Abū al-Fadl ibn Nāsir, and others. Likewise,

---

## Page 5925

Abū al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzī mentions similar reports in his work on the merits of the months, yet states in al-Mawdūʿāt (Fabricated Hadiths) that they are lies and fabrications. Those who compile hadiths on asceticism and heart-softening exhortations include whatever has been narrated on these subjects. Among the most distinguished and exceptional works in this field is Kitāb al-Zuhd (The Book of Asceticism) by ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak, though it contains very weak hadiths. The same applies to the books on asceticism by Hannād ibn al-Sarī, Asad ibn Mūsā, and others.

The finest work in this field is al-Zuhd by Imam Ahmad. However, it is arranged by individuals’ names, whereas Ibn al-Mubārak’s al-Zuhd is arranged by subject. These books describe the asceticism of the prophets, the Companions, and the Successors.

Later authors fall into two groups. Some describe the asceticism of both earlier and later generations, such as Abū Nuʿaym in al-Hilya and Abū al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzī in Sifat al-Safwa. Others confine themselves to later figures, beginning with the emergence of the designation “Sufis,” as Abū ʿAbd al-Rahmān al-Sulamī does in Tabaqāt al-Sūfiyya (The Generations of the Sufis), and his associate Abū al-Qāsim al-Qushayrī in al-Risāla (The Epistle). As for those who relate these stories on their own, such as Ibn Khamīs and others like him, they recount accounts without chains of transmission: some are authentic and others false.

---

## Page 5926

An example is their claim that al-Hasan kept company with 'Alī. Yet the experts agree that al-Hasan al-Basrī neither met 'Alī nor learned anything from him. Rather, he learned from 'Alī’s companions, such as al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, Qays ibn Mu'ādh, and others.

The same applies to their accounts that al-Shāfi'ī and Ahmad met Shaybān the shepherd and asked him about the prostrations of forgetfulness. The experts likewise agree that al-Shāfi'ī and Ahmad never met Shaybān the shepherd; indeed, they did not even live in his time.

In Haqā'iq al-Tafsīr (The Realities of Quranic Exegesis), Abū 'Abd al-Rahmān relates sayings attributed to Ja'far ibn Muhammad and others which the experts know were falsely attributed to Ja'far ibn Muhammad. More lies have been attributed to Ja'far than to anyone else, for Allah had distinguished him with knowledge and religious devotion. He, his father Abū Ja'far, and his grandfather 'Alī ibn al-Husayn were among the foremost imams in knowledge and religious devotion. No one like Ja'far appeared among the Prophet’s household after him.

Consequently, many heretics and religious innovators began attributing their own doctrines to him. Even the authors of Rasā'il Ikhwān al-Safā (The Epistles of the Brethren of Purity) attribute these epistles to him. Yet they were composed more than two hundred years after his death, when the doctrine of the Ismā'īlī 'Ubaydids, who built Cairo, emerged. They were composed according to their doctrine, which they pieced together from the teachings of the Greek philosophers, the Persian Magians, and the Shī'a within the Muslim community. Hence the scholars said:

“Their doctrine is outwardly Rāfidism, but inwardly pure unbelief.”

---

## Page 5927

They also claimed that Ja'far discussed foreknowledge of worldly events through such things as bodily twitching, thunder, lightning, al-Haft, and other matters which Allah kept Ja'far and the imams of his household far above discussing. This has been explained at length elsewhere.

And (the point here is that one should distinguish sound reports from weak ones among those transmitted from the early generations of this community and its imams. The same discernment is required in rational arguments and theoretical reasoning, as well as in spiritual experiences, ecstatic states, unveilings, and inward communications. Each of these three categories contains truth and falsehood, and these must be distinguished in every category. The comprehensive principle is this: whatever agrees with Allah’s Book, the authentically established Sunnah of His Messenger, and the way of his Companions is true; whatever contradicts these is false.

For Allah says:

“O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you. If you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is best and most excellent in outcome.”

And the Most High says:

“Mankind was one community; then Allah sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners, and sent down with them the Scripture in truth to judge between people concerning their differences. None differed over it except those who had been given it, after clear proofs had come to them, out of mutual envy. Then Allah guided those who believed, regarding their differences, to

---

## Page 5928

the truth, by His permission. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.”

In Sahīh Muslim, ‘Ā’ishah—may Allah be pleased with her—reports that when the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—rose to pray at night, he would say:

“O Allah, Lord of Gabriel, Michael, and Isrāfīl, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen! You judge between Your servants concerning their differences. Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth concerning which they differ. Indeed, You guide whom You will to a straight path.”

These matters are discussed at length elsewhere. We have discussed the shaykhs’ statements concerning samāʿ (listening), as related by al-Qushayrī in his Epistle and by others, and have explained them word by word. This, however, is not the place for such an extensive discussion.

The essential point is this: when discussing whether samāʿ or anything else constitutes an act of obedience and a means of drawing near to Allah, there must be evidence from Islamic law establishing that. Likewise, when discussing whether it is forbidden or not, there must be evidence from Islamic law establishing that. For nothing is forbidden except what Allah has forbidden, and nothing is part of religion except what Allah has prescribed.

Allah—glorified and exalted is He—has condemned the polytheists for inventing a religion He had not prescribed for them and for forbidding what Allah Most High had not forbidden. The Most High says:

---

## Page 5929

“Or do they have partners who have prescribed for them a religion that Allah has not authorized?”

The Most High also says:

“When they commit an indecency, they say, ‘We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it.’ Say, ‘Allah does not command indecency. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?’”

“Say, ‘My Lord has commanded justice. Direct your faces toward Him at every place of worship, and call upon Him, devoting your worship sincerely to Him.’”

Many people, in samāʿ and other practices, engage in forbidden indecencies and things that lead to them, claiming that these reform the hearts and are therefore among the things Allah has commanded. Such people fall, to some extent, within the meaning of this verse.

The Most High says:

“Say, ‘Who has forbidden the adornment Allah has brought forth for His servants, and the good things He has provided?’ Say, ‘They are for the believers in this worldly life, and exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection.’ Thus do We make Our signs clear for people who know.”

“Say, ‘My Lord has only forbidden indecencies, whether open or hidden; sin; unjust aggression; associating with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority; and saying about Allah what you do not know.’”

The polytheists used to forbid certain foods and garments, making this part of their religion. Some of the Companions had also resolved to embrace monasticism, so Allah Most High revealed:

“O you who believe, do not forbid the good things Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors.”

“And eat of what Allah has provided for you, lawful and good”—to the end of the verse.

---

## Page 5930

The essence of religion is to worship Allah alone, to worship Him only as He has prescribed, and not to worship Him through religious innovations. As the Most High says:

“To test you as to which of you is best in deeds.”

Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyād said: “The most sincere and the most correct.” They asked, “Abū ‘Alī, what does ‘the most sincere and the most correct’ mean?”

He replied: “If a deed is sincere but not correct, it will not be accepted. If it is correct but not sincere, it will not be accepted. It must be both sincere and correct. Sincerity means that it is done for Allah, and correctness means that it accords with the Sunnah.”

What al-Fudayl stated is something upon which the leading spiritual masters agreed. Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said: “An insight of the kind spoken of by these spiritual masters may occur to my heart, but I do not accept it without two witnesses: the Book and the Sunnah.”

Shaykh Abū Sulaymān also said: “Someone inspired to do something good must not act upon it until he hears a transmitted report supporting it. Once he hears such a report, it is light upon light.”

Al-Junayd said: “This knowledge of ours is bound by the Book and the Sunnah. Whoever has not read the Quran and written down hadith is not qualified to speak about this knowledge of ours.”

Sahl ibn ‘Abdullāh al-Tustarī said: “Every spiritual experience unsupported by the Book and the Sunnah is false.” He also said: “Every deed founded on religious innovation is a torment to the soul, and every deed done without following the prophetic example is self-deception.”

## Page 5931
