Statements like these abound in their words. Since this is so, no one may follow a path to Allah except through what the Messenger has prescribed for his community. He is the one who calls to Allah by His permission and guides to His path. Whoever obeys him will enter Paradise, and whoever disobeys him will enter the Fire. Through him, Allah has distinguished truth from falsehood, guidance from misguidance, and right conduct from waywardness.

Such listening is also recommended for them outside the prayers. It is reported of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that “he came out to the people of the Suffa, among whom one man was reciting while the others were

## Page 5935

listening, and he sat with them.”

When the Companions of Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gathered together, they would ask one of them to recite while the rest listened. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb, may Allah be pleased with him, would say, “Abū Mūsā, remind us of our Lord.” He would then recite while they listened.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by Abū Mūsā while he was reciting and began listening to his recitation. He said, “This man has indeed been granted a voice like one of David’s flutes.” He also said, “Abū Mūsā, I passed by you last night while you were reciting, and I began listening to your recitation.” He replied, “Had I known that you were listening to my recitation, I would have made it truly beautiful for you”—meaning that he would have beautified it for him.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever does not recite the Quran melodiously is not one of us.”

“Beautify the Quran with your voices.”

He also said:

“Allah listens far more attentively to a man with a beautiful voice than the owner of a singing slave-girl listens to her.”

In his words, “Allah has never listened so intently…,” the expression means hearing. The same usage occurs in Allah’s words:

“And has listened to its Lord, as it must.”

That is, it has heard. There are many reports concerning this.

Such listening produces effects that nourish faith, including sacred insights and pure spiritual states whose explanation and description would be lengthy. It also has praiseworthy bodily effects: humility of the heart, tears in the eyes, and shuddering of the skin. Allah has mentioned these three in the Quran, and they were found among the Companions of Allah’s Messenger

---

## Page 5936

may Allah bless him and grant him peace—those whom Allah praised in the Quran. After them, three effects appeared among the Successors: agitation, convulsions, and fainting—or death and frenzy. Some of the early scholars disapproved of this, either because of their innovation or because of their love. Most leading scholars and early authorities, however, did not disapprove of it: when the cause is not prohibited, a person is excused for its consequences.

The reason for this, however, is the intensity of what comes upon their hearts and their hearts’ inability to bear it. Had listening failed to affect them because of their hardness of heart, they would have been blameworthy, just as Allah condemned those of whom He said:

“Then your hearts became hardened after that.”

He also said:

“Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of Allah and what has come down of the truth? And let them not be like those who were given the Scripture before, whose hearts hardened as time passed, and many of whom are defiantly disobedient.”

If listening produced praiseworthy effects in them without taking them beyond the bounds of reason, they would be like those whom it brought to the point of being overwhelmed: they too would be praiseworthy and excused.

As for those who gather to listen with the aim of reforming their hearts—whether to unaccompanied chanting resembling ghubār, or to chanting accompanied by clapping and the like—this is a form of listening newly introduced into Islam. It arose only after the passing of the three generations praised by the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he said:

“The best generations are the generation in which I was sent, then those who follow them, then those who follow them.”

Leading figures of the Muslim community disapproved of it, and the foremost shaykhs did not attend it.

---

## Page 5937

And al-Shāfiʿī—may Allah have mercy on him—said: “I left behind in Baghdad something introduced by heretics, which they call taghbīr and use to turn people away from the Quran.”

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal was asked about it and said: “It is an innovation; I dislike it.” He was told: “But it softens the heart.” He replied: “Do not sit with them.” He was asked: “Should they be shunned?” He replied: “It should not go that far with them.”

He thus made clear that it was an innovation not practised by the virtuous early generations, whether in the Hijaz, Syria, Yemen, Egypt, Iraq, or Khurāsān. Had it benefited Muslims in their religion, the early generations would have practised it.

Such figures as Ibrāhīm ibn Adham, al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyād, Maʿrūf al-Karkhī, al-Sarī al-Saqatī, and Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī did not attend it; nor did such figures as Shaykh ʿAbd al-Qādir, Shaykh ʿAdī, Shaykh Abū al-Bayān, Shaykh Hayāt, and others. Indeed, the statements of some of these figures—such as Shaykh ʿAbd al-Qādir and others—contain prohibitions against it. The foremost shaykhs likewise forbade it.

Some shaykhs did attend it, stipulating a suitable place, favourable circumstances, companions, and a shaykh who would guard against Satan. Most of the trustworthy shaykhs who attended it renounced it late in life. Al-Junayd, for example, attended it as a young man but withdrew from their company late in life.

He used to say: “Whoever deliberately seeks out such listening

---

## Page 5938

will be led astray by it, whereas whoever encounters it by chance finds relief in it.” Thus, he censured those who gather for it, while allowing it for those who encounter it unintentionally, without deliberately sitting down to listen.

The reason is that its language is general and lacks specificity. Verses mentioning love, union, estrangement, separation, longing, enslavement to love, patiently enduring reproach and blame, and similar themes employ general expressions equally applicable to those who love the Most Merciful, idols, brethren, homelands, women, or beardless youths. Such listening may therefore contain some benefit when it stirs what dwells within and rouses what lies dormant, provided that what it arouses is something Allah and His Messenger love.

Its harm, however, outweighs its benefit, as is the case with wine and gambling: in both there is great sin and benefits for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit. This is why the revealed Law did not prescribe it: it prescribes only what is wholly or predominantly beneficial. Anything whose harm outweighs its benefit is like taking one dirham in exchange for a dinar, or stealing five dirhams and giving two of them in charity.

For such listening arouses the fervour common to these different kinds of love, stirring latent impulses within the soul whose effects harm it. It feeds the soul and tempts it, so that the soul substitutes it for listening to the Quran, until it retains no love for listening to the Quran and finds neither pleasure nor delight in it. Rather,

---

## Page 5939

the soul is left with an aversion to it and is distracted from it. This is like someone who occupies himself with studying the Torah, the Gospel, and the learning of the People of the Book and the Sabians, drawing knowledge and wisdom from them, and thereby turning away from Allah’s Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger to other matters too lengthy to detail. Since such listening does not in itself impart the spiritual states and knowledge that Allah and His Messenger love—and may instead obstruct them and impart what Allah and His Messenger do not love, or even what they hate—neither Allah nor His Messenger, nor the early generations of this community nor its foremost spiritual teachers, commanded it.

One subtle point here is that sound affects the soul through its beauty: sometimes it brings joy, sometimes sorrow, sometimes anger, and sometimes contentment. When its effect becomes strong, it intoxicates the spirit, which then experiences an exhilarating pleasure without discernment. Something similar happens to the soul when it becomes intoxicated through dancing, and also to the body when it becomes intoxicated through food and drink. For intoxication is an exhilaration that produces pleasure without reason. The benefit afforded by that pleasure cannot compensate for the resulting loss of reason, which hinders remembrance of Allah and prayer and breeds enmity and hatred.

“In short,” a believer must know that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, left nothing that brings one nearer to Paradise without speaking of it, nor anything that keeps one away from

---

## Page 5940

the Fire without speaking of it, and that if this listening were beneficial, Allah and His Messenger would have prescribed it. For Allah says:

“This day I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favour upon you, and chosen Islam as your religion.”

If a believer finds that it benefits his heart but finds nothing in either the Book or the Sunnah to support it, he should pay it no heed.

Sahl ibn Abd Allāh al-Tustarī said:

“Every spiritual experience unsupported by the Book and the Sunnah is false.”

Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said:

“An insight of the spiritual masters may occur to my heart, but I accept it only with the testimony of two upright witnesses: the Book and the Sunnah.”

Abū Sulaymān also said:

“Someone inspired to do something good must not act upon it until he finds a transmitted report supporting it. Once he finds such a report, it becomes light upon light.”

Al-Junayd ibn Muhammad said:

“This knowledge of ours is bound by the Book and the Sunnah. Whoever has neither read the Quran nor written down hadith is not qualified to speak about this knowledge of ours.”

Furthermore, Allah says in the Book:

“Their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping.”

The early generations—the Companions and their successors—explained that mukā’ refers to whistling and similar vocal sounds, such as singing, while tasdiyah means clapping the hands. Allah has thus told us that the polytheists used to treat clapping

---

## Page 5941

and singing as their prayer, worship, and means of drawing near to Allah, substituting them for the prayer prescribed by Allah and His Messenger.

As for the Muslims—the Emigrants, the Helpers, and those who followed them in righteousness—their prayer and worship consist of reciting and listening to the Quran, bowing, prostrating, remembering Allah, supplicating to Him, and other such acts that Allah and His Messenger love. Whoever adopts singing and clapping as worship and a means of drawing near to Allah has thus imitated the polytheists and resembled them in practices foreign to the believers—the Emigrants and the Helpers. If he does this in the houses of Allah, his resemblance to them becomes greater still; and if he occupies himself with it instead of praying, remembering Allah, and supplicating to Him, his resemblance to them becomes profound. He thus incurs a considerable share of the censure indicated by the words of Allah, Glorified and Exalted:

“Their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping.”

Yet he may be forgiven for this on account of his exercise of independent judgment, good deeds that efface sins, or other grounds that distinguish a Muslim from a disbeliever. Nevertheless, his differing from the polytheists in other respects does not preclude his being blameworthy, departing from the Sharia, and engaging in the innovation through which he has imitated them. The believer should therefore be alert to this and distinguish between the listening of the believers, which Allah and His Messenger have commanded, and the listening of the polytheists, which Allah and His Messenger have forbidden.

---

## Page 5942

and recognize that this newly introduced form of listening belongs to the same category as the listening of the polytheists and is closer to it than to the listening of the Muslims. Although some righteous Muslims have erred in this matter, Allah does not allow their reward and righteousness to go to waste because of their error. For the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“When a judge exercises independent judgment and reaches the correct conclusion, he receives two rewards; when he exercises independent judgment and errs, he receives one reward.”

This is comparable to a group from the early generations who fought the Commander of the Faithful, Ali, on the basis of an interpretation, although Ali ibn Abī Tālib and his companions were closer to the truth than they were. He said of them: “Whoever sought Allah will have Paradise.” Likewise, some among the earlier and later generations considered certain drinks permissible on the basis of an interpretation—even though the Quran and Sunnah establish the prohibition of what they deemed permissible—although their error is forgiven them.

The righteous spiritual teachers who attended this form of listening stipulated conditions for it that are only rarely met. Thus, most such listening gatherings fall outside the terms upon which those teachers agreed. Even so, they erred—may Allah forgive them for their error in departing from the Sunnah—even though they were excused. The cause of their error led many communities into the wrongdoing that they forbade

## Page 5943

them to commit. There is no code, course, law, or path for all people more perfect than the law with which Allah sent His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. As he used to say in his sermons:

“The best speech is the speech of Allah, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.”

“Among their errors is the assumption that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, the Companions, and the Successors attended this form of listening—listening to whistling, clapping, singing, and the striking of palms together. This hadith is a lie by the consensus of those acquainted with the life, Sunnah, and circumstances of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. Likewise, some liars fabricated the claim that Ahl al-Suffa (the people of the shaded platform) fought against the believers alongside

---

## Page 5944

the polytheists. Such fabrications are invented only by those who have departed from the command of Allah and His Messenger, and are accepted by groups ignorant of the circumstances of the Messenger and his Companions—indeed, of the very foundations of Islam.

As for “dancing,” neither Allah nor His Messenger nor any of the imams commanded it. Rather, Allah says in His Book:

“Be moderate in your pace.”

He also says in His Book:

“The servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth humbly.”

That is, with tranquillity and dignity. The worship of Muslims consists instead of bowing and prostrating. Nor did Allah, His Messenger, or any of the early generations of this community command beating the frame drum and dancing in the tābaq. Rather, they commanded recitation of the Quran in prayer and tranquillity.

If a person is overcome by a spiritual state that carries him beyond what is prescribed, and that state arises from a prescribed cause, such as listening to the Quran or the like, he is excused for that state, as explained earlier. But it is otherwise if he deliberately resorts to means he has not been commanded to pursue, knowing that they will lead him into something improper for him—as when someone drinks wine knowing that it will intoxicate him. If he says, “The state came over me while I was drunk,” he is told, “When the cause is prohibited, the intoxicated person is not excused.”

Thus, anyone who genuinely experiences these corrupt states is a misguided innovator, akin to the enemy’s guards and the helpers of oppressors among those possessing corrupt states, who resemble Christian, polytheist, and Sabian worshippers in some of their states,

---

## Page 5945

and anyone who falsely claims such states is a misguided hypocrite.

Al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyād, the foremost Muslim of his time, said concerning Allah’s words,

“to test you as to which of you is best in deed”:

“It means the most sincere and the most correct.”

He was asked, “Abū ʿAlī, what do ‘the most sincere’ and ‘the most correct’ mean?”

He replied, “If a deed is sincere but not correct, it will not be accepted; and if it is correct but not sincere, it will not be accepted. It must be both sincere and correct. Sincere means done for Allah, and correct means in accordance with the Sunnah.”

He also used to say, “Whoever honours an innovator has helped to undermine Islam. Whoever marries his daughter to an innovator has severed her ties of kinship. Whoever sternly rebukes an innovator, Allah will fill his heart with security and faith.”

When he and other spiritual masters referred to innovation, they generally meant innovations in acts of worship and spiritual states, as Allah said concerning the Christians:

“Monasticism they invented; We did not prescribe it for them.”

Ibn Masʿūd said:

“Adhere to the path and the Sunnah. No servant who follows the path and the Sunnah remembers Allah in solitude and shivers with fear of Him without his sins falling away from him as dry leaves fall from a tree. No servant who follows the path and the Sunnah remembers Allah in solitude and sheds tears out of fear of Him will ever be touched by the Fire. Indeed, moderation upon the path and the Sunnah is better than strenuous effort contrary to the path and the Sunnah. So take care that your deeds—whether marked by strenuous effort or moderation—follow the way of the prophets and their Sunnah.”

## Page 5946

Whoever does this is among the leaders of misguidance, concerning whose chiefs it was said:

## Page 5947

And if it is neither prescribed nor commanded, then purifying oneself for it or listening to it in silence and seeking the opening of the gate of mercy are akin to the practices of monks—not the worship of the people of Islam and faith, the people of the Quran, or the people of the Sunnah and spiritual excellence. ## Page 5948

He was asked:

Concerning someone who says, “Listening to music is unlawful for others but lawful for me”: does this make him defiantly sinful or not?

He replied—may Allah be pleased with him:

Anyone who claims that universally prohibited acts—such as indecencies, injustice, and musical amusements—are unlawful for others but lawful for him must be called upon to repent. If he repents, well and good; otherwise, he is to be put to death.

Anyone who claims that frame drums and flutes are unlawful for some people but not others contradicts the Sunnah, scholarly consensus, and the leading scholars of the religion. He is among those who have gone astray. Thus, whoever persists in such a claim is defiantly sinful. And Allah knows best.

---

## Page 5949

He was asked:

Concerning people who dance to singing accompanied by a frame drum, after which some prostrate to others as a gesture of humility: is this a practice of the Sunnah, or was it practised by the righteous shaykhs?

The answer:

It is not permissible to prostrate to anyone other than Allah. Treating drumming, singing, and dancing as worship is among the religious innovations that were practised neither by the early generations of this Ummah nor by its leading shaykhs, such as al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyād, Ibrāhīm ibn Adham, Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī, Maʿrūf al-Karkhī, al-Sarī al-Saqatī, and others.

Likewise, the leading shaykhs of later times—such as Shaykh ʿAbd al-Qādir, Shaykh ʿAdī, Shaykh Abū Madyan, Shaykh Abū al-Bayān, and others—did not attend “innovated listening sessions.” Rather, they attended “religiously prescribed listening sessions”: the kind of listening practised by the prophets and their followers, such as listening to the Quran. And Allah knows best.

---

## Page 5950

Shaykh al-Islām was asked:

About a man who loves listening sessions and dancing. Another man advised him, reciting these verses:

“They denounced dancing and declared it forbidden;
So for that, I bid them farewell.
Worship Allah, O jurist, and pray;
Adhere to the Sacred Law, for listening sessions are forbidden.
Rather, forbidden to you, yet lawful
For people whose spiritual states incur no blame—
Like those who became pure, to whom there appeared,
From the side of the Mount, a burning brand and speech.
But when listening is coupled with amusement,
It is forbidden to everyone—forbidden.”

The Answer

He replied:

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of all worlds. This poetry contains reprehensible speech and falsehood. Indeed, its beginning entails opposition to the Sacred Law, while its ending opens the door to heresy, unbelief, and opposition to divine, religious, and prophetic truth.

For the poet’s words:

“Like those who became pure, to whom there appeared,
From the side of the Mount, a burning brand and speech”

---

## Page 5951

entail likening these people to Moses son of ‘Imrān, who was called from the side of the Mount and who, when he saw the fire,

“said to his family, ‘Stay here; I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I can bring you some news from it, or a burning brand, so that you may warm yourselves.’”

This is the view of a group of people who follow the path of spiritual discipline and purification, believing that through it they can reach a point at which Allah addresses them as He addressed Moses son of ‘Imrān. These people fall into three categories:

“One group” claims that the words addressed to them are greater than those addressed to Moses son of ‘Imrān. Such claims are made by some adherents of oneness and union who maintain that existence is one, such as the author of al-Fusūs and others like him. They claim that they rank above the prophets and that the address they receive from Allah is greater than that received by Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad—may blessings and peace be upon them. It is well known that this unbelief is greater than the unbelief of the Jews and Christians, who regard the prophets as superior to others but believe in some prophets and disbelieve in others.

“The second category” consists of those who say that Allah speaks to them just as He spoke to Moses son of ‘Imrān. Such claims are made by some of the philosophers and Sufis who

---

## Page 5952

say that the speech addressed to Moses was an emanation flowing into his heart from the Active Intellect, and that prophethood can be acquired.

“The third category” consists of those who say that Moses is superior, but that someone practising spiritual discipline may hear the address that Moses heard. Moses, however, was its intended recipient, unlike this person. This is found in the accounts of the author of Mishkāt al-Anwār (The Niche of Lights). The author of Khalʿ al-Naʿlayn (The Removal of the Sandals) and others like them followed the same path.

As for his words at the beginning of the poem, addressed to his interlocutor:

“Adhere to the revealed law, O jurist, and pray,”

this suggests: you are bound to follow the revealed law, whereas we have another path to Allah. Whoever claims to have a path to Allah that leads to His pleasure, honour and reward, other than the law with which Allah sent His Messenger, is likewise an unbeliever. He must be called upon to repent; if he does not repent, he is to be beheaded. Such are a group who dispensed with religious obligations and claimed that a servant can reach Allah without following the messengers.

“Another group” believes that the elite among Allah’s close friends have no need to follow Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—just as al-Khidr had no need to follow Moses. These people fail to understand that Moses was not sent to al-Khidr, whereas Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—is a Messenger to everyone, in both outward and inward matters. Moreover, what al-Khidr did did not contravene the law of Moses; rather, it accorded with it. Moses simply did not know the circumstances that made those actions permissible. Once he learned them, it became clear that those actions accorded with his law rather than contravening it.

---

## Page 5953

He was also asked:

About those who perform feats with fire and put on displays involving arrows, saffron, and the like.

He replied:

As for those who put on “displays” involving arrows, saffron, musk, fire, and a robe, they are not among Allah’s righteous close friends. Rather, they belong to the factions of the devils. Their states are satanic, not miraculous gifts granted to the righteous. They corrupt minds, religious beliefs, and honour, as well as women and boys. Only someone steeped in ignorance, or an enemy of Allah and His Messenger, would think well of them. They are of the same kind as the Tatars who wage war against Allah and His Messenger. And Allah knows best.

---

## Page 5954

He was asked:

About a farmer whose religious observance and prayers are unknown. A shaykh in his town has given him authorization, and he has since taken to eating snakes and scorpions, abandoned farming, and begun seeking his livelihood. Is it permissible to give him charity or not?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. Eating foul things, including snakes and scorpions, is forbidden by the consensus of the Muslims. Whoever eats them while believing this to be lawful must be called upon to repent and, unless he repents, is to be put to death. Whoever believes that eating them is forbidden but nevertheless eats them is an evildoer who disobeys Allah and His Messenger. How, then, could he be a righteous man? Even if he ritually slaughtered a snake, eating it afterwards would remain forbidden according to the overwhelming majority of scholars, for the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“Five harmful creatures are to be killed both outside and within the Sacred Precinct: the snake, the scorpion, the kite, the mouse, and the vicious dog.”

The Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—thus commanded that these creatures be killed both outside and within the Sacred Precinct. He called them transgressors because they transgress—that is, they turn upon people and attack them, making it impossible to guard against them, just as one cannot guard against attacking beasts of prey. It follows that

---

## Page 5955

the aggression of these creatures is greater than that of any fanged beast of prey, and they are fouler and even more strictly forbidden to eat.

As for those who eat them and classify this as one of the “miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s allies,” they are worse than the evildoers who eat them. Such miraculous gifts cannot consist of eating foul things that Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, just as they cannot consist of abandoning religious obligations. Rather, these fraudulent feats performed by these innovators—entering fire, handling snakes, and producing labdanum, sugar, blood, and rosewater—are of two kinds.

The first consists of accomplishing these things through tricks involving natural means: for example, using certain known oils to go and walk through fire, or drinking something that counteracts snake venom. Other examples include grasping a snake by its ‘anqasah so that it cannot harm him, handling a water snake, or removing a snake’s skin and stuffing it with food. How many followers of these people have been killed by snakes! Another example is rubbing one’s skin with dragon’s-blood resin, so that, when one sweats during listening sessions, something resembling blood appears on the skin. All manner of tricks and deceptions are devised for them.

The second kind involves more formidable practitioners. They experience satanic states that come upon them during devilish listening sessions. Devils descend upon them just as they enter the body of a possessed person, and one of them becomes increasingly affected, as does a possessed person. He then comes into direct contact with fire and snakes

---

## Page 5956

and scorpions, and it is the devil who actually performs these acts. The same is done by their brethren whom devils accompany—those whom people regard as the worst of creatures, belonging to the group whom people seek out to treat the possessed, although people regard them as among the worst of creatures. When summoned, they dress as warriors, and jinn enter them and fight their counterparts inhabiting the possessed. People hear voices and see stones being thrown, but do not see who is doing this. They see the human standing on the tip of a long spear, whereas it is actually the devil who stands there. People see a fire being stoked, into which he places axes and hoes. The human then licks them with his tongue, whereas it is actually the devil who has entered him that does this.

People see these individuals handling snakes, vipers, and other creatures, and performing feats more remarkable than those performed by these misguided innovators who deny the truth and deceive others. They claim to be Allah’s allies, whereas they are among His enemies, neglecting His obligations and transgressing His limits. Because of these satanic and naturally produced phenomena, the ignorant suppose them to be Allah’s allies. Yet these phenomena are of the same kind as those experienced by Allah’s enemies among the disbelievers and evildoers.

None of these people may be assisted in neglecting what is commanded, doing what is forbidden, or establishing spiritual leadership contrary to the Quran and Sunnah. Nor may anyone give such a person his stipend for serving as a shaykh in a manner that takes him outside obedience to Allah and His Messenger. Rather, stipends are to support those who obey Allah and His Messenger and call others to obey Allah and His Messenger. And Allah knows best.

---

## Page 5957

He was asked:

A man remains secluded in his house, neither going out nor coming in. He prays at home and does not attend congregational prayers. When he goes out for Friday prayer, he covers his face. He also contrives bouts of shouting for no reason, and men and women gather around him. Should he be left as he is, or must his conduct be denounced?

He answered:

This way is an innovation, contrary to the Quran, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the Muslims. Allah Most High is to be worshipped only through what He has prescribed, not through innovations.

Allah Most High says:

“Or do they have partners who have ordained for them a religion which Allah has not permitted?”

Abandoning Friday and congregational prayers as an act of worship, believing that abstaining from them is unconditionally better than attending them, constitutes disbelief. Anyone who does this must be called upon to repent of it; unless he repents, he is to be put to death. For it is necessarily known in Islam that Allah is not worshipped by abandoning Friday and congregational prayers, but rather by performing them. Whoever makes withdrawal from these prayers a religious practice does not follow the religion of the Muslims. Rather, he resembles the monks who seclude themselves in hermitages and monasteries.

One such person may attain a kind of unveiling through ascetic discipline or through devils—by being brought close to them or otherwise. This does not benefit him; rather, he is a disbeliever in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Allah Most High has commanded His creatures to worship Him alone, associating nothing with Him

---

## Page 5958

and to worship Him as He has prescribed, and He has commanded them not to worship Him in any other way.

Allah Most High says:

“So whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and associate no one in the worship of his Lord.”

He also says:

“To test you as to which of you is best in deeds.”

Thus, someone following the path of asceticism and worship may outwardly adhere to the Sharia, yet seek to show off, gain publicity, and win people’s veneration. In that case, his deeds are invalid, and Allah does not accept them. As authentically reported, Allah says:

“I have no need whatsoever for partners. Whoever performs a deed in which he associates someone else with Me, I disavow it; it belongs entirely to the one he associated with Me.”

It is also authentically reported that the Prophet said:

“Whoever seeks publicity, Allah will expose him; whoever shows off, Allah will expose him.”

Even if his intention is sincere, but he worships through practices that have not been prescribed—such as remaining perpetually silent; continually standing in the sun or on a rooftop; habitually stripping off his clothes and confining himself to garments of wool, palm fibre, or similar materials; covering his face; or abstaining from eating bread or meat, drinking water, and the like—these acts of worship are invalid and rejected. As authentically reported from ‘Ā’ishah, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever introduces into this matter of ours something that does not belong to it, it is rejected.”

Another version reads:

“Whoever performs a deed that does not conform to our teaching, it is rejected.”

In Sahīh al-Bukhārī, Ibn ‘Abbās reported:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw a man standing in the sun and asked, ‘What is this?’ They replied, ‘This is Abū Isrā’īl. He has vowed to remain silent, to stand, and to remain exposed

---

## Page 5959

to the sun while fasting.’ The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, instructed him to fast only.” This is because fasting is an act of worship that Allah Most High loves, whereas the other practices are not acts of worship, even if someone imagines that they bring him closer to Allah Most High.

It is authentically reported that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would say in his sermons:

“The best speech is the speech of Allah, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The worst matters are those newly introduced into religion, and every innovation is misguidance.”

An authentic report also relates:

“Some of his Companions made the following statements. One said, ‘As for me, I will fast without breaking my fast.’ Another said, ‘As for me, I will pray without sleeping.’ Another said, ‘As for me, I will not marry women.’ Another said, ‘As for me, I will not eat meat.’ The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘What is the matter with men who say such-and-such? I, however, fast and break my fast, sleep, marry women, and eat meat. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me.’”

If this is the case regarding practices that are, in principle, acts of worship—for fasting and prayer are forms of worship, while abstaining from meat and marriage is permissible, yet when someone departed from the Sunnah by committing himself to more than was prescribed, or to abstaining from permissible things as monks do, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, disavowed anyone who did so, since he had turned away from his Sunnah to its opposite, and said, “There is no monasticism in Islam”—then what of someone who turns away from one of the greatest rites of Islam: attending Friday and congregational prayers?

It has been related from Ibn ‘Abbās that he was asked more than once about someone who fasts

---

## Page 5960

by day and stands in prayer at night, but attends neither Friday nor congregational prayers. He replied:

“He is in the Fire.”

In the two Sahīh collections, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is reported to have said:

“People must stop neglecting Friday prayers, or Allah will surely seal their hearts, and then they will be among the heedless.”

He also said:

“Whoever neglects three Friday prayers out of carelessness, without an excuse, Allah will seal his heart.”

In the Sahīh and the Sunan collections, it is reported:

“A blind man said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, I have a guide who does not always assist me as I need. Can you grant me a concession to pray in my home?’ He said, ‘Do you hear the call to prayer?’ He replied, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘Then respond to it.’ In another version, he said, ‘I find no concession for you.’”

Friday prayer is obligatory by agreement of the imams. Congregational prayer is also obligatory according to many scholars—indeed, according to most of the early generations. There are two opinions as to whether it is a condition for the validity of prayer. The stronger of the two accords with the Prophet’s statement reported in Sunan Abī Dāwūd:

“Whoever hears the call and does not respond, without an excuse, has no prayer.”

A group of scholars holds that congregational prayer is a collective obligation. Another opinion is that it is an emphatically recommended Sunnah. There is no disagreement among the scholars that a man’s prayer in congregation is twenty-five times better than his prayer alone

---

## Page 5961

as is authentically reported from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Nor is there any disagreement among them that whoever considers praying alone superior to praying in congregation is a misguided innovator who opposes the religion of the Muslims.

Those who practise these innovations are blameworthy, and it is known that Allah does not accept these practices, even if their intention is worship. Likewise, He does not accept the worship of monks and others who exert themselves in asceticism and worship, because they do not worship Him as He has prescribed, but through an innovation they have introduced. As He says:

“and monasticism which they invented.”

For the person who worships through these innovations aims to be revered and visited. His deeds are neither devoted sincerely to Allah nor correct according to the Sunnah. Rather, they are, as the saying goes, tainted and deficient—like the flesh of a dead pig, unlawful on two counts.

Every Muslim must commit himself to worshipping Allah alone, without any partner, and obeying His Messenger. He must enjoin this upon everyone, forbid everyone from doing the opposite, and denounce anyone who departs from it, even if that person flies through the air and walks on water. No one beneath the heavens may be allowed to contravene what the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has brought. Rather, if he professes Islam, he must be required to obey the Messenger and follow his binding Sunnah and guiding law. If he does not profess Islam, he is a disbeliever, however great his asceticism and monastic devotion may be.

---

## Page 5962

If a disbeliever is under a covenant of protection, the rulings applicable to others of his status apply to him; if he belongs to a belligerent community, the rulings applicable to others of that status apply to him. This innovator and those like him must be denounced with a sound intention: the aim must be obedience to Allah and His Messenger, not the pursuit of personal desires, rivalry, or anything else.

Allah Most High says:

“Fight them until there is no more fitnah and all worship is for Allah alone.”

The aim, then, is that all worship should be for Allah. Nothing constitutes religion except what Allah Most High has prescribed through His Messengers. It is reported in the two Sahih collections:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked: ‘O Messenger of Allah, a man fights to display his courage, another out of partisan zeal, and another to be seen by others. Which of these is fighting in Allah’s cause?’ He replied: ‘Whoever fights so that Allah’s word is supreme is fighting in Allah’s cause.’”

Thus, the aim must be the supremacy of Allah’s word and the ascendancy of His religion. All Muslims must know that the practices of ostentatious innovators are neither part of the religion nor the conduct of Allah’s righteous servants. Rather, they are the conduct of people of ignorance, misguidance, and association of partners with Allah Most High—those who depart from worshipping Him alone, devoting their religion sincerely to Him, and obeying His Messengers.

The “foundation of Islam” is: I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Whoever seeks ostentation and acclaim through his acts of worship has not fulfilled the testimony that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.

---

## Page 5963

and whoever departs from the revealed law that the Messenger commanded him to follow and worships through religious innovation has not fulfilled the testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. These two “foundations” are fulfilled only by someone who worships none but Allah and does not depart from the law of Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, which he conveyed from Allah. For he said:

“I have left you upon a clear path, whose night is like its day. None deviates from it but one who is doomed.”

He also said:

“There is nothing that brings you closer to Paradise that I have not told you about, nor anything that distances you from the Fire that I have not told you about.”

Ibn Masʿūd said:

“Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, drew a line for us, then drew lines to its right and left. He then said: ‘This is Allah’s way, and these are other ways; upon each of them is a devil calling people to it.’ Then he recited: ‘And this is My straight path, so follow it, and do not follow other paths, lest they lead you away from His path.’”

Thus, acts of worship, ascetic practices, teachings, and forms of scrupulous abstention that depart from Allah’s way—the straight path to which Allah has commanded us to ask Him to guide us, and which the Sunnah indicates—are the ways of Satan. Whatever extraordinary feats any of them may display, none of them is greater than their leader, the Dajjāl, who says to the sky, “Rain,” and it rains; to the earth, “Bring forth vegetation,” and it brings forth vegetation; and to the ruins, “Reveal your treasures,” and they bring forth treasures of gold and silver that accompany him.

Yet despite all this, he is an enemy of Allah and a disbeliever in Him. Allah’s allies are those mentioned in His words:

“Indeed, Allah’s allies shall have no fear, nor shall they

---

## Page 5964

grieve.”

“Those who believe and are mindful of Allah.”

They are the believers who are mindful of Allah. Such mindfulness consists in doing what Allah has commanded and refraining from what He has forbidden. How, then, can someone who abandons what Allah has commanded and adopts a form of worship that Allah has forbidden be one of them?

In Sahīh al-Bukhārī, Abū Hurayrah—may Allah be pleased with him—reports from the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—that Allah Most High says:

“Whoever shows enmity to an ally of Mine…”—to the end of the hadith.

Thus, He, glorified is He, has made clear that nothing by which a servant draws near to Allah equals fulfilling the duties He has imposed upon him.

Drawing near to Allah through obligatory duties alone is the path of those who take the middle course, the people of the right. Then, drawing nearer through the voluntary acts that Allah loves is the path of the foremost, those brought near to Him. The acts He loves are those that Allah and His Messenger have commanded, whether as obligations or as recommendations—not whatever a person deems desirable according to his own opinion and desires.

And Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knows best.

## Page 5965

Shaykh al-Islām, the pre-eminent scholar of his age, Taqī al-Dīn Abū al-ʿAbbās Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Halīm ibn ʿAbd al-Salām ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Qāsim ibn Taymiyyah al-Harrānī—may Allah be pleased with him—was asked:

About a “group” who gather with the intention of committing major sins, including murder, highway robbery, theft, drinking wine, and other such acts. This involved a frame drum without jingles and a singer singing permissible poetry, without a flute.

When he did this, a number of them repented. People who had neglected prayer, committed theft, and failed to pay zakat began to avoid doubtful matters, fulfil their religious obligations, and abstain from forbidden things. Is it permissible for this shaykh to arrange such listening sessions in this manner because of the benefits they produce, given that he cannot call them to righteousness by any other means?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah, Lord of all worlds.

The foundation of the answer to this question and others like it is to recognize that Allah sent Muhammad

—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion. And sufficient is Allah as a witness.

“My mercy encompasses all things, so I shall decree it

## Page 5967

for those who fear Me and give zakat, and those who believe in Our signs.”

“Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find described in the Torah and the Gospel they possess. Those who believe in him, honour him, support him, and follow the light sent down with him—it is they who will prosper.”

Allah commanded the Messenger—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—to observe all that is right, forbade all that is wrong, made all good things lawful, and made all foul things unlawful. It is authentically reported from him—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—in the Sahīh that he said:

“Every prophet Allah sent was duty-bound to guide his people to what he knew was best for them and forbid them what he knew was worst for them.”

It is also authentically reported that al-‘Irbād ibn Sāriyah said:

“The Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—gave us an exhortation that made our hearts tremble and our eyes shed tears. We said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, this seems like a farewell exhortation. What, then, do you charge us with?’ He replied, ‘I counsel you to listen and obey, for whoever among you lives after me will see much disagreement. Adhere to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the rightly guided caliphs who come after me. Hold fast to it and bite firmly onto it with your molars. Beware of newly introduced matters, for every innovation is misguidance.’”

It is authentically reported that he—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

---

## Page 5968

There is abundant evidence in the Quran and Sunnah for this “great, comprehensive principle.” Scholars have devoted sections of their books to it under the heading “Book of Holding Fast to the Quran and Sunnah,” as al-Bukhārī, al-Baghawī, and others have done. Whoever holds fast to the Quran and Sunnah is among Allah’s God-fearing allies and belongs to His successful party and His victorious army.

The early generations—including Mālik and others—used to say, “The Sunnah is like Noah’s Ark: whoever boards it is saved, and whoever stays behind drowns.” Al-Zuhrī said, “Those of our scholars who came before us used to say: ‘Holding fast to the Sunnah is salvation.’”

Once this is understood, it is clear that the means by which Allah guides those who are astray, directs those who have gone wrong, and accepts the repentance of sinners must be found in the Quran and Sunnah with which Allah sent His Messenger. Otherwise, if what Allah sent with the Messenger—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—were insufficient for this, the religion brought by the Messenger would be deficient and in need of completion.

It should be understood that Allah has commanded righteous deeds, making them either obligatory or recommended, and has forbidden corrupt deeds. When an action involves both benefit and harm, the Lawgiver is wise: if its benefit outweighs its harm, He prescribes it; if its harm outweighs its benefit, He does not prescribe it, but rather forbids it. As the Most High says:

“Fighting has been prescribed for you, though you dislike it. You may dislike something that is good for you and love something that is bad for you. Allah knows, and you do not know.”

The Most High also says: “They ask you

---

## Page 5969

about intoxicants and gambling. Say, ‘In them is great sin and benefit for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit.’” For this reason, Allah Most High subsequently prohibited them. The same applies to deeds that people regard as bringing them closer to Allah, but which Allah and His Messenger have not prescribed: their harm must outweigh their benefit. Otherwise, if their benefit predominated over their harm, the Lawgiver would not have neglected them. For he—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—is wise: he neither neglects the interests of religion nor deprives believers of what brings them closer to the Lord of all worlds.

With this understood, we say to the questioner:

The fact that the aforementioned shaykh sought to bring those gathered to commit major sins to repentance, but could do so only through the innovated method described, shows that he is either ignorant of the prescribed means by which sinners repent or unable to employ them. The Messenger—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—the Companions, and their successors used to call people worse than these—people guilty of disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience—through prescribed means with which Allah enabled them to dispense with innovated methods.

It is therefore impermissible to say that the prescribed means with which Allah sent His Prophet contain nothing through which sinners can repent. For it is established by incontrovertible knowledge and mass-transmitted reports that people from various nations, whose number Allah Most High alone knows, have repented of disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience through prescribed means that contain nothing of the innovated gathering described;

---

## Page 5970

indeed, the earliest forerunners among the Emigrants and Helpers, and those who followed them in righteousness—who are the best of Allah’s pious friends in this community—repented to Allah Most High through prescribed means, not through these innovated methods. Muslim cities and villages, past and present, are full of people who have repented to Allah, feared Him, and done what He loves and is pleased with through prescribed means, not through these innovated methods.

It is therefore impossible to say that sinners can repent only through these innovated methods. Rather, it may be said that some shaykhs are ignorant of the prescribed means and unable to employ them. They lack knowledge of the Book and the Sunnah, and of what to say to people and have them hear so that Allah may turn to them in mercy. Such a shaykh therefore abandons prescribed means for innovated methods, either with good intentions—if he has religious commitment—or with the aim of gaining authority over them and taking their wealth unjustly. As Allah Most High says:

“O you who believe, many rabbis and monks consume people’s wealth unjustly and turn people away from the path of Allah.”

No one abandons prescribed means for innovated methods except out of ignorance, inability, or a corrupt motive. For it is well known that listening to the Quran is the practice of the prophets, those who know Allah, and the believers. Allah Most High says concerning the prophets:

“Those were the ones upon whom Allah bestowed His favour among the prophets: descendants of Adam, of those We carried with Noah, and of Abraham and Israel, and those whom We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell down prostrate, weeping.”

---

## Page 5971

And Allah Most High says concerning those who know Him:

“When they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they recognize.”

Allah Most High says concerning those endowed with knowledge:

“Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall upon their faces in prostration.”

“They say, ‘Glory be to our Lord! Surely the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.’”

“They fall upon their faces, weeping, and it increases them in humility.”

He says concerning the believers:

“The believers are only those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned, whose faith increases when His verses are recited to them, and who put their trust in their Lord.”

“Those who establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them.”

“They are the true believers.”

Allah Most High says:

“Allah has sent down the best of speech: a Book consistent in its parts, with repeated teachings. The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver at it; then their skins and hearts soften at the remembrance of Allah. That is Allah’s guidance.”

Through this listening, Allah has guided His servants and set right their affairs in this life and the Hereafter. With it the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sent, and he enjoined it upon the Emigrants, the Helpers, and those who followed them in righteousness. It was for this that the early generations would gather. When the Companions of Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gathered, they would ask one of their number to recite while they listened. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb—may Allah be pleased with him—would say to Abū Mūsā, “Remind us of our Lord.” Abū Mūsā would then recite while they listened.

It is reported in al-Sahīh that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī while he was reciting and began listening to his recitation. He said: “This man has indeed been endowed with a flute-like voice

---

## Page 5972

like those of the family of David.”

He also said, “I passed by you last night while you were reciting, and I began listening to your recitation.” Abū Mūsā replied, “Had I known that you were listening to me, I would have made it especially beautiful for you”—meaning that he would have made his recitation more beautiful.

It is reported in al-Sahīh that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to Ibn Masʿūd, “Recite the Quran to me.” He replied, “Shall I recite the Quran to you when it was revealed to you?” He said, “I love to hear it from someone else.”

Ibn Masʿūd related: “I recited Sūrat al-Nisāʾ to him until I reached this verse:

‘How will it be, then, when We bring a witness from every nation and bring you as a witness against these people?’

“He said to me, ‘That is enough.’ I looked at him and saw his eyes streaming with tears.”

It was for this kind of listening that the generations praised by the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would gather. He said:

“The best generations are those among whom I was sent, then those who follow them, then those who follow them.”

Among the earliest generations, the righteous gathered for no other kind of listening—not in the Hijāz, Yemen, Syria, Egypt, Iraq, Khurāsān, or the Maghrib. The innovated practice of listening arose only later. Allah has praised those who devote themselves to this listening and condemned those who turn away from it. He has also declared it a means of receiving mercy. Allah Most High says:

“When the Quran is recited, listen to it attentively and remain silent, so that you may receive mercy.”

Allah Most High says:

“Those who, when reminded of their Lord’s verses, do not respond to them as though deaf and blind.”

Allah Most High says:

“Has the time not come for those who believe to be humbled

---

## Page 5973

in their hearts at the remembrance of Allah and the truth that has been revealed?”

Allah Most High says:

“Had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear. But even if He had made them hear, they would have turned away in aversion.”

Allah Most High says:

“So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them.”

“What is the matter with them, turning away from the reminder,”

“Like startled wild donkeys,”

“Fleeing from a lion?”

Allah Most High says:

“Who does greater wrong than someone who is reminded of his Lord’s verses, yet turns away from them and forgets what his own hands have done?”

Allah Most High says:

“When guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer misery.”

“But whoever turns away from My remembrance will have a life of hardship, and We will raise him blind on the Day of Resurrection.”

“He will say, ‘My Lord, why have You raised me blind when I used to see?’”

“He will say, ‘Just as Our signs came to you and you forgot them, so today you will be forgotten.’”

There are many passages like these in the Quran, commanding people to follow the Book and wisdom with which Allah sent His Messenger, and commanding them to listen to them.

Allah Most High has prescribed this listening for Muslims in the Maghrib, ‘Ishā’ and Fajr prayers. Allah Most High says:

“And the recitation at dawn; indeed, the recitation at dawn is witnessed.”

It was for this that ‘Abd Allāh ibn Rawāha praised the Prophet, saying:

Among us is Allah’s Messenger, reciting His Book,
When dawn’s clear light breaks forth.
He spends the night keeping his side away from his bed,
While disbelievers lie sunk in theirs.

---

## Page 5974

He brought guidance after blindness; through him our hearts
Are certain that what he said will come to pass.

The states experienced by those who listen in this manner are mentioned in Allah’s Book: trembling hearts, flowing tears and shuddering skin.

Poetry-listening gatherings arose only after these generations, and the imams denounced them. Al-Shāfiʿī—may Allah have mercy on him—even said: “I left behind in Baghdad something introduced by the heretics, which they call taghbīr. They claim that it softens hearts, but they use it to turn people away from the Quran.”

Imam Ahmad was asked about it and said: “It is newly introduced.” He was then asked, “Should we sit with them during it?” He replied: “One should not sit with them.”

Taghbīr consists of beating their skins with a rod and is among the better forms of these listening practices. Yet the imams disapproved of it, so what of the other forms? The great spiritual masters who were leading authorities did not attend these newly introduced listening gatherings, such as al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyād, Ibrāhīm ibn Adham, Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī, Maʿrūf al-Karkhī, al-Sarī al-Saqatī and others like them.

Nor did the foremost later shaykhs, such as Shaykh ʿAbd al-Qādir, Shaykh ʿAdī, Shaykh Abū Madyan, Shaykh Abū al-Bayān, Shaykh Abū al-Qāsim al-Hawfī, Shaykh ʿAlī ibn Wahb, Shaykh Hayāh and others like them. Some shaykhs attended these gatherings but subsequently abandoned them.

Al-Junayd was asked about this listening and said: “Whoever deliberately seeks it out is put to trial by it, whereas whoever encounters it without seeking it finds relief in it.” He thus explained

---

## Page 5975

that whoever deliberately seeks out this listening is put to trial by it, whereas there is no harm in someone happening to hear something congenial to him. The prohibition applies only to deliberate listening, not merely hearing. Thus, if a man passes people engaged in forbidden speech, he is not obliged to stop his ears, but he may not deliberately listen without a need. Likewise, the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—did not instruct Ibn ʿUmar to stop his ears when he heard a shepherd’s flute, because he was merely hearing it, not deliberately listening.

The question posed by this questioner and others—“Is it lawful or unlawful?”—is ambiguously worded and obscures the issue. The ruling becomes so confused that many muftis cannot formulate a precise answer. This is because listening, like other actions, may be considered from two perspectives:

The first concerns whether it is prohibited or not—whether it may be practised like other activities that people enjoy, even if they involve some amusement and play, such as listening at weddings and similar occasions. People engage in these activities for pleasure and amusement, not as worship or to draw closer to Allah.

The second is to engage in it as a religious observance and an act of worship, to reform hearts, make the servants’ love for their Lord pure and undivided, cleanse their souls and purify their hearts

---

## Page 5976

and to awaken in their hearts reverent fear, repentance, love, tenderness, and other qualities belonging to worship and obedience rather than play and amusement.

A distinction must therefore be drawn between listening practised by those seeking nearness to Allah and listening practised for amusement; between listening at weddings, celebrations, and similar customary occasions, and listening intended to reform hearts and draw closer to the Lord of the heavens. Concerning the latter, the questions are:

Is it an act of devotion and obedience? Is it a path to Allah? Can they do without it, given that it softens their hearts, stirs their ardent love for their Beloved, purifies their souls, removes hardness from their hearts, and serves other such purposes sought through listening? Christians likewise practise this kind of listening in their churches as worship and obedience, not as amusement and play.

Once this is understood, the real question is:

Is it permissible for the shaykh to make these practices—which are either prohibited, disliked, or permissible—into acts of devotion, worship, and obedience, and a path to Allah through which he calls people to Allah, leads sinners to repentance, directs those who have gone astray, and guides the misguided?

It is well known that religion has “two foundations”: nothing belongs to religion except what Allah has prescribed, and nothing is forbidden except what Allah has forbidden. Allah Most High has reproached the polytheists for forbidding what He has not forbidden and instituting a religion for which He has given no permission.

---

## Page 5977

And if a scholar were asked about someone running between two mountains, “Is he permitted to do that?” he would answer, “Yes.” But if he were told, “He does so as an act of worship, like making the passage between al-Safā and al-Marwah,” he would say, “Doing this as worship is forbidden and reprehensible. The person doing it must be called upon to repent; if he does not repent, he is to be put to death.”

Likewise, if he were asked about leaving the head uncovered and wearing a waist-wrapper and an upper-body wrap, he would rule that this is permissible. But if he were told, “He does so as a form of ihrām (ritual consecration), as a pilgrim does,” he would say, “This is forbidden and reprehensible.”

If he were asked about someone standing in the sun, he would say, “This is permissible.” But if he were told, “He does so as an act of worship,” he would say, “This is reprehensible,” as al-Bukhārī narrated from Ibn ‘Abbās—may Allah be pleased with them both:

“Allah’s Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, saw a man standing in the sun and asked, ‘Who is this?’ They said, ‘This is Abū Isrā’īl. He intends to stand in the sun without sitting down, seeking shade, or speaking.’ The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, ‘Tell him to speak, sit down, seek shade, and complete his fast.’”

Had he done this for his own comfort or some permissible purpose, he would not have been forbidden to do it. But because he did it as an act of worship, he was forbidden to do so. Similarly, if a man entered his house from the back, that would not be forbidden to him. But if he did so as an act of worship, as people used to do in the pre-Islamic period:

---

## Page 5978

when one of them entered ihrām, he would not go under a roof—they were forbidden to do this, as the Most High says:

“Righteousness is not in entering houses from the back. Rather, righteousness is in fearing Allah. So enter houses through their doors.”

He, glorified be He, thus made clear that this is not righteousness, even though it is not itself forbidden. Whoever does it as an act of righteousness and a means of drawing near to Allah is therefore disobedient, blameworthy, and an innovator. Religious innovation is dearer to Iblīs than sin, because the sinner knows that he is sinning and so repents, whereas the innovator imagines that what he is doing is an act of obedience and therefore does not repent.

Likewise, someone who attends gatherings for listening to poetry for amusement and entertainment does not count this among his righteous deeds or hope to be rewarded for it. But someone who does so as a path to Allah Most High makes it part of his religion. If someone forbids him to do it, he regards that person as forbidding his religion, and believes that abandoning it would cut him off from Allah and deprive him of his portion from Allah Most High.

Such people are misguided by agreement of the Muslim scholars. None of the imams of the Muslims says that adopting this as a religious practice and a path to Allah Most High is permissible. Rather, whoever makes this a religious practice and a path to Allah Most High is misguided, fabricates falsehood, and opposes the consensus of the Muslims. Anyone who considers only the outward form of an action and pronounces upon it, without considering how the person performs it and what he intends, is ignorant and speaks about religion without knowledge.

The question about such a matter should therefore be put as follows:

“Is what these people do a path to Allah Most High, a means of drawing near to Him, and an act of obedience that Allah and His Messenger love, or not? Will they be rewarded for it or not? If this is not a means of drawing near to Allah, an act of obedience to Him, or worship of Him, yet they do it as a means of drawing near to Him

---

## Page 5979

and as an act of obedience and worship and a path to Allah Most High, is it permissible for them to hold this belief and perform this practice on that basis?”

When the question is put this way, no scholar who follows the Messenger—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—can say that this is a means of drawing near to Allah, an act of obedience, a form of worship, or part of Allah’s way and the path by which these people call others to Him. Nor can he say that it is something Allah Most High has commanded His servants to do, whether as an obligation or as a recommendation. Whatever is neither obligatory nor recommended is not praiseworthy, a good deed, an act of obedience, or worship, by agreement of the Muslims. Whoever does something neither obligatory nor recommended, treating it as belonging to either category, is a misguided innovator. Performing it on this basis is undoubtedly forbidden.

This applies especially to the many people who adopt this innovated practice of listening as a spiritual path and prefer it to listening to the Quran in terms of ecstasy and spiritual experience. They may even believe it to be superior. Thus, you find them listening to the Quran with heedless hearts, idle talk, restless movements, and raised voices. Their hearts do not turn towards it, nor do their souls find comfort in it. But when they hear “whistling” and “clapping,” their hearts listen intently, the beloved is united with the lover, voices grow hushed, and movements cease. There is no coughing, sneezing, clamour, or shouting.

If they recite or hear anything of the Quran, they do so reluctantly, as though subjected to forced labour, just as a person does not listen to something for which he has no need

---

## Page 5980

and from which he derives no benefit. Yet when they hear Satan’s pipe, they love it, turn eagerly towards it, and their souls become wholly absorbed in it. These people are Satan’s troops and enemies of the Most Merciful, though they imagine themselves to be among Allah’s pious allies. Their condition more closely resembles that of the hypocrites who are Allah’s enemies. For the believer loves what Allah Most High loves, hates what Allah Most High hates, befriends Allah’s allies, and opposes His enemies. These people, however, love what Allah hates, hate what Allah loves, befriend Allah’s enemies, and oppose His allies.

For this reason, they receive satanic visitations corresponding to their use of Satan’s pipes. The further they stray from Allah, His Messenger, and the way of the believers, the closer they draw to the enemies of Allah and His Messenger and to Satan’s troops. Some fly through the air, while it is Satan who carries them. Others throw those present into convulsions, while it is their devils who do so. Some produce food and accompaniments and fill a pitcher out of thin air, while it is the devils who have done this. The ignorant suppose these to be miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s pious allies. They are, however, merely phenomena of the same kind as those experienced by soothsayers, sorcerers, and others like them among the devils. Whoever distinguishes between states originating with the Most Merciful, the self, and Satan will not confuse truth with falsehood.

We have discussed “the question of listening” at length elsewhere and cited the spiritual masters’ statements concerning it. Success comes through Allah, and Allah knows best. May Allah bless Muhammad, his family, and his Companions, and grant them peace.

## Page 5981

Shaykh al-Islām—may Allah have mercy on him—said:

Section

I have previously written about “unveilings and visions,” explaining that they fall into “three categories,” both outwardly and inwardly. Likewise, “hearing, being addressed, and conversations” fall into three categories, inwardly and outwardly.

The “listener” may hear the actual sound itself, whether it is the speaker’s vocal speech or something other than his speech, just as one sees the speaker himself.

Or he may hear the sound’s echo and reverberation, just as he sees the speaker’s image in water or a mirror. Such seeing and hearing are qualified, as when one says, “I saw him in the mirror.” Hearing, however, encompasses both forms.

Or a representation may be presented to him—meaning the speaker’s words—in audible sounds, just as the speaker may be represented to him in a form that he sees. For example, the speaker may tap with his hand, pluck strings with his hand, or produce sounds separate from himself through which he conveys his intended meaning.

---

## Page 5982

And likewise inwardly:

A person may hear, in sleep or while awake, the speaker’s actual words—for example, those of angels—just as he sees with his heart the very thing unveiled to him in sleep or wakefulness. Or he may hear a representation of the speaker’s words within himself, just as he sees a representation of the speaker within himself, like a dream whose interpretation is the very thing seen. Or meanings may be represented to him as audible speech requiring interpretation, just as actual things may be represented to him as visible figures requiring interpretation. This is the case with most of what is seen and heard in dreams: it requires interpretation and resembles metaphor and illustrative parables. Such is the matter. And Allah knows best.

Section

On Existence in Wakefulness and Sleep

Seeing things with the eye takes two forms:

The first is the eye’s seeing an object without an intermediary. This is seeing in the unqualified sense, such as seeing the sun and the moon. As the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“You will see your Lord just as you see the sun and the moon.”

People have differed over whether vision consists in the object seen being imprinted upon the eye, results from the reflection of visual rays, or involves neither. These are well-known positions.

---

## Page 5983

The second is seeing an image, as when looking into water, a mirror, or the like. This is a qualified form of seeing. Thus, the jurists have said that if someone swears, “I shall not see Zayd,” then sees his image in water or a mirror, he has not broken his oath, because this is not what is understood by seeing without qualification. This is to sight what hearing an echo is to hearing.

When someone wishes to see the people and animals passing behind him, he looks into a mirror facing him, and it reveals to him what is actually behind him. In this kind of vision, he may see reality clearly, or reality may appear to him in a representation that requires verification, just as Gabriel appeared in human form. Likewise, the heart has the capacity to see, for its sight is true sight, and its blindness is true blindness. As Allah Most High says:

“For it is not the eyes that are blind, but the hearts within the breasts.”

At times, the heart sees the thing itself when it is unveiled to it; at other times, it sees the thing represented within itself, serving as its mirror, while also being that which sees. This may occur either in wakefulness or in sleep, as when a man sees something in a dream and then encounters that very thing while awake, without any change.

The heart also has a “third state,” just as the eye has a way of seeing in sleep. This is what most people experience: seeing a dream that presents an illustrative likeness of reality. A person cannot fully grasp the vision of reality itself, either directly or through the mirror of his heart. Rather, he sees something that admits of interpretation and uses it to infer what it signifies. “Dream interpretation” is the passage from a thing to its likeness and counterpart, and this is

---

## Page 5984

the essence of comparison and reasoning by analogy. For understanding something through the familiar, habitual use of comparison and analogy is easier than grasping something immediately without a known parallel.

What is seen in this manner—in this state and in the preceding one—exists within a person’s heart and soul, even though it is a likeness of reality and a means of apprehending it.

What is seen in the first manner, however, is the very thing that exists externally, not something seen within the heart. Some philosophizing laypeople claim that the speech the prophets hear and the angels they see exist only within their hearts. Such is the extent of their knowledge, for that is the furthest limit of what they have experienced and witnessed among their fellow human beings, so they suppose that nothing lies beyond it. Others may oppose them, imagining that what is heard and seen cannot exist within a person, but must all come from outside. Both views are mistaken.

Rather, some of it exists within a person, such as what one sees and hears in sleep, whether an image that admits of no interpretation or one that does.

Some of it exists externally, such as Mary’s seeing the messenger when he appeared to her

---

## Page 5985

as a well-proportioned man, and the Companions’ seeing Gabriel in the form of a Bedouin.

It is thus clear that seeing realities with the eye corresponds to seeing them with the heart. Each comprises “three categories”: perceiving the externally existing thing itself; perceiving it through its representation in an inward or outward mirror; and perceiving it represented in a form other than its own, either inwardly in the heart or outwardly before the eye. And Allah, glorified be He, knows best.

Reasoning by analogy concerning sensory matters is therefore like reasoning by analogy concerning intellectual matters. What I have written about visionary disclosures has its counterpart in communications, for sight and hearing disclose what follows.

## Page 5986

When certain shaykhs hold gatherings for devotional listening, the “men of the unseen” attend, the ceiling and walls split open, and the angels descend, dancing with them or over them.
